name: Alchemical Character Creation (Five Steps)
summary: Alchemical creation follows the same five-step Solar skeleton but replaces every step's internals: Attributes come from a Caste-linked triad rather than a Physical/Social/Mental split, Abilities have no Caste/Favored discount at all, Charms are implanted artifacts drawn from a fixed number of Slots instead of a purchasable list, and Willpower/Essence/the two Essence pools use Alchemical-specific formulas built around the signature Clarity Trait rather than the Great Curse.
mechanics: Step One (Concept): choose concept, Caste, and Nature before anything else. Caste is assigned by which of the Five Magical Materials predominates in the character's Vat-built frame, not by personality (closer to a Dragon-Blood's aspect than a Solar's Caste); the Sodalities also try to match a resonant soul to that Material. Autochthonian society favors the Natures Architect, Bureaucrat, Follower, Judge, Leader, Paragon, Savant and Visionary; Gallant/Hedonist/Thrillseeker are tolerated at the edge of propriety, and Rebel draws open derision; a sidebar details a unique local reading of Paragon ('Paragon of Integration') as the Autochthonian ideal of a selfless-but-not-servile cooperator. Step Two (Attributes): every character gets 1 free dot in each Attribute as usual, but instead of Primary/Secondary/Tertiary categories, each Caste has 3 fixed Caste Attributes (see the five Caste rows) that receive 9 dots with no Attribute below ••; the player then picks 3 of the remaining 6 Attributes as Favored and assigns 6 dots there; the last 3 Attributes split the final 4 dots. Step Three (Abilities): uniquely among Exalted, Alchemicals have no Caste or Favored Abilities whatsoever - all 23 starting dots are freely distributed, guided only by non-binding suggestions (2+ in a primary attack Ability, 1+ in a secondary range, 2+ in a defensive Ability, 2+ Athletics, at least 1 dot each in a Craft/Lore/Occult, 3+ spread across Performance/Presence/Socialize, 2+ Bureaucracy); Larceny, Ride and Sail are Rare Abilities in Autochthonia before contact with Creation, and a 2-die unfamiliarity penalty applies when Autochthonians handle living mounts/boats (and vice versa for Creation natives with Autochthonian conveyances) until several weeks' practice. Step Four (Advantages): every Alchemical automatically receives Class ••• for free (see class-background) plus 10 further Background dots to spend (13 total); only Artifact may exceed ••• without bonus points. Charms take the form of surgically implanted artifacts: a starting character has 4 General Charm Slots (any Charm) and 4 Dedicated Charm Slots (Caste/Favored Charms only), and must choose 8 Charms to fill all 8 Slots; extra Slots cost bonus points (see alchemical-bonus-points-and-experience-costs) and each comes with a free qualifying Charm. Virtues get 1 free dot each plus 5 more to distribute, capped at 3 without bonus points; Compassion is explicitly the Virtue that pushes back against Clarity. Step Five (Finishing Touches): Willpower equals the sum of the two highest Virtues (capped below 8 unless both of those Virtues are 4+); Essence starts at 2. Personal Essence pool = (Essence x 3) + Willpower. Peripheral Essence pool = (Essence x 5) + (Willpower x 3) + (highest Virtue x 2), before any Charm-granted bonus capacity. Health levels are the standard mortal 7, plus one extra -2 level per dot of permanent Essence. Finally, 15 bonus points may be spent at any time per the bonus-point cost table.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, Steps One through Five and the Character Creation Process/Castes/Virtues summary sidebar, pp. 58-64 (PDF 59-65). Extracted from a clean text layer and cross-checked against rendered images of the summary/Caste-Attribute/bonus-point pages.

name: Universal Anima Effect & Alchemical Anima Banners (all Castes)
summary: Every Alchemical, regardless of Caste, can spend 1 mote to intensify her anima banner along a five-tier display table keyed to how much Peripheral Essence she has spent this scene (1-3/4-7/8-10/11-15/16+ motes), with each tier trading away more Stealth/concealment capability for a brighter, harder-to-hide, and eventually trail-marking display; she may also spend 3 motes per die to temporarily boost any Caste or Favored Attribute for a scene.
mechanics: Anima banners fade by one display level every 20 minutes unless refreshed by further Peripheral Essence spending; a fading anima is treated as still being at its highest recent level for the purpose of flaring back up. Table: 1-3 motes - sparks crackle around the soulgem/used Charms, noticeable only on a reflexive Perception + Awareness roll, Stealth still usable normally, fades within an hour of the character stopping expenditure. 4-7 motes - arcs of Essence sizzle visibly across soulgem and Charms, unmistakably marking the character as Alchemical and shutting off any concealment Charms/magic, though Stealth can still be used in natural cover at +2 difficulty. 8-10 motes - a torch-bright aura envelops the body in a caste-appropriate color, every Charm blazes, and traces of the caste's Magical Material bleed from the skin (evaporating within Essence-rating turns, leaving no useful tracking sign); stealth is impossible at this level. 11-15 motes - same visual display as 8-10 but the bleeding Material traces persist for a full hour, letting the character retrace her own path with automatic success while equally helping anyone else who can see the trail follow her; the display itself still fades in 20 minutes without further spending, so a glowing trail can abruptly stop while the light itself keeps burning at the end point. 16+ motes - an iconic, caste-flavored display (e.g. billowing smoke for Soulsteel, arcing lightning for Orichalcum) that engages every sense for a single turn before receding to the 11-15 level for the rest of the scene; any further Peripheral spending re-triggers the iconic flare. Separately, any Alchemical may spend 3 motes per die (lasting a number of turns equal to permanent Essence) to boost a Caste or Favored Attribute, capped at double the Attribute's unmodified rating; these bonus dice count against the normal Charm dice cap.
cost: 1 mote to flare the banner to a new display level; 3 motes per die to boost a Caste/Favored Attribute.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes; reflexive, no Charm purchase required.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Anima Effect' / 'Alchemical Anima Banners' table, p. 75 (PDF 76). Table verified against a rendered page image; text extraction matched exactly.

name: Artificial Metabolism (feeding, immunities)
summary: Alchemicals do not breathe except to speak, cannot drown, and are immune to inhaled toxins and non-magical disease or infection; they are also permanently sterile. They still eat, but purely to synthesize Essence and fuel autonomic repair rather than for ordinary nourishment, and prolonged starvation progressively cripples their Essence recovery and eventually their ability to heal at all.
mechanics: After a number of consecutive days of starvation equal to her Stamina, an Alchemical begins suffering a cumulative 1-mote penalty on her hourly Essence-respiration rate for every additional day of deprivation (or a slower 1 mote per 3 days for less severe food shortfalls). She heals at only the mortal rate once any such penalty is active, and stops healing entirely once the accrued mote penalty reaches 4. A single day of proper eating restores normal metabolic function immediately, but any missed days first require an equal run of consecutive well-fed days (up to a number equal to her Stamina) before full recovery. Otherwise Alchemicals eat and dispose of waste the same amount and way as a mortal of similar build.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Alchemical Physiology and Powers' -> 'Artificial Metabolism', p. 73 (PDF 74).

name: Life, Death, and the Soulgem
summary: While properly fed, Alchemicals heal exactly like other Exalted, mending dented metal and cracked Charms without scarring; but lethal or aggravated damage that drops one below Incapacitated causes her whole body to dissolve into a puddle of clay, crystal shards and broken metal over a number of turns equal to her Essence, shattering every installed Charm into raw salvage and leaving only a pristine, undamaged diamond soulgem behind.
mechanics: Because so much valuable Magical Material is built into an Alchemical's frame, unscrupulous parties sometimes plunder living Exalted through outright vivisection rather than waiting for a natural death. On death (dropping below Incapacitated from lethal/aggravated damage), the body dissolves over Essence-many turns; the wreckage of shattered Charms is worth roughly Resources ••••• to anyone willing to scavenge it, but the diamond soulgem itself remains intact amid the ruin.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Alchemical Physiology and Powers' -> 'Life and Death', p. 73 (PDF 74).

name: Refitting, Essence Advancement, and Metropolis Evolution
summary: Alchemicals cannot grow, learn new Charms, or raise Essence on their own initiative; every such change requires unconscious surgery at a Vat Complex, and raising Essence in particular physically transforms the Exalt's body through a fixed sequence of size/form thresholds that, after centuries of life, culminates in literal metamorphosis into the living core of an entirely new Autochthonian city.
mechanics: Minor refits (installing/removing Charms or Charm Slots) take one week regardless of how many are changed; raising an Attribute takes one week per dot; the Exalt is fully unconscious throughout, floating in the Vat while a technician monitors the process. Raising Essence is far more involved: it takes a number of months equal to the character's current Essence rating, during which she remains dimly, helplessly conscious in total sensory deprivation while her soul is refined. Endowments and similar outside magic cannot grant Essence or raise Attributes for an Alchemical; any attempt instead grants a different Endowment of the Storyteller's choosing. Physical thresholds: Essence 2-3 stay within human size ranges (6-7 feet) and largely human proportions. Essence 4-5 grow to 9-12 feet and become mostly metal and crystal under the weight of installed Charms. The Essence 5-to-6 transition (available only after 100+ years of life) strips the body down to bare soulgem-and-Essence-reservoir core, which is rebuilt into a new, 20+-foot frame resembling a warstrider or many-limbed custodian, usually with a humanoid mask retained somewhere for communication. Essence 7 (available after 250+ years) is a further extension of the same process, reaching up to 30 feet. Essence 8 (available only after 500+ years, and rare even then) is reserved for Alchemicals who undergo a seven-month, largely helpless transformation: the Exalt journeys to an uninhabited site, grows a 100-foot chrysalis egg from her own Essence, and disassembles inside it into the sessile living core of a brand-new city (a patropolis if male, metropolis if female); from that point the city's towers, factories and trams are her body, she can manufacture her own Charms, and only destroying the core itself can kill her. Essence 9 requires roughly a millennium of life and Essence 10 roughly two millennia; Exalted pursuing these deliberately extend their own refit time to decades of conscious meditation.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Alchemical Physiology and Powers' -> 'Refitting, Essence and Evolution', pp. 73-74 (PDF 74-75). The Essence 8-10 city-transformation material shades toward Storyteller-facing setting lore, but is kept as calculated here because it directly defines what an advancing player character's Essence rating physically means and requires (unlike the wholly optional adamant-caste-legend sidebar).

name: Orichalcum Caste
summary: The Orichalcum Caste are the Shining Ones - brilliant, forceful leaders and doctrinal experts the Tripartite treats as the closest thing Alchemicals have to public visionaries, prone to arrogance and philosophical friction with their own peers even as they inspire mortal civilization toward utopian ambition.
mechanics: Anima Effect: for a reflexive 5 motes, an Orichalcum Caste charges her body with golden lightning for a scene, adding her Essence to the damage of all attacks (melee strikes visibly spark on contact; thrown/ranged attacks crackle as they leave hand or weapon). Caste Attributes: Strength, Charisma, Intelligence - the caste is written as immensely strong, unquestionable and brilliant, to the point that high-Charisma Archons are described as commanding awe rather than mere likability. Associations: the color yellow, gold, orichalcum, the element of lightning, illumination, inspiration, leadership, excellence. Sobriquets: Shining Ones, Archons, Flames of Autochthon, Blessed of Noi. Concepts: defender of the people, advisor to the Tripartite, cleric of the Great Maker, mad scientist. Caste Markings/anima flavor: Charms built of burnished brass, gold and orichalcum with crystal/glass windows revealing moving internal works; anima blazes gold and white lightning, leaving momentary residual sparks on nearby metal.
compatibility: One of the five Alchemical Castes chosen at character creation, mirroring the Solar Dawn Caste's forceful-leader role.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Orichalcum' Caste section, pp. 76-77 (PDF 77-78); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image.

name: Moonsilver Caste
summary: The Moonsilver Caste are the Mirrorblades - the Tripartite's secret agents, disguise experts, scouts and assassins, who mute their own anima to work unseen and eventually graduate from spying on citizens to striking directly at gremlin queens and pack leaders once they grow too large for covert work.
mechanics: Anima Effect: for a reflexive 5 motes, a Moonsilver Caste suffuses herself with quicksilver grace for a scene, adding (her Essence x 2) to base initiative; she perceives the world in apparent slow motion while moving at her own normal pace, and observers notice only unusual deftness if given any opportunity to notice at all. Caste Attributes: Dexterity, Appearance, Wits - written as universally nimble, quick and socially mercurial, adapting to or evading notice from those around them. Associations: the color white, silver, moonsilver, the element of oil, innovation, secrets, guile. Sobriquets: Mirrorblades, Proteans, Razors of Autochthon, Blessed of Debok Moom. Concepts: everyman spy, explorer of the Far Reaches, assassin, heretic finder. Caste Markings/anima flavor: Charms display smooth, organic, almost grown-rather-than-forged curves; anima seeps from beneath the skin as dozens of undulating tendrils of light flickering pale silver and white.
compatibility: One of the five Alchemical Castes chosen at character creation, mirroring the Solar Night Caste's stealth/infiltration role.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Moonsilver' Caste section, pp. 78-79 (PDF 79-80).

name: Jade Caste
summary: The Jade Caste are the Hammers of Autochthon - the approachable, egalitarian middle management and frontline officers who interact with ordinary mortals daily, leading by durability and shared example rather than by distant authority, and who tend to command exceptionally loyal mortal units.
mechanics: Anima Effect: for a reflexive 5 motes, a Jade Caste hardens her claylike flesh into flexible stone for a scene, adding her Essence to both natural bashing and lethal soak. Caste Attributes: Stamina, Charisma, Wits - built to endure industrial and combat trials while remaining the most publicly approachable Caste, adapting plans on the fly. Associations: the color green, jade, the element of metal, truth, unity. Sobriquets: Stone Hands, Executives, Hammers of Autochthon, Blessed of Runel. Concepts: hero of the factory, voice of the Populat, guardian of morale, arbitrator. Caste Markings/anima flavor: Charms are deliberately blocky and functional rather than baroque, usually restrained to one or two complementary shades of jade's five natural colors; anima expresses as intersecting polyhedrons in a geometric lattice, colored to match the caste's jade tones.
compatibility: One of the five Alchemical Castes chosen at character creation, mirroring the Solar Zenith Caste's frontline-leadership role.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Jade' Caste section, pp. 80-81 (PDF 81-82).

name: Starmetal Caste
summary: The Starmetal Caste are the Viziers - reclusive social engineers, motivational theorists and spymasters who coordinate (rather than personally conduct) most Autochthonian intelligence work, preferring judicious partial-truth and calculated, minimal violence over the Orichalcum Caste's public leadership style.
mechanics: Anima Effect: for a reflexive 5 motes, a Starmetal Caste aligns himself with the Design of the Great Maker for a scene, adding (his Essence divided by 2, rounded up) to all attack, damage and base initiative rolls; a prismatic halo trails slightly ahead of him hinting at his coming movements, though onlookers cannot actually use the warning to predict or avoid his specific attacks until they land. Caste Attributes: Dexterity, Manipulation, Intelligence - balancing subtlety and cunning with scalpel-precise, rarely-telegraphed physical action when it becomes necessary. Associations: the color blue, steel, starmetal, the element of crystal, half-truths. Sobriquets: Plot Weavers, Viziers, Daggers of Autochthon, Blessed of Mog. Concepts: tactical advisor, data interpreter, pattern theorist, social prognosticator. Caste Markings/anima flavor: Charms use a minimalist aesthetic of braided starmetal wire filigree (the rarest of the Five Magical Materials) with occasional random Essence sparks; anima is deep blue shot through with prismatic static.
compatibility: One of the five Alchemical Castes chosen at character creation, mirroring the Solar Eclipse Caste's diplomat/schemer role.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Starmetal' Caste section, pp. 82-83 (PDF 83-84); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image.

name: Soulsteel Caste
summary: The Soulsteel Caste are the Grim Watch - relentless enforcers, hunters and interrogators who deal with threats the other Castes' plans fail to prevent, from gremlin incursions to dissidents and Gremlin-Syndrome-afflicted peers, and who are simultaneously the most feared and the most self-policing of the five Castes.
mechanics: Anima Effect: for a reflexive 5 motes, a Soulsteel Caste stirs the tormented souls trapped within her frame for a scene, generating an aura of numbing dread that adds (her Essence divided by 2, rounded up) to the difficulty of all attacks targeting her; the effect works even against automatons, the walking dead and other beings normally immune to fear (only perfect magical fear-immunity ignores it). Caste Attributes: Stamina, Manipulation, Perception - built to be as physically tough as they are frightening, skilled at extracting compliance, and constantly, unwaveringly vigilant. Associations: the color black, iron, soulsteel, the element of smoke, violence, callousness, enforcement. Sobriquets: Grim Watch, Sentinels, Scourges of Autochthon, Blessed of Ku. Concepts: gremlin killer, problem solver, torture expert, motivator, dissident recycler. Caste Markings/anima flavor: Charms appear crudely hammered from black alloys with visible rivets, perpetually stained with soot; anima is shadowy black-and-blue-lightning-streaked smoke.
compatibility: One of the five Alchemical Castes chosen at character creation, mirroring the Solar Twilight Caste's enforcement/problem-solving role.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Soulsteel' Caste section, pp. 84-85 (PDF 85-86); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image.

name: Legends of the Sixth Caste (Adamant, apocryphal)
summary: An in-world rumor, not an official Vat product: Autochthonian folklore tells of a mysterious sixth Caste built from adamant that appears from nowhere to strike down gremlins or the incompetent and vanishes before anyone can verify the sighting; the book presents this purely as Storyteller-optional material, with a brief stat sketch offered only for STs who decide the legend is literally true in their game.
mechanics: If used, Adamant's Caste Attributes are Strength, Appearance and Perception (completing the pattern of every Attribute being shared by exactly two Castes across all six). Its anima power costs 5 motes and adds bonus dice equal to permanent Essence to all Stealth rolls or attempts to escape tracking, for a scene. The text speculates (without confirming) that any real Adamant Caste Exalted would have Vats hidden inside biomechanical factory-deities grown for that purpose and cloaked by powerful enchantments, would serve the highest Autochthonian gods directly as unseen eyes and hands watching over even their own cousins, and would have been created secretly by the Divine Ministers as a contingency against the other Castes growing too powerful, after Autochthon's core sank into torpor. Neither the Olgotary nor the Alchemicals themselves have any confirmed record of ever building such a Caste.
compatibility: Storyteller-only, and only if the Storyteller chooses to make the legend literally true; not a standard player-selectable Caste under the normal character-creation rules.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Legends of the Sixth Caste' sidebar, p. 61 (PDF 62); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image. Classified gm-only rather than selectable because the book explicitly gates any mechanical use behind Storyteller discretion ('For Storytellers interested in including the sixth caste...') rather than offering it as a chargen option.

name: Clarity
summary: Alchemicals were built after Autochthon's withdrawal from Creation and so bear no part of the Great Curse; in its place they carry Clarity, a Trait measuring the balance between the human soul housed in their bodies and the cold, mechanical logic of the Machine God, tracked as separate permanent and temporary ratings whose sum can never exceed 10.
mechanics: Permanent Clarity represents an increasing, effectively irreversible mechanization of thought and Essence, gained only from raising Essence above 5 or installing certain powerful Charms; it cannot be shed while the condition that granted it (the Essence rating, the installed Charm) still applies, but removing that condition immediately removes the matching permanent dots. Temporary Clarity fluctuates with behavior and is the half of the Trait that can be actively managed session to session. The two ratings are added together to determine the character's effective total Clarity for the social/behavioral effects table.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes; replaces the Limit Trait entirely for this splat.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Clarity' section, p. 69 (PDF 70); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image.

name: Gaining Clarity (Inhuman Essence, Suppressing Virtues, Forsaking Humanity, Charms)
summary: Alchemicals accumulate Clarity by leaning into their mechanical nature at the expense of their humanity, through three named triggers plus whatever specific Charms grant on activation or installation.
mechanics: Inhuman Essence: gain 1 dot of permanent Clarity for every dot of Essence rated above 5 (this is the primary source of permanent Clarity for most characters). Suppressing Virtues: gain 1 point of temporary Clarity whenever the Exalt spends Willpower to act contrary to a Virtue rated 3+; she may instead suppress that Virtue without spending Willpower by leaning on her mechanical side, but doing so costs 2 points of Clarity instead of 1. Forsaking Humanity: gain 1 point of Clarity for every full week spent without meaningful human contact (such as venturing deep into the Far Reaches); qualifying contact must involve an overt demonstration of empathy or at least sustained, peaceful discourse across a full scene, and contact with other Alchemical Exalted does not count toward avoiding this gain. Charms: certain Charms explicitly award temporary or even permanent Clarity on activation and/or installation, per their own individual text (not detailed here; out of scope for this inventory pass).
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Gaining Clarity' section, pp. 69-70 (PDF 70-71); visually cross-checked against rendered page images.

name: Losing Clarity (Human Contact, Embracing Virtue)
summary: Clarity never 'breaks' the way a Solar's Limit does; only temporary Clarity can be shed at all, and only through two means - meaningfully connecting with mortals, or successfully spending Willpower to act on a Virtue - while permanent Clarity is locked in place for as long as its granting condition (high Essence, an installed Charm) persists.
mechanics: Human Contact: at the end of any scene in which the Exalt meaningfully interacts with normal humans, roll her Compassion at standard difficulty (subject to Clarity's own Social/Compassion dice penalty, if any); success removes 1 point of temporary Clarity, while a botch instead deepens her alienation and adds 1 point of Clarity. This method can only reduce Clarity by 1 point per day, no matter how many qualifying scenes occur. Embracing Virtue: whenever an Alchemical spends Willpower to channel a Virtue and the resulting action succeeds, she loses 1 point of temporary Clarity. Permanent Clarity is unaffected by either method and can only be reduced by removing the Essence-above-5 or Charm condition that granted it in the first place.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Losing Clarity' section, p. 70 (PDF 71); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image.

name: Effects of Clarity (0-10 social/behavioral table)
summary: As an Alchemical's total (permanent plus temporary) Clarity rises through five bands from 0 up to the fixed maximum of 10, her capacity to empathize with mortals steadily erodes while her rapport with Autochthonian gods, automata, and fellow high-Clarity Alchemicals grows; the book pairs this dice-mechanical progression with explicit guidance that high Clarity should read as alien and unsettling rather than as sadistic or as license for gratuitous cruelty.
mechanics: 0-2: no detectable dissociation; the character is exactly as pleasant as her Social Attributes/Abilities suggest. 3-4: noticeably colder and less patient; -1 die to all Social rolls except intimidation when dealing with most sentient/feeling beings, but +1 die to Social rolls (including intimidation) with Autochthonian deities, automata, and Alchemicals of equal-or-greater Clarity; also -1 die to Compassion rolls. 5-7: notably inhuman, clipped and laconic, ignoring mortals' emotional needs by default and reporting or chastising dissent; the Social penalty/bonus pair widens to 2 dice. 8-9: humanity is a distant memory; she can simulate courtesy with effort but feels nothing; the Social penalty/bonus pair widens to 3 dice, and she gains +1 die on Mental Attribute or Temperance rolls involving memory, analytical deduction, or dispassionate self-control (Storyteller's call on which rolls qualify). 10 (maximum): aloof and utterly alien, entirely amoral but not malicious, retaining full free will and Nature-driven goals; the Social penalty/bonus pair widens to 4 dice, she automatically fails all Compassion rolls, and the qualifying Mental/Temperance bonus widens to 2 dice. A companion 'Playing and Storytelling Clarity' section stresses that Clarity changes how a character pursues her existing Nature-driven goals (toward cold efficiency and minimum necessary force), not whether she has goals at all, and that even Clarity 10 characters plan and weigh consequences rather than reveling in violence.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Effects of Clarity' table and 'Playing and Storytelling Clarity' guidance, pp. 70-71 (PDF 71-72); visually cross-checked against rendered page images.

name: Gremlin Syndrome (Dissonance, Alchemical-only Flaw)
summary: A small, growing minority of Alchemicals manifest Dissonance instead of Clarity - a Void-tainted mirror Trait that imposes the same rising Social/Compassion penalties as Clarity but grants none of Clarity's positive bonuses (except among fellow gremlins), replaces Clarity's calm cognitive bonus with a raw damage bonus at maximum rating, and expresses as active, gleeful sociopathy rather than cold order; Autochthonian society hunts down and executes anyone confirmed to have it.
mechanics: Dissonance is purchased as an Alchemical-only Flaw worth 5 bonus points. It tracks and penalizes exactly like Clarity for Social interactions and Compassion, but a Dissonant character gains no Social bonus at any Clarity-equivalent band except when dealing with other gremlins or similarly mad beings, and receives no bonus dice for calculated thought/self-control at high ratings; instead, a Dissonance rating of 10 adds 1 die to the raw damage of all attacks, reflecting sheer brutality rather than precision. Where Clarity tends toward building and preserving order, Dissonance tears it down at every opportunity, punctuated by brief lucid periods whenever channeled Virtues knock the rating back down. The book explicitly restricts this Flaw to Storyteller antagonists or, at most, rare tragic PCs played by very mature players who understand the character is likely to end up hunted and destroyed.
compatibility: Any Alchemical caste, if the Storyteller allows the Flaw at all; intended primarily for Storyteller characters.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Gremlin Syndrome' sidebar, p. 71 (PDF 72).

name: Class (new Background, replaces Followers/Influence/Resources)
summary: Class is the core socioeconomic Background for anyone in Autochthonia's largely currency-less economy, folding Followers, Influence and Resources into a single rating that sets social standing, requisition authority, and standard of living; Alchemicals automatically receive Class ••• for free at creation (separate from their normal Background dots) and may raise it further with bonus points, while mortal characters must purchase it from scratch like any other Background.
mechanics: Dot table: no dots (x) - a Lumpen outcast; a tolerable Resources •-equivalent standard of living, but a 1-die penalty to Social pools against higher-Class characters (also the rating held by surface slaves taken during the Locust Crusade). 1 dot - a general laborer/aide of the Populat; Resources ••-equivalent, dormitory housing shared by dozens with no personal claim to space (also shared, after a successful Locust Crusade, by loyalist Outsider-caste Creation-dwellers who are barred from entering Autochthonia). 2 dots - a Populat shift chief overoseeing 20-300 workers; Resources •••-equivalent, apartment shared with roughly a dozen peers. 3 dots - a Populat foreman overseeing an entire factory, or a junior Tripartite member (expected to also carry 1-2 dots of matching Backing); lives at Resources ••• with a dedicated aide staff but can requisition up to Resources ••••, subject to superiors demanding justification; +1 die to Social rolls against lower-Class Autochthonians. 4 dots - a Populat supervisor over an entire industry in a city, or a veteran Tripartite member (2-3 dots of Backing expected); Resources ••• or •••• standard of living, can requisition as high as Resources ••••• at the risk of scrutiny; +1 die to Social rolls against lower-Class Autochthonians. 5 dots - a Populat director/sub-director or senior Tripartite leader (4-5 dots of Backing expected); palatial residence at Resources •••• or •••••; +2 dice to Social rolls against lower-Class Autochthonians. Lumpen exiled to the Reaches for serious crimes exist entirely outside this Background and receive no resource allocation at all; any status they hold is purchased as Backing instead, and any hoarded wealth or followers come from Resources/Followers under the Solar rules, options otherwise closed to ordinary Autochthonians.
cost: Background dots (0-5), as with any Background; Alchemicals start with a free, separate Class ••• at character creation.
compatibility: All Alchemicals and Autochthonian mortals; Lumpen exiles in the Reaches use Backing/Resources/Followers instead.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Expanded Backgrounds' -> 'Class' section, pp. 66-67 (PDF 67-68); dot table visually cross-checked against a rendered page image.

name: Artifact (altered for Alchemicals)
summary: Alchemicals draw on the full resources of Autochthonian industry, so each dot of the Artifact Background buys three total dots of Artifact-rated gear rather than one, the Background may be bought all the way to ••••• during character creation without bonus points (though the 4th and 5th dot each cost two dots), and dots here can additionally buy spare Charms held on retainer at the Vats up to the character's Essence rating.
mechanics: Most Alchemical-owned artifacts are built from the same Magical Material as the Exalt's own Caste, though this is not a hard requirement. Because the total combined Artifact rating purchased per Background dot is tripled relative to core Exalted, and because character creation alone permits reaching ••••• (at extra cost for the last two dots), Alchemicals field noticeably more equipment than other Exalted of comparable Background investment. Separately, Artifact dots may buy additional Charms as artifacts (rated up to the character's minimum qualifying Essence, and only for Charms whose Trait prerequisites the character actually meets); these Charms are kept on retainer at the Vats and do not count against or increase the number of Charms installed in Slots.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Expanded Backgrounds' -> 'Artifact' section, p. 65 (PDF 66).

name: Backing (altered for Alchemicals/Autochthonians)
summary: Because Autochthonia has no independent power blocs, Backing represents rank inside a specific named branch of the Tripartite - the Olgotary's plutarchs, regulators or adjudicators; the Theomachracy's lectors, preceptors or clerics; or one of the Five Sodalities (Luminors, Conductors, Harvesters, Scholars, Surgeons) - and requires Class •••+ as a prerequisite; a rare, dangerous alternative exists in Backing held within an exile colony (no Class requirement) or an outlawed Voidbringer/black-market circle.
mechanics: Characters who are autocrats, celebrants or councilors must hold Backing ••••• in the matching branch of the Olgotary, the Theomachracy, or a Sodality respectively. Backing purchased for standing in a specific Reaches exile colony is understandably limited in scope since it lacks a Class rating behind it. A small number of demented cultists and criminals hold Backing in a Voidbringer sect or the black market instead, at the risk of execution if the authorities ever discover the membership.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes and Autochthonian mortals with Class •••+ for legitimate Tripartite Backing; exile-colony and illicit Backing bypass the Class prerequisite entirely.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Expanded Backgrounds' -> 'Backing' section, pp. 65-66 (PDF 66-67).

name: Familiar (altered for Alchemicals: requisitioned constructs)
summary: Autochthonia has almost no biological fauna, so Alchemicals do not keep familiars the way other Exalted do; instead the Background sets the maximum power of a spirit-built construct servitor the character may telepathically requisition from the Autochthonian gods on demand, one at a time, with a replacement automatically dispatched if the current one is lost or dismissed.
mechanics: A character's rating caps the power of any single familiar summoned, not the properties of one fixed creature; only one familiar may be kept at a time, but losing or dismissing it lets the character immediately requisition another. A familiar still functions in Creation (but not the Wyld, Underworld, or Malfeas) and always knows the exact direction back to its master. Dot table: no dots (x) - human retainers only, or none at all. 1 dot - a small, mostly harmless servitor with Intelligence • and one marginally useful function, able to share one sense within (Essence x 10) yards, obeying verbal commands exactly (even suicidal ones); arrives within an hour inside Autochthonia. 2 dots - larger and either moderately dangerous (guard-dog-analogous) or smarter (Intelligence ••); arrives within three hours. 3 dots - up to the character's own size or as small as a spy-drone insect, usually Intelligence •• (or ••• at a cost to other prowess), combat models rivaling great cats/dire wolves, peaceful models with up to three distinct useful capabilities (one may allow telepathic messaging in shared-sense range), the largest usable as a steed; arrives within a day. 4 dots - up to twice the character's size, Intelligence •• if built for combat (armored, weaponized), or highly mobile/fast if built for transport (wall-climbing, flight), or a master craftsperson with auxiliary skills if built for peaceful tasks; can communicate telepathically and usually speaks passable Autochthonic; arrives within a week (custom-built). 5 dots - an Essence 3 mechanical god in its own right with an appropriate Charm suite, potentially multiple forms up to yeddim-scale, typically materializes with the Dematerialize Charm, superhuman combat skill or multi-mode transit/portal-opening for steeds, or Intelligence ••• seneschal-grade competence for support roles, with telepathy/shared senses out to a mile; takes up to a month to arrive.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes; mortals may not purchase this Background.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Expanded Backgrounds' -> 'Familiar' section, pp. 66-68 (PDF 67-69); dot table visually cross-checked against rendered page images.

name: Manse (restricted for Alchemicals: Autochthonia has none)
summary: Autochthonia contains no actual Manses, so the Manse Background is entirely off-limits to Alchemical characters in any story set while the Seal of Eight Divinities remains unbroken; once the Locust Crusade begins and Alchemicals reach Creation, they discover geomancy as a power source and purchase/use Manse exactly like a Solar Exalt.
mechanics: Prior to contact with Creation, this Background simply cannot be purchased or used by Alchemical characters - there is nothing in Autochthonia for it to represent. After Alchemicals begin operating in Creation (post-Locust-Crusade era, or any story that puts them there), the Background reverts to functioning identically to the standard core-Exalted Manse Background.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes, but only in stories set after contact with Creation; unavailable entirely for stories confined to Autochthonia before the Seal breaks.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Expanded Backgrounds' -> 'Manse' section, p. 68 (PDF 69).

name: Vats (new Background)
summary: Vats tracks an Alchemical's standing access to her home city's Vat Complex: how many spare Charms she keeps on retainer beyond her installed Slots, and how quickly the Complex will schedule a refit for her, functioning simultaneously as a status reward and a practical necessity for characters whose duties change frequently; a Vat can also be used to accelerate healing and Essence recovery.
mechanics: Dot table: no dots (x) - no special access; must submit formal refit requests at least a month ahead for minor work (Charms, Attributes) or six months for Essence increases. 1 dot - one extra Charm on retainer; two weeks' notice for minor refits, two months for major upgrades. 2 dots - two extra Charms; a full week's notice for minor refits, a month for major upgrades. 3 dots - three extra Charms; two days' to two weeks' notice depending on complexity. 4 dots - four extra Charms; one day's to one week's notice depending on severity. 5 dots - five extra Charms; refit requests receive immediate priority with no advance notice required, barring the Vats already being at full capacity. Separately, an Alchemical may plug into a Vat to accelerate recovery: for every hour spent, she regains (Essence x 5) motes and multiplies her healing rate by her permanent Essence while she slumbers; she will not wake on her own until fully recovered, and forcibly waking her early costs 1 point of Willpower plus 1 unsoakable level of bashing damage from spiritual shock. She may request as much recovery slumber time as needed, provided she gives (5 minus her Vats rating) hours' notice.
cost: Background dots (0-5), as with any Background.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Expanded Backgrounds' -> 'Vats' section, pp. 68-69 (PDF 69-70); dot table visually cross-checked against a rendered page image.

name: Building a Vat Complex in Creation (sidebar)
summary: Alchemicals operating away from Autochthonia lack access to a real Vat Complex, so the book provides rules for improvising one out of a converted Manse: an expensive, slow, and permanently Hearthstone-destroying substitute that keeps Alchemicals refit-capable while abroad but is strictly a maintenance tool, never a means of creating new Alchemical Exalted.
mechanics: Building a synthetic Vat Complex requires a level-4+ Manse and exotic ingredients costing Resources •••••; the technician directing the month-long construction must have ••••• in both Lore and Occult and •••• in Craft (Architecture). Converting a Manse this way permanently destroys any Hearthstone it produces (and crumbles any existing Hearthstone to dust); the site no longer generates ambient Essence to respire. Every use of a synthetic Vat to upgrade an Alchemical costs ongoing Resources: •••• for Essence 3-5, ••••• for Essence 6+, and ••• for all other upgrade uses except accelerated healing/Essence recovery, and all repairs/upgrades performed there take twice as long as they would in Autochthonia. Access to a synthetic Vat costs the same Background dots as access to a real one inside Autochthonia, provided the structure exists yet. It is never possible to build wholly new Alchemical Exalted at a Vat built outside Autochthonia - only Autochthon's own return to Creation could change that.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes operating in Creation, contingent on someone actually funding and building the synthetic Complex first.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Building Vats' sidebar, p. 69 (PDF 70); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image.

name: Followers, Influence, and Resources (subsumed into Class)
summary: A clarifying note that these three standard Backgrounds do not exist independently for ordinary Autochthonians - they are folded entirely into Class - with a single carve-out for Exile characters living in the Reaches' colonies, who fall outside the Class system and may purchase Followers or Resources under the normal core-Exalted rules; Influence has no application inside Autochthonia at all, for anyone.
mechanics: For any character subject to the Class Background (i.e., essentially everyone inside civilized Autochthonia), Followers, Influence and Resources are not separately purchasable; their effects are represented by the character's Class rating instead. Exiles in the Reaches, who exist entirely outside the Class system, may buy Followers or Resources exactly as Solar Exalted would. Influence is simply unused within Autochthonia under any circumstances.
compatibility: Civilized Autochthonians (including Alchemicals): excluded from these three Backgrounds in favor of Class. Reaches exile characters: may use Followers/Resources normally.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Expanded Backgrounds' -> 'Followers, Influence and Resources' section, p. 68 (PDF 69). Classified excluded rather than reference-only because it actively forecloses three standard Background options for the ordinary chargen path, matching the rationale used for Abyssal's cult-and-the-abyssals row.

name: Alchemical Bonus Points and Experience Costs
summary: Alchemical character creation and post-creation advancement use their own bonus-point and experience-cost tables, distinct from core Exalted, because Alchemicals raise Attributes/Essence/Charms exclusively through Vat refits and because Charm Slots (General vs. Dedicated) and Martial Arts Charms carry their own bought-and-installed costs on top of ordinary trait purchases.
mechanics: Bonus point costs (15 points available at creation): Attribute 4 (3 for a Caste or Favored Attribute); Ability 2; Background 1 (2 if raised above •••); Specialty 1; Virtue 3; Willpower 2; Essence 10; Charm Slot 6 for General or 5 for Dedicated (each purchase includes one free qualifying Charm); Martial Arts Charm 6 (requires the Perfected Lotus Matrix Charm already installed). Experience costs (post-creation): Caste or Favored Attribute increase = (current rating x 4) - 1; new General Charm Slot = 12 (includes one free Charm the character qualifies for); new Dedicated Charm Slot = 10 (includes one free Charm for a Caste/Favored Attribute the character qualifies for); new Martial Arts Charm = 11 (requires the Perfected Lotus Matrix Charm); new Man Machine Weaving Protocol = 12; new God Machine Weaving Protocol = 14; upgrading a Charm Slot from Dedicated to General = 2; a new Charm placed on retainer at the Vats (without a Slot to house it) = 6; Essence increase = (current rating x 9).
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Two: Character Creation and Traits, 'Bonus Points' and 'Experience Costs' tables, p. 64 (PDF 65). Man Machine Weaving Protocol / God Machine Weaving Protocol / Martial Arts Charm and Perfected Lotus Matrix are Chapter Three Charm-system terms referenced here only because they appear directly in this cost table; the Charms themselves are out of scope for this inventory pass.

name: Charm Slots, Panoplies, Submodules, and Arrays
summary: Explains the core Alchemical Charm-as-implant model: Charms are surgically installed in General or Dedicated Charm Slots up to a hard limit, spare Charms are stockpiled as a "Panoply," a single Charm can be permanently expanded with cheap "submodule" upgrades, and Alchemicals build "Arrays" (their version of a Combo) that bundle several Charms into one surgically-installed unit with a reduced combined installation cost and automatic access to every legal Combo among its members.
mechanics: Charm Slots come in two varieties: General (holds any Charm) and Dedicated (only Charms tied to a Favored or Caste Attribute). Starting characters get 4 Dedicated and 4 General Slots plus 8 Charms to fill them. Additional Slots may be bought with bonus points at creation or xp plus a surgical refit during play; every new Slot comes with a free qualifying Charm of the player's choice. Alchemicals may also hold Charms beyond their Slots via the Vats or Artifact Backgrounds; once play begins, extra Panoply Charms (without a new Slot) cost 6 xp. The Charms held in reserve at the Vats are collectively called a Panoply. At the Vats, an Alchemical may swap any installed Charms for Panoply Charms or leave Slots empty (e.g. to conserve Personal Essence), and may upgrade a Dedicated Slot to General for 2 xp; refitting takes time (see alchemical-refitting-essence-and-evolution). Submodules are fixed-xp permanent upgrades to a single specific installed Charm; whenever that Charm is installed, all its purchased submodules are also available. Most submodules need an hour of refit at the Vats. Submodules should generally be weaker than a full Charm; anything as powerful as a Charm should cost more, need a notably higher minimum Essence, or simply be a new Charm. Arrays: cost 1 bonus point per Charm included, or xp equal to the sum of the minimum Attribute ratings of every Charm in the Array; unlike a Combo, any Attribute-based Charm may join an Array (supernatural martial arts Charms are excluded). Once linked, the arrangement is permanent; owning the same Charm both in and out of an Array (or in two Arrays) requires buying separate copies, though any submodules purchased for a Charm automatically apply to every copy for free. Arrays grant two benefits: Reduced Installation Cost (the whole Array has one combined installation cost equal to three-fourths of the summed installation costs of its component Charms, rounded up, but the entire Array must be installed or removed as a single unit — no partial installation) and Integrated Combos (the Alchemical automatically has access to every possible Combo that could be built from instant-duration Charms in the Array that could benefit the same action, plus any reflexive Charms regardless of action; the Storyteller is final arbiter of legality; activating an integrated Combo costs 1 Willpower on the first Charm as with any Combo, and such Combos should have their own name/visual display, ideally planned in advance or built from the first stunt that uses them).
compatibility: All Alchemical castes.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Charm Slots and Panoplies' / 'Submodules' / 'Arrays' sections, pp. 89-90 (PDF 90-91).

name: Designing New Charms & Eclipse/Moonshadow Access to Alchemical Charms
summary: Storyteller-facing rules for how brand-new Alchemical Charms or submodules formally enter play (either by Storyteller fiat or an in-fiction design-and-submission process at a patropolis), plus the separate mechanism letting Solar Eclipse and Lunar Moonshadow Caste Exalted buy limited access to the Alchemical Charm list through their own anima powers.
mechanics: Two ways to add a new Charm beyond the book's list: (1) the Storyteller simply rules the Charm already exists, and the character obtains it on her next refit or via experience as usual; (2) the character spends a number of weeks equal to the Charm's minimum Attribute rating designing the artifact, then formally submits the design to her home city's patropolis; if approved, the template is added to the city's Vats records (available to any Exalt), and a functional copy costs normal experience a month later. New Charm designs become a valuable commodity traded between cities for favors, resources, or other templates, and most spread across the Eight Nations within a year. Designing a submodule follows the same process but needs only one week of planning, becoming available a week after the patropolis affirms it. Separately, through their anima powers Eclipse and Moonshadow Caste Exalted can "learn" Alchemical Charms for 20 xp each, requiring the same kind of surgical refit at a Vat Complex as an Alchemical; each purchase grants one General Charm Slot plus the desired Charm. As long as the character retains whatever grace granted her access to Autochthonia's technological secrets, she may add further Panoply Charms for 8 xp instead of paying for new Slots. Neither caste may build Arrays, though they can form ordinary Combos of Attribute and Ability Charms provided every non-reflexive Charm in the Combo benefits the same action (a Combo relying on an installed Alchemical Charm only works while that Charm remains installed). An Exalt with empty Charm Slots still visibly displays odd magitech implants even with no Charms currently installed. Non-Alchemicals cannot learn weaving Charms, and the Storyteller may bar any other Charm from these castes for balance or fairness.
compatibility: Storyteller guidance for all Alchemicals; the Eclipse/Moonshadow clause applies specifically to Solar Eclipse Caste and Lunar Moonshadow Caste characters who gain access via their own anima powers.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Designing New Charms' / 'Eclipses and Moonshadows' sections, p. 90 (PDF 91).

name: Alchemical Charm Format, Limitations, and Presentation Conventions
summary: A short rules-conventions passage explaining how Alchemical Charm write-ups differ from other Exalted's stat blocks: a new "permanent" Charm Type for always-on installed effects, a Prerequisite Charms field meaning devices the Exalt must already have installed or hold in her Panoply, the fact that Alchemicals deliberately lack the universal perfect/persistent defenses other Celestial Exalted enjoy, that called shots cannot target Charms as if they were separate body parts, and that Essence 8+ "municipal" Charms work on an urban scale.
mechanics: Type gains a new option, 'Permanent': like Ox-Body Technique, such Charms are always considered active as long as they remain installed, have no listed duration or activation cost, and their listed cost is simply the installation cost. Prerequisite Charms lists devices the Alchemical must already have installed or stored in her Panoply before this Charm can be added — mere knowledge is not enough, unlike other Exalted's Charm trees. Alchemical Charms are Celestial-level in raw power, but this splat pointedly lacks any all-purpose perfect or persistent defense; instead it fields many narrower, specialized defensive Charms that a clever opponent can route around. Every Attribute has one basic dice-adding Charm, but it can never add more bonus dice to a pool than the Attribute's own rating; a separate family of Charms instead grants artificial-specialty-type bonuses that stack cumulatively with true specialties rather than counting as ordinary Charm dice. Because Alchemical Charms are literally part of the Exalt's body, called shots cannot disable them any more than a called shot could take out another character's eyes or hands. Charms requiring Essence 8+ are termed 'municipal' Charms, since they function on an urban scale — an entire factory or basic-infrastructure facet may itself constitute a single such Charm for these enormous beings.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes; these are stat-block reading conventions that apply to every Charm presented in the chapter.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Limitations and Effect' / 'Presentation' sections, p. 91 (PDF 92). Classified reference-only rather than calculated because this is purely a stat-block-reading-convention and design-philosophy passage, not a discrete formula or player choice in its own right.

name: Transitory Augmentation of (Attribute)
summary: The universal Attribute-boosting General Charm — really nine separately-purchased Charms, one per Attribute — that lets an Alchemical temporarily add dots to that Attribute for a single instant action, and cheapens her anima power's own Attribute boost when installed for a Caste or Favored Attribute.
requirements: Minimum (Attribute) 1; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None. Purchased and installed separately for each of the nine Attributes.
mechanics: For every mote spent, add one dot to the controlling Attribute for the purposes of a single instant-duration action or event, up to a maximum bonus equal to the Attribute's own base rating. An Alchemical who has this Charm installed for a Caste or Favored Attribute reduces the cost of her anima power's Attribute boost (see alchemical-anima-banners-universal) from 3 motes per die to 2 motes per die.
cost: 1 mote per die; Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Reflexive. General Charms category (fits any Charm Slot).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'General Charms' -> 'Transitory Augmentation of (Attribute)', p. 91 (PDF 92).

name: Sustained Augmentation of (Attribute)
summary: The permanent-Type counterpart to Transitory Augmentation — nine separately-installed Charms, one per Attribute — that mechanically reinforce the Exalt's body or mind, granting a flat +1 dot to that Attribute's natural rating and raising its maximum possible rating by one dot for as long as the Charm stays installed.
requirements: Minimum (Attribute) 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None. Purchased and installed separately for each Attribute; a character cannot install more than one copy for the same Attribute, but may have as many different Attributes augmented as desired.
mechanics: No activation cost or duration; the Charm is simply always in effect once installed (Type: Permanent). The Exalt gains one additional dot to the chosen Attribute, counted as part of her natural rating rather than a dispellable bonus, and her maximum possible rating in that Attribute rises by one dot. Flavor ties the specific implant to its Attribute: metal pistons alongside artificial muscle for Strength, ball-bearing joints and higher-function motor skills for Dexterity, organic metal-alloy flesh for Stamina, hardwired protocols for Charisma or Manipulation, a literally sculpted physique for Appearance, integrated sensors for Perception, and transcendent neural webs for Intelligence or Wits.
compatibility: Duration: N/A. Type: Permanent. General Charms category (fits any Charm Slot); listed as a qualifying prerequisite ('Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of...') for most other Attribute-keyed Charms in this chapter.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'General Charms' -> 'Sustained Augmentation of (Attribute)', pp. 91-92 (PDF 92-93).

name: Tactical Analysis Engrams
summary: A cluster of skull-mounted analytic implants that let an Alchemical instantly read tell-tale combat data off any target she studies, from raw Trait ratings to the exact statistics of weapons, armor, and visible offensive Charms.
requirements: Minimum Wits 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Wits.
mechanics: Roll Wits + Awareness (difficulty 2) on activation; each success reveals one piece of information the player selects: the target's rating in any one Physical Attribute, Wits, Archery, Athletics, Brawl, Dodge, Endurance, Martial Arts, Melee, Resistance or Thrown (Storytellers may allow other Traits in extreme cases, learning only the bare rating without identifying the Trait); all the target's specialties in one such Trait; the target's base initiative; the target's current wound-penalty rating; the core statistics of any one weapon/attack the Alchemical has seen the target use; the core statistics of any one worn armor or shield; or the function of any one visible, or previously-used-in-scene, directly combative Alchemical Charm installed in the target (this can extend to combative spirit Charms known in Autochthonia after a month of regular exposure and a cost of 3 xp per type of being). Each full minute spent observing the same target lets the Exalt reuse this Charm against that target for free, without spending Essence.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Reflexive. Close Combat Charms tree (Wits-keyed); root of the Wits branch of that tree.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, first Charm, pp. 92-93 (PDF 93-94); visually cross-checked against the Close Combat Charms I tree diagram (p. 92/PDF 93).

name: Accelerated Response System
summary: A pair of separately-installable defensive implants — one in the shoulders/arms for a full-pool parry, one in the hips/thighs for a full-pool dodge — letting an Alchemical fend off a single incoming attack with total commitment.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Dexterity.
mechanics: Two permutations must be bought and installed separately. The shoulder/arm version lets the Exalt parry a single attack against her using her full Dexterity + (Brawl, Martial Arts or Melee) pool on activation. The hip/thigh version lets her dodge one attack using her full Dexterity + Dodge pool (plus Essence under Exalted Power Combat), contorting away without giving ground. Both require the Alchemical to be aware of the incoming attack; a character with both variants installed may use both against the same attack.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Reflexive. Close Combat Charms tree (Dexterity-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, p. 93 (PDF 94); visually cross-checked against the Close Combat Charms I tree diagram.

name: Dynamic Reaction Enhancement System
summary: A spinal implant that lets an Alchemical burn Essence just before acting to slow her perception of the turn, buying extra initiative.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Dexterity.
mechanics: Activated prior to the character's initiative roll; adds +2 initiative for every mote spent, to a maximum bonus of (Dexterity x 2).
cost: 1 mote per +2 initiative; Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Reflexive. Close Combat Charms tree (Dexterity-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, p. 93 (PDF 94); visually cross-checked against the Close Combat Charms I tree diagram.

name: Celerity Enabling Module
summary: A joint-and-spine implant wired to the Dynamic Reaction Enhancement System that grants either a burst of superhuman extra actions or, alternatively, a scene-long ability to reflexively dodge or parry every attack from one chosen foe.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Dynamic Reaction Enhancement System.
mechanics: Two mutually exclusive modes, never used simultaneously. Primary mode (instant, Extra Action): grants a number of extra actions equal to permanent Essence, usable for any physical task, including declaring or refreshing a full dodge or full parry to its maximum pool. Secondary mode (reflexive, one scene): the Exalt selects a single target and may, for the rest of the scene, dodge or parry every attack that target makes against him using his full dice pool (choosing per attack), without needing to be aware of the attack; the Charm automatically supplies a parry against undodgeable attacks and a dodge against unparriable ones, and lets the Exalt parry lethal attacks unarmed via Brawl, Martial Arts or Melee without a stunt. Selecting a new target, or switching to the extra-action mode, requires reactivating the Charm at full cost, immediately ending all current defenses against the prior target.
compatibility: Duration: Instant/One scene. Type: Extra Action/Reflexive. Close Combat Charms tree (Dexterity-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, pp. 93-94 (PDF 94-95); visually cross-checked against the Close Combat Charms I tree diagram.

name: Anticipatory Simulation Processor
summary: A starmetal-monofilament brain implant that lets an Alchemical's mind race ahead of time itself, provisionally living out a turn's events so she can "rewind" and change her action if the outcome goes badly, at the cost of temporary Clarity.
requirements: Minimum Wits 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Wits, Accelerated Response System, Celerity Enabling Module.
mechanics: The player may declare the Charm's use at any point in a turn for 5 motes (this also awards the Alchemical 1 point of temporary Clarity). The turn then plays out normally, but at any point before it ends the player may reflexively spend another 5 motes and 1 Willpower to "rewind" the turn back to the initiative count when the Charm first activated; in-fiction, the character has merely simulated the intervening events, which have not truly happened outside her mind. Unless and until the Alchemical deviates from the earlier simulated sequence, every subsequent roll and action repeats exactly as before; once she deviates, real play resumes and no character is bound by the earlier prediction beyond actions already declared within that turn. Because the Charm relies on intuition and mental acumen rather than true precognition, it cannot be activated in encounters where Primordials, Malfeans, or unshaped raksha have directly acted, since their transcendent, alien nature defies simulation by lesser beings.
cost: 5 motes (plus a further 5 motes and 1 Willpower to rewind); Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Reflexive. Close Combat Charms tree (Wits-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, p. 94 (PDF 95); visually cross-checked against the Close Combat Charms I tree diagram.

name: Polymodal Joint Bearings
summary: Ball-bearing joint implants granting superhuman flexibility, useful for escaping bindings or clinches and contorting through tight defenses, with an optional submodule that removes offhand penalties and lets feet work as hands.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Dexterity.
mechanics: While active, adds three dice to rolls to escape manacles or other bindings, control or escape a clinch, dodge via extreme contortion, or perform any other feat where preternatural flexibility clearly helps (the Storyteller may deny or reduce the benefit for dubious applicability); these bonus dice are a form of artificial specialty, cumulative with true specialties. The omnidextrous submodule (2 bonus points/6 xp, requires Wits 3+) removes the usual offhand-action penalty entirely and lets the character use his feet as hands for tool use or fine-dexterity feats without penalty (unarmed foot strikes remain classified as kicks).
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Simple. Close Combat Charms tree (Dexterity-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, pp. 94-95 (PDF 95-96); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image and the Close Combat Charms I tree diagram.

name: Limb Extension Armatures
summary: Telescoping or moonsilver-stretching limb implants that let an Alchemical extend her reach dramatically, adding speed to hand-to-hand strikes made at extended range and letting her strike mounted foes without penalty.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Dexterity.
mechanics: While active, limbs reach up to (Essence x 2) additional yards for Alchemicals of permanent Essence 2-5, or (Essence x 4) additional yards for Essence 6+; limbs extend or retract reflexively at will. For every two yards of extra reach used at maximum extension, add 1 to the speed modifier of hand-to-hand attacks; the character may also strike mounted targets without penalty. Advantages of added reach outside combat are largely situational, subject to player imagination and Storyteller approval.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Simple. Close Combat Charms tree (Dexterity-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, p. 95 (PDF 96); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image and the Close Combat Charms II/III tree diagram.

name: Multi-Limb Frame
summary: Surgically-added extra limbs (insectoid, humanoid, or Moonsilver-quicksilver tendrils depending on caste and preference) that reduce multiple-action penalties, installable repeatedly up to the Exalt's Dexterity or Wits, or alternatively installed permanently in place of the character's original arms.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Sustained Augmentation of Dexterity.
mechanics: Simple-type installation grants one or two extra limbs per installation (paralyzed/folded without committed Essence; usable as normal arms/hands when activated) and reduces multiple-action penalties for physical actions using any arm by one die per installation, stacking across repeated installations up to a maximum equal to the character's Dexterity or Wits, whichever is lower; unused limbs fold visibly against the body (or hide in compartments if the character also has an Integrated Artifact Transmogrifier). Alternatively, install as a Permanent-type Charm (1 mote installation cost) replacing the character's arms outright with overtly artificial limbs instead of adding extras; this does not count against the installation cap, applies the same cumulative multiple-action-penalty reduction, and adds +1 to hand-to-hand damage dealt through those limbs (or a weapon they hold). Any installation of this Charm also removes the offhand-action penalty for any limb — including natural hands and Hyperdextrous Tentacle Apparatus appendages — provided the Exalt also has Sustained Augmentation of Wits installed.
cost: 1 mote (simple) / None (permanent); Installation Cost: None (simple) / 1 mote (permanent).
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite (simple) / N/A (permanent). Type: Simple/Permanent. Close Combat Charms tree (Dexterity-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, p. 95 (PDF 96); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image and the Close Combat Charms II/III tree diagram.

name: Hyperdextrous Tentacle Apparatus
summary: A pair of long, clawed metal tentacles emerging from the torso that can act as extra dexterous limbs, strike or clinch as improvised weapons, and, when fully empowered, act independently in combat at the cost of the Exalt's first point of permanent Clarity.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Sustained Augmentation of Strength, Sustained Augmentation of Wits, Multi-Limb Frame. Installable a maximum number of times equal to the Exalt's Essence.
mechanics: Un-activated, the tentacles function as long-reaching arms/hands (reach of permanent Essence yards, doubled at Essence 6+, further extendable by Limb Extension Armatures), reducing multiple-action penalties as Multi-Limb Frame does, cumulatively with it. Used as weapons for striking or parrying: speed +(Essence x 2), accuracy +(Essence), damage +(Dexterity)L, defense +(Essence), rate equal to Wits under Exalted Power Combat; their length allows a sweep maneuver. Used to clinch: accuracy and defense +(number of tentacles performing the grab), rate 1 under Exalted Power Combat. For 8 motes and 1 Willpower, the Alchemical can simultaneously empower every tentacle from every installation, giving each independent life: she may take multiple actions normally at standard (possibly reduced) penalties, each tentacle takes its first action of every turn at her full dice pool, and for every empowered tentacle gripping a victim in a clinch beyond the first she may make extra constriction attempts each turn (Exalted Players Guide, p. 205). The first installation of this Charm grants the Alchemical 1 point of permanent Clarity.
cost: 8 motes, 1 Willpower (to empower all tentacles); Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: One scene. Type: Simple. Close Combat Charms tree (Dexterity-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, pp. 95-96 (PDF 96-97); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image and the Close Combat Charms II/III tree diagram.

name: Integrated Arsenal Upgrade
summary: Built-in hand-to-hand weapons (two per installation) housed inside an Alchemical's Multi-Limb Frame appendages, foldable in and out on command and effectively impossible to disarm.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Multi-Limb Frame.
mechanics: Grants two weapons per installation, each anchored in an extra or replaced Multi-Limb Frame appendage; one reflexive action retracts any number into hidden compartments, another reflexively deploys them (only one weapon deployed per limb at a time, though several can be stored in one arm). Any weapon form is permitted (sword, lance, chain, spinning drill, etc.), using the statistics of the closest mundane weapon type (a drill bit might use knife statistics but deal piercing damage); an hour of upgrade at the Vats (1 bonus point/2 xp) makes a given weapon exceptional, and exceptional weapons may later become perfect weapons for the same cost (Exalted Players Guide, p. 145). Two-handed weapons fold into a single limb but usually need two limbs to wield; an Exalt with Strength double the weapon's requirement may wield it one-handed at -1 to accuracy and defense. Built-in weapons cannot be disarmed by any means, even magic; a destroyed weapon regrows over the course of a week.
compatibility: Duration: N/A. Type: Permanent. Close Combat Charms tree (Dexterity-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, pp. 96-97 (PDF 97-98); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image and the Close Combat Charms II/III tree diagram.

name: (Material) Synthesis Wave Emitter
summary: A set of six separately-purchased Charms — one per Magical Material, plus an adamant version — that channels the Exalt's anima through a hand-to-hand strike, imbuing it with the relevant Material's combat bonus or, for adamant, a sharpness that shreds armor.
requirements: Minimum Strength 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory Augmentation of Strength. Alchemicals automatically treat the version matching their own Caste's Material as Favored, regardless of whether Strength is itself a Favored/Caste Attribute.
mechanics: Used supplementally with a hand-to-hand attack; the striking weapon or limb glows and trails dust of the chosen Material. For the five Magical Materials, applies that Material's standard melee-weapon bonus to the strike (per core Exalted, p. 341, and the Exalted Players Guide, p. 209). The adamant version instead reduces the target's armored soak by 4 on a successful hit, making bladed weapons extremely sharp or blunt attacks shatteringly forceful. Also usable when striking with an actual magical weapon of the matching Material, in which case identical bonuses stack. Alchemicals with multiple versions installed may apply different ones to different attacks in the same turn, but cannot stack multiple versions onto a single attack without a Combo.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Supplemental. Close Combat Charms tree (Strength-keyed); six Charms in one family (five Magical Materials plus adamant).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, p. 97 (PDF 98); visually cross-checked against the Close Combat Charms III tree diagram.

name: Transcendent Multimodal Weapon Matrix
summary: A hand-mounted assembly of the Alchemical's Caste Material that lets her grow an artifact close-combat weapon on demand, one weapon template per installation, functionally unable to be disarmed since the weapon is a physical extension of her own body.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Dexterity, (Caste Material) Synthesis Wave Emitter.
mechanics: Each installation provides one weapon template (Artifact rating capped at 3), which must be a simple magical version of a mundane close-combat weapon (daiklave, goremaul, and the like; shock pikes, fire lances, and artifacts with secondary magical functions unrelated to close combat are not permitted). Activating a weapon costs motes equal to its standard attunement cost; weapons are always formed of the Alchemical's Caste Material, granting its bonus. The weapon cannot be disarmed short of amputation, which instantly shatters it into raw Material fragments (so the Charm cannot be farmed for mass-produced artifacts); deactivating it is a reflexive action that folds it away, but the wielding hand can perform no other task while a weapon is grown. Separate installations let different hands (or Multi-Limb Frame appendages) each grow a different weapon simultaneously; limbs can only grow the weapons anchored to them, and changing the arrangement requires removing and reinstalling the Charm.
cost: Varies (equal to the grown weapon's attunement cost); Installation Cost: None.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Simple. Close Combat Charms tree (Dexterity-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, p. 98 (PDF 99); visually cross-checked against a rendered page image and the Close Combat Charms IV tree diagram.

name: Electrification Onslaught Dynamo
summary: Chest- or back-mounted conductor nodes that let an Alchemical deliver an electric shock through virtually any physical contact — an offensive strike bonus, a retaliatory counter-shock, a clinch jolt, or even a harmless-seeming handshake.
requirements: Minimum Strength 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory Augmentation of Strength.
mechanics: Activates as few or as many conductor nodes as desired for one of several uses: (1) after a successful hand-to-hand strike, deal an extra 1L or 2B per mote spent (up to Strength motes), soaked separately using only the victim's natural soak; (2) release the same jolt as a retaliatory counter whenever a foe successfully strikes the Alchemical with a metallic weapon or unarmed attack (even for zero damage), including via a parry using the blocking limb/weapon as conductor (which halves the Essence cap, rounded up); used this way the shock is a counterattack that cannot be evaded except by a perfect defense or answered with another counterattack; (3) release the jolt against an opponent immediately after winning a clinch roll, before she can break the hold; (4) deliver the shock through any casual or nonviolent contact, whether or not the Exalt initiated it, such as a handshake.
cost: Varies (1L or 2B per mote spent, up to Strength motes); Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Reflexive. Close Combat Charms tree (Strength-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Close Combat Charms' tree, p. 98 (PDF 99); visually cross-checked against the Close Combat Charms IV tree diagram.

name: Chemical Fog Generator
summary: A torso-mounted vent system that fills an area with obscuring, choking black smoke, upgradeable with four named toxic-gas submodules — knockout, tear, nerve, and soul gas — each with its own resistance roll and effect.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Fills a roughly spherical volume with a radius of (Essence) yards per mote spent (capped at Manipulation motes per turn); lingers 20 minutes indoors in still air (10 minutes with a mild breeze, 5 turns with a heavy breeze) or 5 minutes outdoors in still air (1 minute in a light breeze, 3 turns in heavy wind). Base smoke imposes murky-vision penalties out to 10 yards and total blindness beyond that (3-yard murky radius in dim light); anyone breathing it unprotected takes 1 unsoakable bashing level per minute (delayable by holding breath, or slowed to a 5-minute interval with a filter such as a wet scarf). Submodules (2 bonus points/6 xp each; only one may be deployed per use): Knockout Gas — mortals roll Stamina + Resistance (difficulty 2) or pass out for 30 minus (Stamina + Resistance) minutes; Exalted/superhuman beings resist at difficulty 1 with per-minute exposure checks; a filter provides full protection. Tear Gas — a poison-style exposure (difficulty 2, success no damage, failure 1B, duration/penalty one hour/-3) checked every turn until the victim passes out; a filter reduces the resistance difficulty by 1. Nerve Gas (requires Essence 3 to install) — uses the statistics of arrow frog venom, exposure checked every five minutes; mortals convulse and die in a number of turns equal to Stamina unless a Stamina + Resistance roll (difficulty 6) succeeds, otherwise suffering the Exalted failure effect (extras die automatically); a filter reduces the difficulty by 2.
