mechanics: The drone has Dexterity = Exalt's Dexterity + Essence; Perception and all Abilities equal the Exalt's own (opponents suffer +2 difficulty to hit it, and it fits through any inch-wide opening); Strength 1 (feats of strength capped at the Exalt's Essence regardless of Athletics); Stamina/soak(L/B)/health levels equal to the Exalt's Essence, losing 1 Perception dot per health level lost and dissolving if destroyed or if commitment is withdrawn (the socket regrows a replacement in a day); tentacle-leg attacks (speed +0, accuracy +0, damage 1L, defense -2; rate 3 under Exalted Power Combat); double the Exalt's running speed with insect-like surface adhesion; and a range cap of the Exalt's Essence in miles for control/transmission, auto-retreating toward the Exalt's last known position if blocked or out of range (the link counts as an arcane link, and anti-scrying wards block it). Multiple drones may be installed (installations beyond the first skip the installation cost and are mounted as inconspicuous rivets elsewhere on the body). Submodules (2 bonus points/6 experience points each): Autonomous (Intelligence 1 plus one Ability dot the Exalt has, acting independently, fleeing if attacked unless ordered otherwise); Communication (relays/transmits the Exalt's voice, audibly distorted); Hovering (flight at running speed instead of scuttling); Injection Needle (requires Multifunction Hypodermic Apparatus; delivers one stored drug dose via the drone's Dexterity + the Exalt's Medicine); Playback (records experiences to a memory crystal, downloaded on return to the socket); Stealth (gains Optical Shroud-equivalent concealment while motionless a full turn, lost on any movement unless passively anchored to a moving perch); Flesh-Burrowing (Essence 3+; a Dexterity + Medicine attack, difficulty 2, lets the drone burrow into a wounded target and ride its senses until it exits via the same attack or is surgically removed, difficulty 3, dealing 1L either way).
requirements: Minimum Perception 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Perception.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Simple. Sensory and Spiritual Charms tree (Perception-keyed); root of a Perception branch.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Sensory and Spiritual Charms' tree, pp. 125-127 (PDF 126-128); visually cross-checked against the Sensory and Spiritual Charms I tree diagram. This Charm completes the five-Charm Sensory and Spiritual Charms I sub-tree. The Injection Needle submodule forward-references Multifunction Hypodermic Apparatus (pp. 134-136/PDF 135-137), inventoried later in this same pass under Medical Charms.

name: Interpolative Situational Analysis Processor
summary: A cognitive-cluster implant that gathers and filters all of an Alchemical's sensory data into pertinent investigative details and speculative connections, functioning as a Storyteller-guided detective aid.
mechanics: Roll Wits + (Awareness or Investigation, whichever is higher) at standard difficulty. Each success reveals or recalls one detail most relevant to a single line of inquiry (including details from earlier scenes), which the Storyteller combines with speculative hints connecting them (e.g. reconstructing a murder scene's blood spatter, body position, and wound nature, plus an inference about the killer's skill and relationship to the victim). The Storyteller should offer a mix of plausible truths and red herrings without answering the question outright; if the true answer is wholly unexpected or actively concealed by misdirection, the Charm may produce false suppositions.
requirements: Minimum Wits 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Both Transitory and Sustained Augmentation of Wits.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Sensory and Spiritual Charms tree (Wits-keyed); root of the Wits branch.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Sensory and Spiritual Charms' tree, p. 128 (PDF 129); visually cross-checked against the Sensory and Spiritual Charms II tree diagram on p. 129.

name: Soulgem Detector
summary: A forehead-mounted stud wired to an Alchemical's own soulgem that detects every soulgem within range, distinguishing whether each holds a soul and whether it is set into a mortal, an Exalt, or no one, with more powerful long-range variants at higher Essence.
mechanics: Detects every soulgem within (Perception x 10) yards, automatically knowing whether a gem holds a soul and its implantation status, though only one gem's Essence pattern can be diceless-focused on at a time; a soulgem capped in lead becomes invisible to this Charm (a highly illegal procedure). A more powerful variant (Perception 3, Essence 5) extends range to (Perception x 100) yards, and a greater variant (Perception 6, Essence 8) extends it to (Perception) miles.
requirements: Minimum Perception 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Perception.
compatibility: Duration: One scene. Type: Simple. Sensory and Spiritual Charms tree (Perception-keyed); root of a Perception branch.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Sensory and Spiritual Charms' tree, pp. 128-129 (PDF 129-130); visually cross-checked against the Sensory and Spiritual Charms II tree diagram. The higher-Essence range variants are described as upgraded versions of the same Charm rather than separate purchases.

name: Cross-Phase Scanner
summary: Facial receptor nodules attuning an Alchemical's senses to immaterial energies, letting her perceive spirits and other incorporeal phenomena as if solid, one sense at a time.
mechanics: For every 2 motes spent, the Exalt may perceive spirits, sanctum entrances, and other incorporeal beings/effects as if they were solid, through one designated sense; such phenomena carry a faint but distinctive tone, color, or other tell that identifies them, and the Exalt never confuses immaterial for material or vice versa.
requirements: Minimum Perception 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Perception.
cost: 2 motes per sense; Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: One scene. Type: Simple. Sensory and Spiritual Charms tree (Perception-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Sensory and Spiritual Charms' tree, p. 129 (PDF 130); visually cross-checked against the Sensory and Spiritual Charms II tree diagram.

name: Transphase Engine
summary: A starmetal-sphere implant letting an Alchemical briefly dematerialize into a translucent phantom state in conjunction with an instant action such as an attack, dodge, parry, or Athletics maneuver.
mechanics: Activated for 4 motes alongside a dice action of instant duration: an attack (letting her strike a dematerialized being), a dodge (becoming a limited 'perfect' defense against a material attack that cannot affect dematerialized beings), a parry (only useful against immaterial beings), an Athletics maneuver (phasing through a door or floor), or another Storyteller-approved use. Integrated mass sensors prevent activation if the character would end the split-second phase still partway through a heavy obstruction (wall, floor, ceiling), so a running dash into a thick wall while relying on this Charm fails embarrassingly or painfully.
requirements: Minimum Wits 3; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Cross-Phase Scanner.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Supplemental. Sensory and Spiritual Charms tree (Wits-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Sensory and Spiritual Charms' tree, pp. 129-130 (PDF 130-131); visually cross-checked against the Sensory and Spiritual Charms II tree diagram.

name: God-Ward Projector
summary: A spine-mounted mechanism that emits an expanding, then-fixed spherical barrier of glowing Essence blocking spirit passage and most spirit Charms from crossing in either direction.
mechanics: Expands to a maximum radius of (Charisma x 5) yards before crystallizing invisibly (though translucent to dematerialized beings) and barring passage to any spirit regardless of power; it also blocks spirits outside from affecting anyone/anything inside with their Charms unless their permanent Essence exceeds the Alchemical's Charisma. Spirits already inside when it hardens may act and remain freely; leaving causes a tingling sensation and bars reentry. Materialized spirits (or any spirit possessing a host) cross freely. The ward persists fixed in place until the Alchemical dies or moves outside it, at which point it immediately collapses.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Cross-Phase Scanner.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Sensory and Spiritual Charms tree (Charisma-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Sensory and Spiritual Charms' tree, p. 130 (PDF 131); visually cross-checked against the Sensory and Spiritual Charms II tree diagram. This Charm completes the five-Charm Sensory and Spiritual Charms II sub-tree.

name: Sustenance Replication Engine
summary: A stomach-linked reactor and digestive recycler that lets an Alchemical divide her food requirement by her Essence (or eliminate it at Essence 5+ for an upkeep cost), and can also bleed out an edible nutrient paste for feeding mortals.
mechanics: The Exalt produces no waste and divides the food needed to stay healthy by her permanent Essence. Essence 5+ Alchemicals may forgo nourishment entirely, synthesizing nutrients directly from Essence for an uncommitted upkeep of 5 motes per day; failing to pay it (or failing to eat if not using that option) leads to ordinary starvation penalties. Secondary function: bleeding a bland, chalky but nutritionally complete gray paste from a forearm vein port, enough to feed one mortal one meal for 5 motes and one minute of bleeding; such meals contain negligible Essence and give Alchemicals no benefit.
requirements: Minimum Stamina 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Sustained Augmentation of Stamina.
cost: None, or 5 motes; Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: Permanent, or one minute. Type: Upgrade or Simple. Medical Charms tree (Stamina-keyed); root of the tree.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, p. 130 (PDF 131); visually cross-checked against the small standalone 'Medical Charms I' tree diagram on p. 131, which contains only Sustained Augmentation of Stamina and this Charm -- the remaining Medical Charms described nearby in extraction order actually belong to the larger 'Medical Charms II' diagram on p. 133, an extraction-order-vs-layout mismatch caught by the required visual page check.

name: Toxicity Filtration Subsystems
summary: A body-wide filtration network that gives an Alchemical automatic bonus successes against poison and expunges alcohol/drugs from her system, at the cost of never being able to get drunk or high even when desired.
mechanics: When activated by exposure to a toxin, the Exalt adds her Essence in automatic successes to Stamina rolls and soak against the poison, and expunges alcohol/recreational drugs from her body; if her player rolls more than double the successes needed to reduce a poisoning's severity, the chemical has no effect at all. The Charm activates itself automatically whenever exposed to a dangerous toxin (conscious characters may deliberately suppress it), which as a side effect prevents the Alchemical from ever becoming drunk or high without deliberate suppression.
requirements: Minimum Stamina 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Stamina.
compatibility: Duration: One hour. Type: Reflexive. Medical Charms tree (Stamina-keyed); root of a Stamina branch.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, pp. 130-131 (PDF 131-132); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram on p. 133.

name: Biofunction Inhibitor
summary: A control-valve implant letting an Alchemical enter deathlike regenerative torpor to rest far faster than sleep, accelerating both Essence recovery and Willpower recovery.
mechanics: Over about a minute, all biological processes and Charms slow to a stop until the Exalt appears dead (anyone who knows Alchemical biology recognizes this isn't true death since the body would otherwise dissolve; a trained medic can detect faint life signs with Perception + Medicine, difficulty 4). The Exalt must specify the intended torpor duration when activating and remains fully unaware of her surroundings, only waking early if something could have damaged her (regardless of whether damage is actually applied). Time in torpor is more restful than sleep by a factor of the Exalt's permanent Essence (e.g. an Essence 4 Alchemical compresses a full night's rest into two hours). Torpor also speeds Willpower recovery, but only one Conviction roll is allowed per 25-hour period, and Essence respiration during torpor is no faster than normal sleep.
requirements: Minimum Stamina 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Stamina.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Simple. Medical Charms tree (Stamina-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, pp. 130-131 (PDF 131-132); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram.

name: Restorative Fusion Transponder
summary: A spinal port letting an Alchemical, while resting on a natural Autochthonian surface, cocoon herself in Primordial cables and heal/recover Essence as if resting in a Vat Complex.
mechanics: Activating on a natural surface causes cables and Primordial capillaries to rise and cocoon the Exalt, culminating in a spike docking into the spinal port and rendering her unconscious while her body heals and regains Essence at Vat Complex rates; even starving characters can respire Essence and heal within a cocoon, albeit only at their usual rates. Cocoons have soak 10L/15B and 10 levels of durability before breaking (which wakes the Exalt); otherwise they remain until the Exalt voluntarily dismisses them (even while unconscious, she can track her recovery progress and order withdrawal), after which the ground seals without a trace.
requirements: Minimum Stamina 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Biofunction Inhibitor.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Medical Charms tree (Stamina-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, p. 131 (PDF 132); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram. Cross-references the Vat Complex rest rate to p. 68 (PDF 69), covered by the existing vats-background row.

name: Body-Reweaving Matrix
summary: Hidden colonies of thumbnail-sized spider-automata that swarm across an Alchemical's body to accelerate healing dramatically, regrowing amputated limbs, organs, and even destroyed Charms installed at the time of injury.
mechanics: While active, the Alchemical regenerates a number of bashing levels per turn equal to her permanent Essence; lethal damage heals at one level per turn; aggravated damage heals at one level per 10 hours. Amputated/destroyed organs heal as aggravated damage: whole limbs count as three levels, partial limbs (forearm+hand, or leg from the knee down) as two levels, and hands/eyes/a mouthful of teeth as one level. Any Charms located in an amputated area regrow too, but only those installed as of the time of injury; the amputated originals disintegrate as the Matrix replaces them.
requirements: Minimum Stamina 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Restorative Fusion Transponder.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Reflexive. Medical Charms tree (Stamina-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, pp. 131-132 (PDF 132-133); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram, which shows this Charm at the end of the Stamina branch.

name: Diagnostic Sensor Apparatus
summary: Fingertip sensors that scan a nearby living target's vital signs into an Alchemical's memory for later medical analysis, revealing progressively more diagnostic detail with more time spent interpreting the scan.
mechanics: Scanning costs 1 mote and a turn, targeting a living being within the Exalt's Essence in yards; results remain stored in memory as long as Essence is committed to remembering them. Interpreting the scan requires Intelligence + Medicine at standard difficulty, five minutes per roll, poolable as an extended action; a character knows everything at or below her rolled successes: one success (alive/dead, well or diseased/infected), two (number of ailments), three (physical location of all ailments), four (progression and names of known ailments, plus recovery variables like Stamina/Endurance/Resistance), five (full profiling including vectors, symptoms, and whether an ailment is magical). Once the character stops analyzing, the raw scan data and its Essence commitment fade, leaving only the diagnosis reached so far.
requirements: Minimum Perception 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Perception.
compatibility: Duration: Until analysis completed. Type: Simple. Medical Charms tree (Perception-keyed); root of the Perception branch.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, p. 132 (PDF 133); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram.

name: Biosight Reticle
summary: Diagnostic eye-lenses that render Essence-bearing beings visible through obstructions and darkness by their inner glow, can pierce many concealment Charms, and let the Alchemical read a detailed vital-signs profile of a studied target.
mechanics: Grants bonus dice equal to a hidden target's own permanent Essence to spot them with Perception rolls; negates visual penalties from darkness/fog/smoke/etc. for spotting or attacking animate targets, and can scan through a cumulative yard or more of solid matter before being blocked. Automatically dulls the Great Maker's ambient Essence glow in Autochthonia to background flicker (unfiltered in Creation, letting it reveal Demesnes, Manses, and dragon tracks). Can pierce concealment Charms of equal-or-lesser-Essence characters unless the magic specifically cloaks Essence emanations or relies on mental misdirection, via an opposed roll of (Perception + Awareness + the target's Essence) versus (the target's Dexterity + Stealth); winning spots the target, losing lets their Charm function normally. Once aware of a target, a simple action plus a Perception + Medicine roll reveals one piece of chosen vital information per success: current/maximum health levels, current wound/fatigue penalties, permanent Essence, current Essence pool, Stamina/Endurance/Resistance ratings, injury locations, pregnancy, parasites, disease, or infected-wound locations; further turns of scanning can reveal more (a botch always yields erroneous results).
requirements: Minimum Perception 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Diagnostic Sensor Apparatus.
compatibility: Duration: One hour. Type: Simple. Medical Charms tree (Perception-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, pp. 132-134 (PDF 133-135); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram.

name: Biostasis Field Projector
summary: A palm-mounted capacitor that induces a coma-like stasis in a touched patient, halting bleeding/infection/poison progression, and can be used reflexively on the Alchemical herself to survive damage that would otherwise be lethal.
mechanics: Touch-activated (3 motes); the patient convulses and falls into an apparently-dead stasis detectable as alive only via Perception + Medicine (difficulty 4) or diagnostic magic/Essence sight. Requires several seconds of contact, so it cannot be paired with an unarmed strike to incapacitate an unwilling target, but may substitute for damage after winning control of a clinch; an unwilling patient may resist with Stamina + Resistance (difficulty = the Exalt's Essence). While stabilized, infections/poisons halt spreading, bleeding stops, and mortally wounded patients do not deteriorate past Incapacitated; stasis lasts a day (or until Essence commitment is withdrawn) and is renewable, with 'unfreezing' returning the patient to their exact condition at administration (any new injuries in the interim remain). Used for battlefield first aid, surgical anesthesia, and prisoner transport. Alchemicals may use it on themselves for any specified duration but remain helplessly unconscious until it runs its course; they may also activate it reflexively (3 motes and a recoverable dot of Stamina) when lethal damage would drop them below Incapacitated, entering a deathlike coma of at least one hour instead of dying, with further lethal damage ignorable via reapplication until Stamina drops to 1 or Essence runs out.
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Biofunction Inhibitor, Diagnostic Sensor Apparatus.
compatibility: Duration: One day or indefinite. Type: Simple or Reflexive. Medical Charms tree (Intelligence-keyed); a joint Stamina/Perception/Intelligence branch link.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, pp. 133-134 (PDF 134-135); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram, where this Charm bridges both the Biofunction Inhibitor (Stamina) and Diagnostic Sensor Apparatus (Perception) branches under an Intelligence-adjacent node.

name: Multifunction Hypodermic Apparatus
summary: A retractable torso-mounted needle-tendril that injects synthesized drugs from internal storage, starting with any two of a large catalog of formulas (Paralytic Toxin, Lethal Toxin, Acid, Antivenin, Anesthetic, Immune Booster, Antiseptic, Healing Agent, Coagulant, Hallucinogen, Stimulant, Time Release Drug, Memory Eraser, Triggered Activation Drug), with more purchasable individually.
mechanics: The tendril extends up to two yards to target veins/vital clusters; injecting an unwilling patient requires a Dexterity + Medicine attack roll (against soft targets a hit injects with no damage; against hard targets it deals piercing '1L + successes' damage but records no actual injury, only delivering the drug), while willing patients need no roll and self-injection is allowed. Harmful drugs allow the patient a reflexive Stamina + Resistance roll (difficulty = the Exalt's Essence) unless a special formula states otherwise; beneficial drugs normally bypass this resistance. Installation grants any two starting formulas; each additional costs 4 experience points/2 bonus points (or the Exalt may design new formulas of comparable power via Intelligence + (Medicine or Lore), difficulty 3, with Storyteller approval, for the same 4-experience-point cost). Formula summary: Paralytic/Lethal Toxin (bashing or lethal damage plus an action-die penalty scaled by Intelligence/Essence, reduced on a successful resistance roll; Stamina-exceeds-Intelligence targets are immune); Acid (flat 6L unsoakable-but-for-natural-soak damage, no resistance roll, permanently scarring Appearance -1 on 3+ damage); Antivenin (cures one active poison per dose, cleanses alcohol/drugs, can be pre-administered to intercept one future poison, and can neutralize an inert time-release/triggered dose but not memory eraser); Anesthetic (subtracts Essence from wound penalties, fading at one die/hour, resettable rather than stacking on reinjection); Immune Booster (+1 die vs. disease for Intelligence-many days); Antiseptic (prevents/nullifies wound infection); Healing Agent (heals 2 bashing levels after an hour of rest); Coagulant (instantly stops bleeding); Hallucinogen (synesthesia/pleasure with an Intelligence+Essence action penalty on failure, addictive per a monthly Temperance roll, difficulty 2, decaying an hour at a time; a lesser non-addictive version on success); Stimulant (reduces fatigue penalty by Essence for Intelligence-many hours, but repeated doses without rest inflict 2 unsoakable bashing levels each); Time Release Drug (delays any other injected drug's onset to a specified time, cleansable in advance by Antivenin); Memory Eraser (Essence 3+, 6 xp/3 bp; erases the past hour/scene on a failed Wits-based resistance, or scrambles recent memory recoverable turn-by-turn on success; cannot be a starting formula); Triggered Activation Drug (Essence 3+, 6 xp/3 bp; delays any injected drug's activation for up to a month via 1 additional committed mote until the Exalt disarms or triggers it; cannot be a starting formula).
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Intelligence, Diagnostic Sensor Apparatus.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Medical Charms tree (Intelligence-keyed); root of the Intelligence branch.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, pp. 134-136 (PDF 135-137); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram. The 14-formula drug catalog is summarized rather than reproduced verbatim, matching how this inventory summarizes other large submodule catalogs (e.g. Essence Pulse Cannon, Optical Enhancement). Flagged for a future re-verification pass on exact resistance-roll wording per formula given the length and density of this write-up.

name: Regenerative Essence Transfusion
summary: A Multifunction Hypodermic Apparatus upgrade that either injects mortals with an Exalt-grade healing drug or lets the Alchemical directly transfer Essence to (or drain it from) a patient through the same needle.
mechanics: Healing mode (10 motes, indefinite): injects a glowing healing fluid (using the Apparatus's injection rules) that lets mortal patients heal and resist poison/disease as if they were Exalted for as long as the Exalt commits 10 motes; it cannot speed up beings that already regenerate at Exalt speed or better. Transfer mode: after a successful injection, spend 3 motes to activate a transfer and then donate up to (Stamina + Essence) motes from her own pool to the patient, visibly flowing through the tendril; alternately she may siphon Essence as an attack for 2 motes, rolling Intelligence + Medicine (difficulty 1 if willing, or the target's Essence if unwilling), draining 2 motes into her own pool per success (draining Peripheral before Personal from Exalted victims).
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Biostasis Field Projector, Multifunction Hypodermic Apparatus.
cost: 10 motes, or varies; Installation Cost: None.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite or instant. Type: Simple. Medical Charms tree (Intelligence-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, p. 136 (PDF 137); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram.

name: Metabolic Augmentation Injection
summary: A Multifunction Hypodermic Apparatus upgrade that injects a highly addictive drug temporarily boosting a living patient's Physical Attributes, Appearance, Perception, Wits, and select Abilities, with prolonged use able to mutate the gains into permanent Traits.
mechanics: Uses the Apparatus's injection rules (no resistance roll possible). For every 3 motes spent, raises one of the patient's Physical Attributes, Appearance, Perception, or Wits by one dot (extra Stamina also reduces wound penalties and grants Exalt-style soak/healing); for 1 mote per dot, raises Athletics, Awareness, Endurance, or Resistance. No Trait may be raised by more dots than (the Exalt's Essence minus the patient's permanent Essence), no Attribute may exceed double its original rating, and no Ability may exceed 5 dots after augmentation. Bonuses last as long as Essence is committed; patients carrying the drug a week or more may 'mutate,' letting players later pay experience points to make an augmented rating permanent up to its normal maximum or the augmented value, bypassing training time (Storytellers may instead require future-experience credit). Alchemicals themselves never mutate from carrying the drug, though other Exalted may. The drug is highly addictive to mortals: given a chance to reinject within a month, a mortal's player must roll Temperance (difficulty 2), doing anything short of endangering himself/loved ones on a failure, or anything at all on a botch.
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Biostasis Field Projector, Multifunction Hypodermic Apparatus.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Simple. Medical Charms tree (Intelligence-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Medical Charms' tree, pp. 136-137 (PDF 137-138); visually cross-checked against the Medical Charms II tree diagram. This Charm completes the Medical Charms tree (11 Charms total across the small Medical Charms I diagram and the larger Medical Charms II diagram).

name: Imprinted Data Cluster
summary: Adamant memory-crystal brain implants that let an Alchemical download Ability specialties from a Vats Complex database one mote at a time, storing as many different specialties as desired at the cost of continuous Essence commitment.
mechanics: For every mote spent (only while resting in a Vats Complex), the character downloads one Ability specialty from the facility's databases. Downloaded specialties count as natural specialties for dice-boosting-limit purposes (max three copies of the same specialty per Ability, max three natural specialty dice per roll), but unlike experience-bought specialties they vanish immediately and irrevocably if the Exalt ever withdraws the committed mote, requiring a fresh Vats download to reacquire. A character may store as many distinct specialties as desired simultaneously. Players may spend 3 experience points as an instantaneous reflexive action to release a downloaded specialty's Essence commitment and make it permanent.
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Sustained Augmentation of Intelligence.
cost: 1 mote per dot (specialty); Installation Cost: 2 motes.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Reflexive. Cognitive Charms tree (Intelligence-keyed); root of the tree.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Cognitive Charms' tree, pp. 137-138 (PDF 138-139); visually cross-checked against the Cognitive Charms tree diagram on p. 137.

name: Clarified Data Assimilator
summary: A swarm of microscopic automata woven through an Alchemical's nervous system that substitutes her total Clarity rating for any single Ability's rating on one roll, at an escalating mote cost and a cumulative Clarity toll for repeated use.
mechanics: Each activation replaces the rating of any single chosen Ability with the Exalt's total Clarity for the purposes of one roll (pertinent specialties for the replaced Ability still apply); the base cost is 3 motes, but each subsequent activation adds a cumulative mote to the cost, decreasing by 1 mote for every full day since the character last used the Charm. Characters may not channel a Virtue to aid a roll boosted by this Charm. Installing it grants 1 dot of permanent Clarity, and each use adds 1 point of temporary Clarity.
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Intelligence.
cost: 3 motes (rising cumulatively with repeated same-day use); Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Supplemental. Cognitive Charms tree (Intelligence-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Cognitive Charms' tree, p. 138 (PDF 139); visually cross-checked against the Cognitive Charms tree diagram.

name: Abstract Abacus Implant
summary: Artificial synapse webs that let an Alchemical reduce the difficulty of (and add automatic successes to) logic-based Mental Attribute rolls, act as a perfect free mental clock, and, via a submodule, rapidly learn spoken/written languages.
mechanics: For every 2 motes spent, reduce the difficulty of a logic/deduction-based Mental Attribute roll (math, navigation/cartography, solving enigmas, etc.) by 1; once difficulty hits 1, further 2-mote increments instead add automatic successes, capped at the Exalt's permanent Essence. Also functions as a free, costless perfect mental clock/timer. Interpolative Syntax Emulator submodule (2 bonus points/4 experience points, Essence 3+): after an hour studying a text or listening to an unfamiliar language (or a turn studying a Mind-Ripping Probe victim's linguistic knowledge), the Exalt may spend 3 motes and 3 experience points (or 1 experience point for a tribal language) to instantly learn that tongue, without raising her Linguistics rating or needing separate expenditure for the written vs. spoken form.
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Intelligence.
cost: 2 motes per success/difficulty point; Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Supplemental. Cognitive Charms tree (Intelligence-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Cognitive Charms' tree, pp. 138-139 (PDF 139-140); visually cross-checked against the Cognitive Charms tree diagram.

name: Technological Analysis Engrams
summary: A metallic brain sub-lobe giving an Alchemical an intuitive engineering database, letting her study any machine or artifact for a turn to learn its function, condition, and (with enough successes) repair/sabotage bonuses.
mechanics: Requires only visual scrutiny for devices with visible components, or a turn of handling/running hands over hidden-mechanism devices. Roll Perception + Lore at the end of the turn: difficulty 1-2 for non-magical devices (2 for the most complex/strange), or the item's artifact rating for artifacts (difficulty 6 for N/A-rated artifacts). One success gives a general functional understanding; two also reveal damage/maintenance needs and degree; three give a precise understanding of all capabilities and condition details. A failure gives nothing; a botch gives Storyteller-supplied erroneous details. Repeated study of the same object doesn't stack results. Two or more successes bank one automatic success toward the character's next repair roll on that item that scene, or (alternative use) double the raw damage of her next attack meant to destroy it; only one such banked bonus can be held at a time regardless of reuse.
requirements: Minimum Perception 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Perception, Abstract Abacus Implant.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Cognitive Charms tree (Perception-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Cognitive Charms' tree, pp. 138-139 (PDF 139-140); visually cross-checked against the Cognitive Charms tree diagram.

name: Omnitool Implant
summary: A hand implant letting an Alchemical extrude any simple tool she has the relevant dotted Ability to use, from screwdrivers to welding torches, for narrative and constructive (not combat) purposes.
mechanics: Fingers unfold into tools, or a wrist-mounted stalk extends one if all fingers are occupied; the Exalt can generate any tool needed for an Ability she has at least one dot in (e.g. Craft (Culinary) cutlery, Craft (Locksmithing) lockpicks). One activation supplies as many exchangeable tools as needed for the rest of the scene; the Storyteller vetoes abuse. Tools are high quality, adding one specialty-style die to any roll using them. Blunt/sharp tools can serve as crude improvised weapons (-1 accuracy from normal) but this is the Charm's combat ceiling; interrogators can misuse tools given time and a restrained victim, but this has no bearing on combat. Purely cosmetic, no-real-benefit uses (lighting a pipe, buffing nails) may be allowed by the Storyteller for free.
requirements: Minimum Wits 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Wits.
compatibility: Duration: One hour. Type: Simple. Cognitive Charms tree (Wits-keyed); root of the Wits branch.
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Cognitive Charms' tree, p. 139 (PDF 140); visually cross-checked against the Cognitive Charms tree diagram.

name: Synaptic Acceleration Node
summary: Nervous-system relay crystals that multiply an Alchemical's mental processing speed by her permanent Essence for a paid number of hours, useful for planning agendas or drafting blueprints.
mechanics: For a number of hours equal to motes spent (2 motes per hour), the Exalt's cognition rate multiplies by her permanent Essence: divide the time required for Mental Attribute-based actions (or the interval between rolls in extended actions) by her Essence. For quick mental tasks of a turn or less, she may perform up to her Wits rating of them per turn, with the usual multiple-action penalty reduced by her permanent Essence.
requirements: Minimum Wits 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Wits.
cost: 2 motes per hour; Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: Varies. Type: Reflexive. Cognitive Charms tree (Wits-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Cognitive Charms' tree, p. 139 (PDF 140); visually cross-checked against the Cognitive Charms tree diagram.

name: Incomparable Efficiency Upgrade
summary: A Synaptic Acceleration Node upgrade letting an Alchemical multiply the speed at which she performs a declared, predominantly physical extended task (e.g. digging a ditch, crafting an artifact) by her permanent Essence, though it cannot speed up learning.
mechanics: On activation, the player declares a non-combat extended action lasting more than a turn; while the Exalt commits the required Essence and works without interruptions longer than five cumulative minutes per hour, her working speed on that task multiplies by her permanent Essence. It cannot shorten Ability training or Trait advancement time (speed-reading a manual teaches the content but not practiced skill). The character's movements become clipped and mechanical while under the effect. The Storyteller is the final arbiter of which tasks qualify.
requirements: Minimum Wits 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Synaptic Acceleration Node.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Simple. Cognitive Charms tree (Wits-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Cognitive Charms' tree, pp. 139-140 (PDF 140-141); visually cross-checked against the Cognitive Charms tree diagram.

name: Logic Engineering Lobe
summary: A planning Charm letting an Alchemical precompute a declared future action, reducing its eventual difficulty at 3 motes per point, provided she actually follows through with the plan on the next turn.
mechanics: The player declares an action the Exalt intends to take next turn; the Storyteller states the most likely difficulty given known information. For every 3 motes spent, the final difficulty drops by 1 (usable once per turn). If the character deviates from the declared plan on the following turn, the spent Essence is wasted; if she follows through, the difficulty decreases as purchased (spending more than needed to hit difficulty 1 wastes the excess). Storytellers are encouraged to award stunt dice for players who declare intentions aloud to incredulous opponents in play.
requirements: Minimum Wits 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Abstract Abacus Implant, Synaptic Acceleration Node.
cost: 3 motes per difficulty point; Installation Cost: 1 mote.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Reflexive. Cognitive Charms tree (Wits-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Cognitive Charms' tree, p. 140 (PDF 141); visually cross-checked against the Cognitive Charms tree diagram.

name: Eidetic Processing Core
summary: A permanent brain implant of memory-indexing microscopic automata granting an Alchemical perfect recall of anything experienced since installation, and resistance to memory tampering.
mechanics: The Exalt perfectly remembers anything experienced while the Charm was installed with no roll required. Recalling pre-installation memories requires a reflexive Wits + Awareness roll (difficulty 1, once per turn per specific memory); failure means the automata have trouble locating an imperfectly filed memory, while a botch relocates it into an inaccessible synaptic cluster for the rest of the scene. Against memory-tampering or memory-erasing effects, an opposed roll of the Alchemical's Wits + Awareness versus the aggressor's Manipulation + Performance decides whether the Eidetic Processing Core sees through the change (Alchemical wins) or is fooled, reporting erasures as blank patches and false memories as real (aggressor wins).
requirements: Minimum Wits 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of Wits.
compatibility: Duration: N/A. Type: Permanent. Cognitive Charms tree (Wits-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Cognitive Charms' tree, pp. 140-141 (PDF 141-142); visually cross-checked against the Cognitive Charms tree diagram. This Charm completes the nine-Charm Cognitive Charms tree.

name: Auxiliary Essence Storage Unit
summary: A permanent Charm that expands an Alchemical's Peripheral Essence reservoir by 10 motes per installation, capped by permanent Essence (or Essence x 5 at Essence 8+), and barred from Arrays.
mechanics: Each installation adds 10 additional motes of Peripheral Essence capacity. Exalted cannot install more copies than their permanent Essence (or permanent Essence x 5 for Alchemicals of Essence 8+). This Charm can never be placed in an Array.
requirements: Minimum Stamina 1; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
compatibility: Duration: N/A. Type: Permanent. Essence and Weaving Charms tree; root of the tree (not Attribute-keyed).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Essence and Weaving Charms' tree (the chapter's final Charm tree), p. 141 (PDF 142); visually cross-checked against the Essence and Weaving Charms tree diagram.

name: Man-Machine Weaving Engine
summary: An adamant ring implanted around an Alchemical's soulgem that lets her initiate a single Man-Machine protocol of Alchemical weaving she has separately learned, at the cost of a permanent dot of Clarity and never being removable or Array-eligible.
mechanics: Activating for 1 Willpower spins the ring and lights runes; the character then spends the required Essence to initiate a single known Man-Machine weaving protocol, taking effect after a shaping period comparable to Emerald Circle Sorcery, with a bright soulgem flash marking the effect. Installing this Charm grants 1 dot of permanent Clarity; it can never be removed and can never be placed in an Array. The full catalog of Man-Machine protocols and their effects is explicitly cross-referenced in-book to pp. 145-159 (PDF 146-160), which falls in Chapter Four (Miracles of the Machine God), not this chapter.
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 4; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: None.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Essence and Weaving Charms tree; root of the tree (Intelligence-keyed, but not gated behind an Augmentation-of-Attribute prerequisite).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Essence and Weaving Charms' tree, p. 141 (PDF 142); visually cross-checked against the Essence and Weaving Charms tree diagram. The weaving-protocol catalog itself remains out of scope for this pass; see the README's 'What's still needed' list.

name: God-Machine Weaving Engine
summary: A larger concentric adamant ring surrounding the Man-Machine Weaving Engine, letting an Alchemical initiate a far more powerful God-Machine weaving protocol over two turns of shaping, again at the cost of a permanent dot of Clarity and non-removability.
mechanics: Activating for 2 Willpower spins both rings in opposite directions with a storm of sparks; the character designates a single known God-Machine protocol and spends its Essence cost, and after two turns of shaping (comparable to Sapphire Circle Sorcery) the protocol takes effect with a display rivaling the noonday sun. Installing this Charm grants 1 dot of permanent Clarity; it can never be removed and can never be placed in an Array. As with the Man-Machine Weaving Engine, the full catalog of God-Machine protocols is cross-referenced in-book to pp. 145-159 (PDF 146-160) in Chapter Four, not this chapter.
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 6; Minimum Essence 5; Prerequisite Charms: Auxiliary Essence Storage Unit, Man-Machine Weaving Engine.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Essence and Weaving Charms tree (Intelligence-keyed, but not gated behind an Augmentation-of-Attribute prerequisite).
notes: Chapter Three: Charms, 'Essence and Weaving Charms' tree, p. 141 (PDF 142); visually cross-checked against the Essence and Weaving Charms tree diagram. This Charm completes both the three-Charm Essence and Weaving Charms tree and the entirety of Chapter Three (pp. 87-141/PDF 88-142); Chapter Four begins at printed p. 142 (PDF 143), confirmed via direct extraction of that page's near-empty title-page text.

name: Alchemical Protocols (weaving-protocol framing)
summary: The framing text for Chapter Four's magic system: Autochthon gifted the Alchemical Exalted the power to issue command-prayers ('protocols') to the design weavers/pattern spiders that weave reality's fabric, giving Alchemicals a form of sorcery distinct from Creation's, split into the common Man-Machine Protocols and the rarer, more potent God-Machine Protocols.
mechanics: Alchemical protocol weaving is installed via protocol Charms (the Man-Machine Weaving Engine and God-Machine Weaving Engine) and functions in both Autochthonia and Creation, because Autochthon built a permanent back door into the pattern spiders' programming; only destroying or isolating the pattern spiders from the Loom of Fate could ever remove that access. Sidereal Exalted have no comparable authority over Autochthonia and cannot use astrology, Charms limited by Sidereal rules, or prayer strips to affect it or its native denizens, who count as beyond fate for that purpose. Protocols are organized into Man-Machine Protocols (roughly on par with Terrestrial Circle Sorcery, coverable in principle by sufficiently skilled mortal engineers given time and tools) and God-Machine Protocols (effects wholly beyond mortal capacity, generally fusing high technology with transcendent spirituality). Reweaving a pattern directly (to affect beings outside fate, such as Deathlords or Yozis) doubles a protocol's Essence cost; targeting the Exalt or an area is normally more efficient. Enlightened Mountain Folk who buy and surgically implant the relevant Charms (at double the normal cost) can also weave Alchemical protocols.
compatibility: Alchemical Exalted (via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine and God-Machine Weaving Engine Charms); Mountain Folk with surgically implanted copies of those Charms at double cost.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Alchemical Protocols' intro, pp. 145-146 (PDF 146-147); visually cross-checked, plain single-column prose with no layout hazards. Introduces the two protocol echelons inventoried in the rows that follow.

name: What Works Where (cross-cosmology magic compatibility sidebar)
summary: A boxed sidebar summarizing which of Exalted's several magic systems function in which cosmological venues (Creation, Autochthonia, the Underworld, Malfeas, the Wyld), most relevant to Alchemicals for confirming that their weaving works everywhere but is hampered in the Wyld and against beings outside fate.
mechanics: Sorcery and necromancy are Primordial-hardwired and work everywhere. Alchemical weaving also works everywhere, but affecting beings outside fate is harder (see the doubled-cost rule in the protocols overview), and weaving in the Wyld is difficult and usually doesn't work, though one specific protocol (Transcendent Pattern-Weaving Protocol) works only in the Wyld and alerts every nearby Fair Folk to the weaver's presence. Sidereal astrology works everywhere but cannot target anyone or anything originating in Autochthonia, the Underworld, or Malfeas, all of which count as beyond fate for that purpose; Sidereal prayers likewise never affect Autochthonia or its denizens. Sidereal Charms still function, but are subject to the limits described on p. 129 of Exalted: The Sidereals. Prayer strips, powered by sutras composed on Creation's Loom of Fate, only affect beings originating in Creation.
compatibility: Cross-splat setting reference; most relevant to Alchemicals confirming their protocols work in Creation and the Wyld caveat for Transcendent Pattern-Weaving Protocol.
notes: Chapter Four, 'What Works Where' sidebar, p. 146 (PDF 147); visually cross-checked against the rendered page (a plain right-column sidebar box, no reordering issues).

name: Man-Machine Protocols (framing)
summary: The section header text introducing Man-Machine Protocols as the most common echelon of Alchemical weaving, roughly comparable in power to Terrestrial Circle Sorcery, and explaining the universal activation cost and Clarity gating shared by the Man-Machine protocols catalogued below.
mechanics: Weaving a Man-Machine Protocol requires the weaver to spend 1 point of Willpower to make initial contact with the design weavers, in addition to each protocol's own Essence cost. Most Man-Machine Protocols also carry a Minimum Clarity requirement, representing the lowest degree of communion with the design weavers the Alchemical must have attained for them to process her protocol; a weaver below a protocol's Minimum Clarity cannot weave it at all.
requirements: Minimum Clarity varies per protocol (listed on each protocol's own entry).
cost: 1 Willpower per weaving, plus the protocol's own Essence cost.
compatibility: Alchemical Exalted (and surgically-implanted Mountain Folk) via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four, 'Man-Machine Protocols' section header and framing paragraph, p. 147 (PDF 148); visually cross-checked, ordinary two-column layout with no reordering hazards.

name: Spells That Crossed Over (sidebar)
summary: A boxed sidebar explaining why several Alchemical protocols are identical or near-identical to Creation sorcery spells: both trace back to Primordial-taught magic, and protocols that began with a technological focus or spirits native to Autochthonia survived the transition into the modern weaving-protocol catalog largely unchanged.
mechanics: Sorcery spells cannot simply be translated into Alchemical protocols wholesale; only the specific spells that could be translated have been (these are flagged by individual protocol entries below that cite an equivalent Exalted, Savant & Sorcerer spell). Writing an entirely new protocol is otherwise identical to the process of designing a new sorcery spell (see Exalted core, p. 217), with the constraint that its effects must fit the kind of techno-spiritual results the design weavers are accustomed to generating.
compatibility: Reference/setting note for any Alchemical protocol-designer or Storyteller adjudicating new protocols.
notes: Chapter Four, 'Spells That Crossed Over' sidebar, p. 148 (PDF 149). IMPORTANT EXTRACTION-ORDER NOTE: on this page, PyMuPDF's default text order placed this sidebar's content and the following Driving the Shadow Machine protocol out of the print layout's true reading order (the sidebar box interrupts the two-column flow); the correct order, confirmed by rendering the page to an image, is: this sidebar (left column top) -> Driving the Shadow Machine (left column, continuing into the right column) -> Elsewhere-Evoking Asana (right column). All affected rows below use this visually-confirmed order and page attribution rather than the raw extraction order.

name: God-Machine Protocols (framing)
summary: The section header text introducing God-Machine Protocols as the rarer, far more powerful echelon of Alchemical weaving, belonging solely to Autochthon and his most favored children, advancing the blend of mysticism, technology, and pattern manipulation well beyond what Man-Machine Protocols can achieve.
mechanics: No single universal activation cost or Clarity floor is stated for the God-Machine echelon as a whole (unlike Man-Machine Protocols' universal 1-Willpower/design-weaver-contact rule); each God-Machine Protocol lists its own Essence cost and Minimum Clarity individually, and several of the most potent examples carry Minimum Clarity requirements of 6 or higher.
compatibility: Alchemical Exalted (and surgically-implanted Mountain Folk) via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four, 'God-Machine Protocols' section header and framing paragraph, p. 156 (PDF 157); visually cross-checked, ordinary two-column layout with no reordering hazards.

name: Automaton Override Protocol
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that lets an Alchemical seize remote control of golems, zombies, and other automata (and low-Essence spirit machines), overriding any prior programming or summoner and directing the targets to act on the weaver's behalf instead.
mechanics: The weaver focuses her Essence and speaks a command phrase; a whorl of bright-green arcane symbols flows from her mouth or soulgem into the target automaton, suspending its prior commands. For 5 motes she takes control of one automaton; for 15 motes she may take control of (Essence x 2) automata or technological devices within a 10-yard radius. The protocol can affect golems, zombies, ordinary automata, and items of advanced technology (First Age ships, skyships, weapons), plus spirit machines/mechanical wildlife (such as custodians) whose Essence rating is 2 or less; it has no effect on natural creatures, elementals, or machine spirits of Essence 3 or higher. It can be countered by Emerald Countermagic, by Essence Draining Defense, or by any Alchemical with permanent Essence exceeding the weaver's by 2 or more. Only the invoking Alchemical has override authority; if a higher-Essence Exalt originally summoned the target, the two make a contested Willpower roll to determine who keeps control, with control-wresting potentially stranding a rider inside the automaton if it was a piloted vehicle such as a summoned warstrider.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 3.
cost: 1 Willpower (per the Man-Machine Protocols framing) plus 5 or 15 motes.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 147 (PDF 148); visually cross-checked, ordinary two-column layout.

name: Binding Filament System
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol (also known by the alternate name Her Glistening Silvery Strands) that instantly wraps a target in extraordinarily tough silvery metallic filament, restraining them indefinitely unless they tear free at a painful cost.
mechanics: On completion, the target is wrapped in fine strands of silvery filament. A very strong individual can attempt to break free as a feat of strength requiring a Strength + Athletics total of 10, but doing so causes the strands to act as garrotes, inflicting lethal damage equal to the weaver's Essence (soakable) on the escapee.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 147 (PDF 148); visually cross-checked. Duration is listed as Indefinite in the book (until escaped or otherwise ended); target is a single person.

name: Crystal Lotus of Repose
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that traps a target in a crystalline, lotus-flower-shaped protective containment; the book states it is otherwise identical to the Terrestrial Circle sorcery spell Sleep of Stony Safety.
mechanics: Except for its crystal, lotus-flower-shaped containment (rather than stone), this protocol's effect is identical to the sorcery spell Sleep of Stony Safety (Savant & Sorcerer, p. 117) - an external supplement outside this inventory's scope.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 2.
cost: 1 Willpower (cost/target/duration otherwise as Sleep of Stony Safety, not independently restated here).
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 147 (PDF 148); visually cross-checked. Full mechanics defer to Sleep of Stony Safety in Savant & Sorcerer, a supplement not held/inventoried in this repository; flagged rather than guessed at its exact cost/target/duration.

name: Docility Assurance Field
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that binds a target in a mesh of luminous filaments which does not impede movement but inflicts damage on the target every time they spend Essence, for the duration of a scene or hour.
mechanics: The target is bound in a shifting mesh of light that in no way impairs mobility, but any time the target spends Essence, they take damage: the weaver chooses at the time of weaving either one bashing health level per mote spent or one lethal health level per 2 motes spent (a single mote spent alone causes no damage under the lethal option). This damage can only be soaked with the target's Essence rating. The field does not interfere with non-Essence activities or with Essence already committed before the field was woven. This protocol cannot target a being of greater Essence than the weaver.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 147 (PDF 148); visually cross-checked. Duration: one scene or one hour, whichever is longer.

name: Driving the Shadow Machine
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that conjures a silent, perfectly camouflaging flying vehicle of roiling shadow (a 'tenebrapede') that the weaver and companions can ride at high speed, well-protected from attacks and the elements.
mechanics: The protocol brings into being an incorporeal, Essence-and-light-feeding pocket of shadow that can carry 200 pounds of cargo/passengers per point of the weaver's permanent Essence. It is perfectly silent, goes wherever the Alchemical wills, offers a fully clear 180-degree view from within (while appearing as darkness from outside), and flies at 200 mph (nearly 600 yards/turn). It has 25 health levels and a soak of 25L/35B, provides 90% hard cover to riders, and only a single attack can be made against it or its occupants per turn unless the attacker matches its flight speed; attacking out from it is similarly restricted. It protects occupants/cargo from all but the most extreme climates. If its travel time elapses before reaching the destination, it lands at the nearest city or safe area and gives one minute to unload before fading; otherwise it persists until reaching its destination, being landed early, or being dispelled.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 2.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 148 (PDF 149). Duration: (weaver's Essence x 4) hours. Reading order confirmed by rendered-page comparison: this protocol's header and opening text sit in the left column below the 'Spells That Crossed Over' sidebar, continuing into the top of the right column before Elsewhere-Evoking Asana begins; raw text extraction alone would have suggested a different order.

name: Elsewhere-Evoking Asana
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol requiring a seated meditative posture that manifests a sphere of the great Void surrounding the weaver: an airless, gravity-free, fire-snuffing, extremely cold defensive field that also serves as a form of spiritual communion with Autochthon's exile.
mechanics: While maintained, the weaver is surrounded by a sphere of cold, airless void with radius (Essence x 5) feet. All fire is snuffed, air-breathers inside suffocate, visibility is as heavy snow at night, and damage from the cold equals standing in a bonfire. There is no up or down inside the field; characters need three or more successes on a Dexterity + Athletics roll to propel themselves through it, and once moving they float until they exit (then fall) or fail to muster enough coordination to move at all. Objects/attacks entering the sphere lose all momentum instantly. The weaver, maintaining the posture, floats at the center immune to all the field's effects except the visibility penalty, and regains Essence as though meditating. Ending the posture ends the protocol instantly.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 5.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, pp. 148-149 (PDF 149-150). Duration: the longer of one hour or one scene; Target: area of effect. DATA-QUALITY FLAG: the header on p. 148 names this protocol 'Elsewhere-Evoking Asana,' but the closing paragraph on p. 149 refers to it once as 'Elsewhere-Evoking Prana' - an apparent in-book inconsistency/typo between the two names for the same protocol, not a separate effect. Recorded here under the header name.

name: Entropy Manipulation Protocol
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol favored by Alchemicals venturing into the gremlin-infested Far Reaches: it temporarily knocks all nearby automata offline, dealing damage and forcing them inert for the rest of the scene.
mechanics: All gremlins, golems, zombies, and other automata within (Essence x 10) yards take the weaver's Essence in bashing damage and fall inert; at the start of the next scene they resume functioning, though they may be confused about their situation and may not necessarily resume their prior task. The protocol does not shut down warstriders or other powered armor outright, but deadens unshielded limbs: it imposes a -2 mobility penalty on Artifact ••• armor, reduced by 1 for each additional Artifact dot, so Artifact ••••• armor is unaffected.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 4.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 149 (PDF 150); visually cross-checked, ordinary two-column layout continuing directly from Elsewhere-Evoking Asana. Duration: one scene; Target: all automata within range.

name: Essence Reallocation Protocol
summary: A reflexive Man-Machine Protocol, functionally an Alchemical counterpart to Emerald Countermagic, that counters an incoming Terrestrial Circle Sorcery spell, Man-Machine Protocol, or Shadowlands Circle Necromancy effect and siphons the cancelled effect's Essence into the weaver's own reservoir.
mechanics: As a reflexive protocol, it counters a single incoming Terrestrial Circle Sorcery spell, Man-Machine Protocol, or Shadowlands Circle Necromancy effect, absorbing all of the Essence out of the cancelled effect and channeling it into the weaver's own Essence pool. If the absorbed Essence would push the weaver over her maximum, her metal Charms flare and spark for a moment as they shunt away the excess.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, pp. 149-150 (PDF 150-151); visually cross-checked. Duration: Instant; Target: Special (the cancelled spell/protocol/necromancy effect).

name: Lightning Elemental Concatenation Protocol
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol the book states is identical to the Creation sorcery spell Lightning Spider, suspected to have been given to Creation's sorcerers by Autochthon himself.
mechanics: Identical in effect to the sorcery spell Lightning Spider (an external Exalted core/supplement spell not itself inventoried here).
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
cost: 1 Willpower (cost/target/duration otherwise as Lightning Spider, not independently restated here).
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 150 (PDF 151); visually cross-checked. Full mechanics defer to the sorcery spell Lightning Spider, not inventoried in this family's scope; flagged rather than guessed at its exact cost/target/duration.

name: The Maker's Basic Defense Array
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that surrounds the weaver with hundreds of whirling polished metal spheres forming a shape-changing defensive sphere, functioning as armor that knocks aside incoming blows and can shatter ordinary weapons.
mechanics: The sphere moves with the weaver and can reshape to fit tight spaces. It has an effective hardness of 5 and adds 10L/10B to the weaver's soak. Any weapon not made of the Magical Materials that strikes the array is checked against a single die roll each time: normal weapons shatter on a roll of 7 or less, exceptional weapons on 5 or less, while perfect weapons are immune. Even undamaged, the attacker's player must make a Dexterity + Melee roll (difficulty 2) to avoid having the weapon knocked from their grasp. Unarmed attackers instead suffer 10 dice of soakable bashing damage.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 3.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 150 (PDF 151); visually cross-checked. Duration: 12 hours; Target: Weaver. Has a more powerful God-Machine-tier counterpart, The Maker's Advanced Defense Array.

name: The Maker's Instantaneous Forge
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol, distantly related to the effect that animates Alchemicals themselves, that conjures a shell out of the ground and binds an Autochthonian elemental into it, creating a temporary automaton servant (a 'golem') that serves the weaver faithfully for a limited time.
mechanics: Casting this protocol causes a golem's shell to appear from the ground; the weaver's power binds an Autochthonian elemental (assigned by the Divine Ministers) into the shell to animate it, and while bound the elemental has no will of its own and performs only the weaver's will. The resulting golem's Traits, appearance, and two unique Charms depend on the type of elemental bound (crystal, lightning, metal, oil, or smoke - see the six per-element golem stat block rows). Those two golem-specific Charms cannot be learned by Exalts who could otherwise learn Charms outside their native Exaltation. A summoned golem serves for (summoner's Essence) weeks before merging back into the substance of the Maker; a weaver may have as many such golems active at once as she has points of Essence.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, pp. 150-151 (PDF 151-152); visually cross-checked. Duration: (Essence) weeks; Target: one conjured automaton. Note: the book lists 5 elemental types (crystal, lightning, metal, oil, smoke/steam) yielding 6 named golem stat blocks below because steam and metal are both represented (Engine golem is the steam variant, Steel golem the metal variant).

name: Engine Golem (Steam Automaton)
summary: A steam-elemental golem summoned via The Maker's Instantaneous Forge: a strong, resilient, but slow and graceless construct of hissing steam in a black metal exoskeleton, with Charms to cleanse disease and to blast enemies with scalding steam.
mechanics: Attributes: Strength 6, Dexterity 2, Stamina 5, Charisma 1, Manipulation 1, Appearance 1, Perception 3, Intelligence 2, Wits 3. Virtue: Automaton (never fails Valor rolls, cannot make any other Virtue rolls). Abilities: Athletics 3 (Lift +2), Awareness 3, Brawl 4, Dodge 4, Endurance 5, Medicine 3, Resistance 9, Stealth 1. Charms: Illness Sterilizing Procedure (10 motes, Instant - sprays a target with warm steam, letting the target reroll Stamina + Endurance with no penalty and two bonus dice to shake off a disease/infection; usable repeatedly if it fails) and Scalding Blast Attack (2 motes per damage die, Instant - a jet of scalding steam dealing a lethal die per 2 motes spent, soakable only with Stamina). Combat stats: Base Initiative 5; Punch Speed 5 Acc 6 Dmg 6L Def 6, Kick Speed 2 Acc 5 Dmg 8L Def 5; Dodge Pool 6; Soak 6L/9B (metal body, 4L/4B); Willpower 2; Health Levels -0/-0/-0/-0/-0/-0/Destroyed; Essence 2; Essence Pool 36. Exalted Power Combat variant: Punch Speed 5 Acc 7 Dmg 6L Def 8 Rate 5, Kick Speed 2 Acc 7 Dmg 9L Def 3 Rate 3, Dodge 8.
compatibility: Storyteller-controlled automaton conjured by an Alchemical's The Maker's Instantaneous Forge protocol; serves for (summoner's Essence) weeks.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, The Maker's Instantaneous Forge sub-entry, pp. 150-151 (PDF 151-152); visually cross-checked against the rendered page. Full stat block/NPC content; recorded gm-only per this project's convention for Storyteller-run summoned creatures.

name: Glass Golem (Crystal Automaton)
summary: A crystal-elemental golem summoned via The Maker's Instantaneous Forge: a squat, transparent, exceedingly hard-to-kill construct of polished glass often used as a body servant, with Charms to detect poisons and dispel illusions.
mechanics: Attributes: Strength 3, Dexterity 3, Stamina 5, Charisma 2, Manipulation 2, Appearance 2, Perception 2, Intelligence 2, Wits 2. Virtue: Automaton. Abilities: Athletics 2, Awareness 3, Brawl 4, Dodge 3, Presence 2, Stealth 5, Survival 2, Thrown 4. Charms: Poison Detection Method (3 motes, Instant - any part of the golem within a foot of poison, disease, or venom turns a noxious green) and Vision-Clearing Protocol (4 motes, Instant - nullifies all illusion/glamour-based magic in a 10-foot radius). Combat stats: Base Initiative 5; Punch Speed 5 Acc 7 Dmg 3B Def 7, Shard (thrown glass) Speed 5 Acc 7 Dmg 5L Rate 3 Range 15; Willpower 2; Soak 7B/7L (crystalline body, 2B/5L); Dodge Pool 6; Health Levels -0/-0/-0/-0/-0/Destroyed; Essence 2; Essence Pool 36. Exalted Power Combat variant: Punch Speed 5 Acc 8 Dmg 3B Def 9 Rate 5, Dodge 8.
compatibility: Storyteller-controlled automaton conjured by an Alchemical's The Maker's Instantaneous Forge protocol; serves for (summoner's Essence) weeks.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, The Maker's Instantaneous Forge sub-entry, p. 151 (PDF 152); visually cross-checked. Full stat block/NPC content; recorded gm-only.

name: Magnet Golem (Lightning Automaton)
summary: A lightning-elemental golem summoned via The Maker's Instantaneous Forge: a construct of ferrous sand or scrap iron bound by an electrical field that magnetically draws in nearby metal, favored as a warrior/bodyguard, with Charms to fling lightning bolts and shock attackers.
mechanics: Any iron or steel item within 10 feet is strongly pulled toward the golem (resistable with Strength equal to the weaver's Essence); metal arrows/bolts that come within range are simply absorbed into its mass. Attributes: Strength 5, Dexterity 3, Stamina 3, Charisma 1, Manipulation 2, Appearance 1, Perception 3, Intelligence 2, Wits 2. Virtue: Automaton. Abilities: Archery 5 (Levinbolt +2), Athletics 3, Brawl 3, Dodge 2, Presence 2 (Intimidation +2), Resistance 5. Charms: Levinbolt (2 motes, Instant - a thrown lightning bolt, Dex + Thrown, base damage 5L, range 50 yards, ignites flammables) and Shocking Aura (5 motes, one scene - adds 2L/2B soak and deals one lethal level to anything touching the golem, ignoring non-Magical-Material metal armor). Combat stats: Base Initiative 5; Punch Speed 5 Acc 6 Dmg 5B Def 6; Dodge Pool 5; Soak 5L/7B (ferrous body, 4L/4B); Willpower 2; Health Levels -0/-0/-0/-0/-0/Destroyed; Essence 2; Essence Pool 36; prefers Levinbolts over melee. Exalted Power Combat variant: Punch Speed 5 Acc 7 Dmg 5B Def 8 Rate 5, Dodge 7.
compatibility: Storyteller-controlled automaton conjured by an Alchemical's The Maker's Instantaneous Forge protocol; serves for (summoner's Essence) weeks.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, The Maker's Instantaneous Forge sub-entry, pp. 151-152 (PDF 152-153); visually cross-checked. Full stat block/NPC content; recorded gm-only.

name: Oil Golem (Oil Automaton)
summary: An oil-elemental golem summoned via The Maker's Instantaneous Forge: a fast, liquid entity (clear, amber, or black) that serves as a messenger, scout, or lubricator of the Machine God's factory-cathedrals, with Charms for high-speed movement and merging with bodies of oil.
mechanics: Attributes: Strength 2, Dexterity 5, Stamina 2, Charisma 1, Manipulation 1, Appearance 2, Perception 2, Intelligence 3, Wits 2. Virtue: Automaton. Abilities: Athletics 2 (Balance +3), Awareness 3, Dodge 5, Linguistics (Native: Machine, Old Realm) 1, Melee 5 (Slashing Sword +1), Stealth 5. Charms: Bursting Reservoir Method (10 motes, one scene - runs at 5x normal movement, base 17 yards/turn, but can take no action but moving in the most direct path) and Riding the Viscous Tides (5 motes, one scene - becomes one with a body of oil, swims/walks freely through it with no Perception penalty, and gains +3 Stealth/+2 Dodge dice while immersed). Combat stats: Base Initiative 7; Slashing Sword Speed 10 Acc 12 Dmg 4L Def 12; Dodge Pool 9; Soak 3L/5B (fluid body, 2L/3B); Willpower 2; Health Levels -0/-0/-0/-0/-0/Destroyed; Essence 2; Essence Pool 36; commonly armed with a slashing sword (adjustable if re-equipped). Exalted Power Combat variant: Slashing Sword Speed 13 Acc 12 Dmg 6L Def 11 Rate 2, Dodge 11.
compatibility: Storyteller-controlled automaton conjured by an Alchemical's The Maker's Instantaneous Forge protocol; serves for (summoner's Essence) weeks.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, The Maker's Instantaneous Forge sub-entry, p. 152 (PDF 153); visually cross-checked. Full stat block/NPC content; recorded gm-only.

name: Smudge Golem (Smoke Automaton)
summary: A smoke-elemental golem summoned via The Maker's Instantaneous Forge: a wispy, dark-gray airborne construct with excellent stealth and surveillance skills, favored as a spy, able to record and later report a whole scene's sensory experience to its master.
mechanics: Attributes: Strength 1, Dexterity 5, Stamina 3, Charisma 1, Manipulation 1, Appearance 2, Perception 4, Intelligence 2, Wits 3. Virtue: Automaton. Abilities: Athletics 4 (Jump +2), Awareness 5, Dodge 4, Endurance 2, Stealth 6. Charms: Shared Experience Technique (6 motes, one scene - records everything seen/heard for a scene, unless it takes another action first; to report, the golem returns and the weaver inhales it, downloading the data in a turn) and Unerring Location of the Master (2 motes, Instant - after a turn of concentration, knows the direction and distance to its master). Combat stats: Base Initiative 8; Punch Speed 8 Acc 5 Dmg 1B Def 5 Rate 5, Kick Speed 5 Acc 4 Dmg 4B Def 2 Rate 3; Dodge Pool 9; Soak 5L/7B (insubstantial body, 4L/4B); Willpower 2; Health Levels -0/-0/-0/-0/-0/Destroyed; Essence 2; Essence Pool 36. Exalted Power Combat variant: Punch Speed 8 Acc 6 Dmg 1B Def 7, Kick Speed 5 Acc 6 Dmg 3B Def 4, Dodge 11.
compatibility: Storyteller-controlled automaton conjured by an Alchemical's The Maker's Instantaneous Forge protocol; serves for (summoner's Essence) weeks.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, The Maker's Instantaneous Forge sub-entry, p. 152 (PDF 153); visually cross-checked. Full stat block/NPC content; recorded gm-only.

name: Steel Golem (Metal Automaton)
summary: The metal-elemental variant of golem summoned via The Maker's Instantaneous Forge: the largest of the golem types, a tall, featureless, mirror-polished humanoid of steel that serves as a guardian, able to shriek down enemy morale or turn itself into an immovable statue.
mechanics: Attributes: Strength 4, Dexterity 1, Stamina 6, Charisma 1, Manipulation 3, Appearance 1, Perception 2, Intelligence 1, Wits 2. Virtue: Automaton. Abilities: Athletics 5, Awareness 3, Brawl 5 (Clinch +1), Dodge 3, Endurance 2, Presence 3 (Intimidation +2), Resistance 5. Charms: Grinding Metal Shriek (8 motes, Instant - a shrill screech forcing a Valor check on everyone within 50 yards; failures tremble helplessly for a number of turns equal to a reflexive Manipulation + Presence roll's successes) and Immovable Object Stance (3 motes, Special duration - the golem becomes an immobile, denser statue; a Stamina + Athletics roll sets the difficulty for others' Strength + Athletics rolls to move it, and it ignores damage below that roll's success count and is treated as an object requiring no damage rolls; it can act only to revert to animate form, costing another 3 motes). Combat stats: Base Initiative 3; Slam Speed 3 Acc 6 Dmg 6B Def 1, Crush Speed 3 Acc 7 Dmg 6B Def 2; Dodge Pool 4; Soak 10L/10B (steel body, 7L/4B); Willpower 2; Health Levels -0/-0/-0/-0/-0/Destroyed; Essence 2; Essence Pool 36. Exalted Power Combat variant: Slam Speed 3 Acc 7 Dmg 6B Def 8 Rate 5, Crush Speed 3 Acc 7 Dmg 6B Def 2 Rate 1, Dodge 6. Weighs around 400 pounds.
compatibility: Storyteller-controlled automaton conjured by an Alchemical's The Maker's Instantaneous Forge protocol; serves for (summoner's Essence) weeks.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, The Maker's Instantaneous Forge sub-entry, p. 153 (PDF 154); visually cross-checked. Full stat block/NPC content; recorded gm-only. This is the 'metal' elemental variant referenced by The Maker's Instantaneous Forge (the steam variant is the separate Engine Golem row).

name: Optimized Component Integration Protocol
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that turns the weaver and a group of willing participants into a model of perfect cooperative efficiency on a single shared task, granting bonus dice scaling with group size.
mechanics: The weaver and all willing participants within a 10-foot radius become models of perfect cooperation and interdependence. So long as they work on one shared task (typically an extended action such as building a device or opening a tunnel), all benefiting members gain one bonus die per additional group member, up to a maximum of (Wits + Essence) individuals worth of bonus dice (e.g., a five-member group grants each member four bonus dice). The protocol ends early if the group finishes the task before the duration expires.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 5.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 153 (PDF 154); visually cross-checked. Duration: the longer of one hour or one scene; Target: the weaver and all willing targets in a 10-foot radius.

name: Phlogiston Web
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that expels an enormous net of blazing, sticky solid fire ('phlogiston') from the weaver's body, covering a large area and burning anything caught within it every turn.
mechanics: The web covers 100 square feet per point of the weaver's permanent Essence, in dimensions of the sorcerer's choosing (e.g., an Essence-4 weaver could make a 20'x20' or 10'x40' web). It inflicts (weaver's Essence + 4) lethal health levels per turn to anything caught in it. Cutting free requires a weapon of the Magical Materials and four successes on a Strength + Melee roll; breaking free by pure strength requires a Strength + Athletics roll at difficulty 5. Characters immune to fire take no damage from the protocol.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 154 (PDF 155); visually cross-checked. Duration: (Essence) turns; Target: area of effect.

name: Plague of Bronze Snakes
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol identical to a Savant & Sorcerer spell of the same underlying effect, except that the snakes wriggle out of the Alchemical sorcerer's own body when the protocol is woven.
mechanics: Except for the snakes emerging from the weaver's own body rather than however the sorcery version manifests them, this protocol is the same as the spell found on p. 112 of Savant and Sorcerer (an external supplement not inventoried here).
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
cost: 1 Willpower (cost/target/duration otherwise as the Savant & Sorcerer spell, not independently restated here).
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
