notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, pp. 154-155 (PDF 155-156); visually cross-checked. Full mechanics defer to an unnamed Savant & Sorcerer spell not inventoried in this family's scope; flagged rather than guessed at its exact cost/target/duration.

name: Probability Degradation Matrix
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that turns fate itself against a group of enemies, saturating the area with bad luck, driving away weak familiars and hostile spirits, and imposing a lasting penalty on every affected foe's dice rolls.
mechanics: Enemy familiars with a Familiar rating below 3 flee the area of effect; hostile spirits with permanent Essence below 2 must succeed on a simple Valor roll or flee as well (fleeing at full movement for two turns per point of the weaver's Essence, not returning until the protocol ends). Allies are unaffected, but for the duration every roll made by an afflicted enemy has its target number increased by one, 10s count as only a single success, and every die that rolls a 1 negates one success.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 5.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 154 (PDF 155); visually cross-checked. Duration: one hour or one scene, whichever is longer; Target: enemies in a 10-yard radius.

name: Sonic Hammer Vocalization
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol in which the weaver emits a devastatingly shrill wail that shakes bone, rattles teeth, shatters glass, and drowns out all other sound; otherwise identical to a named Savant & Sorcerer sorcery spell.
mechanics: Items of glass or crystal in the area suffer 10 levels of bashing damage, and hearing over the noise is impossible. In all other respects, this protocol is identical to the spell Thunder Wolf's Howl (Savant & Sorcerer, p. 122, an external supplement not inventoried here).
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 154 (PDF 155); visually cross-checked. Duration: (Essence) turns; Target: area of effect. Otherwise defers to Thunder Wolf's Howl, not inventoried in this family's scope.

name: Soul Archiving Protocol
summary: A rare, classified Man-Machine Protocol that recaptures a loose ghost's soul into a soulgem when it has escaped after being left too long on its corpse, preserving Autochthon's soul-recycling efficiency; controversial and restricted, requiring high Backing from the Luminors to learn.
mechanics: The weaver weaves the protocol while holding out the target soulgem, then makes a contested Willpower + Essence roll against the ghost; if the ghost's will is strong, the weaver may spend 5 motes per additional die added to her pool. A ghost captured this way remains safely in the soulgem with no chance of escape until the death of its next incarnation. The protocol controverts Luminor dogma and is a closely guarded secret; learning it requires Backing of at least 4 from the Luminors.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0; learning requires Backing 4+ from the Luminors.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, pp. 154-155 (PDF 155-156); visually cross-checked. Duration: Permanent; Target: Ghost.

name: Static Essence Absorption Protocol
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol used to police excessive Essence build-up in Autochthonia, letting the weaver drain stored or committed Essence out of a Hearthstone, Essence-containing gem, or attuned item and into her own reservoir, temporarily disabling the drained item.
mechanics: The weaver drains (Essence x 2) motes of Essence from one device that gathers/stores Essence (a Hearthstone or Essence-containing gem) or from an item with committed Essence (an attuned weapon); the drained Essence flows to the weaver as a glistening tendril. A drained Hearthstone stops working for (6 - Manse rating) hours; drained Essence-containing gems must be recharged, and weapons with committed Essence must be reattuned before their wielder regains attunement benefits. The protocol treats all Essence sources the same (Hearthstone, sorcery/necromancy commitment, etc.) and cannot drain an Essence-user's own Essence pools directly.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 2.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 155 (PDF 156); visually cross-checked. Duration: Instant; Target: one item.

name: Summon Autochthonian Elemental
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that functions exactly like Creation's Terrestrial Circle sorcery spell Summon Elemental, but restricted to the elemental types native to Autochthonia (crystal, lightning, metal, oil, smoke, and steam).
mechanics: Identical to Summon Elemental (Exalted core, p. 219), except that only the six Autochthonian elemental types (crystal, lightning, metal, oil, smoke, steam) can be summoned with it. See Exalted: The Autochthonians pp. 173-178 for more on Autochthonian elementals (not yet inventoried).
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 155 (PDF 156); visually cross-checked. Duration: up to one month; Target: Elemental. The Autochthonian elemental catalog itself (pp. 173-178/PDF 174-179) is not yet inventoried; noted as a follow-up item.

name: Summon Machine Spirit
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol very similar to Summon Elemental, but calling forth a machine spirit rather than an elemental; large machine spirits often send subroutine spirits to serve in their place rather than answering personally.
mechanics: Functions like Summon Elemental (Exalted core, p. 219): the weaver designates the desired machine spirit by any criteria and contests it via the same Willpower contest, but captures a machine spirit instead of an elemental. Machine spirits serving the Great Maker are often dedicated to a single function and dislike multi-tasking, so larger spirits frequently dispatch subroutine spirits in their stead (comparable to how greater elementals delegate, per Savant and Sorcerer p. 75).
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, pp. 155-156 (PDF 156-157); visually cross-checked. Duration: Instant; Target: one machine spirit.

name: Theoplastic Engineering Protocol
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that lets an Alchemical directly reshape Autochthon's living techno-organic landscape (or, in Creation, ordinary earth and stone) by pointing and willing the material to flow, used for tunneling, terraforming, and pulling ore veins to the surface.
mechanics: The weaver points toward the material she wishes to work and it flows to accommodate her will, shifting up to 500 cubic feet of material per turn; groups working in concert can open entire new veins. Used in Creation, it can create trenches, mounds, dikes, berms, reservoirs, or pits in soft earth, or sculpt up to (Essence x 100) square feet of stone; repeated use can build tunnels, bridges, or small islands, and pull ore veins to the surface if they are no more than (Essence x 100) feet down and the weaver knows they are there. It can be used to immure an enemy, though slowly (5 turns), while the target can struggle free with a Strength + Athletics roll at escalating difficulty (base 2, +1 per turn the sorcerer continues shaping). The book speculates, untested, that it might also reshape the Underworld's Labyrinth or Malfeas's landscape, both being Primordial flesh as well.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 155 (PDF 156); visually cross-checked (page includes a full-page illustration between columns; text order unaffected). Duration: one scene; Target: Terrain.

name: Vat Surrogate Reweaving Technique
summary: A Man-Machine Protocol that lets an Alchemical instantaneously swap one of her installed Charms for another Charm she has on retainer at the Vats, bypassing the normal downtime or travel needed to visit the Vats in person.
mechanics: If the weaver has Charms held on retainer at the Vats (per the Vats Background), this protocol lets her instantaneously exchange one of her currently installed Charms for one of those retained Charms, without needing downtime or a physical visit to the Vats.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 4; requires the Vats Background with Charms on retainer.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, p. 155 (PDF 156); visually cross-checked. Duration: Instant; Target: One Alchemical Exalt. Cross-references the Vats Background (pp. 68-69/PDF 69-70), already inventoried in this file.

name: Vision Transmitting Protocol
summary: The final catalogued Man-Machine Protocol: the weaver spits forth a growing crystal dodecahedron into which she speaks a message; the crystal functions like the Terrestrial spell Infallible Messenger but also visually transmits the speaker's image and background to the recipient.
mechanics: The weaver spits out a fist-sized crystal dodecahedron that grows to about the size of a human head as she finishes shaping the Essence, then speaks her message into it. The protocol otherwise functions exactly like the Terrestrial Circle spell Infallible Messenger (Exalted core, p. 218), except the recipient can also see the speaker's image in the crystal (and may glimpse background events) as well as hear the message.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: Man-Machine Protocol; usable via the Man-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: Man-Machine Protocols, pp. 155-156 (PDF 156-157); visually cross-checked. Duration: One message; Target: One creature. This is the last Man-Machine Protocol before the God-Machine Protocols section begins on the same page (p. 156/PDF 157).

name: Auspicious Reformatting Mudra
summary: A God-Machine Protocol that lets an Alchemical fundamentally reweave an automaton or machine's pattern, assigning it an entirely different destiny: mending it, transforming it into a different device or familiar, or breaking it down entirely.
mechanics: With a series of hand gestures, the weaver reweaves a target automaton's pattern. If the weaver's Essence is greater than or equal to the target's, the effect is automatic; otherwise the player makes a contested Essence roll against the machine spirit. This can mend/reactivate a broken machine spirit, transform it into something else entirely (e.g., a gremlin into a custodian, or reduce it to inert parts), or reconfigure a machine spirit with up to half the weaver's Essence (rounded up) into a device with an Artifact rating equal to half the Alchemical's Essence (rounded up), or into an Autochthonian familiar with a rating equal to the weaver's Essence. Transforming one artifact into another of equal power instead requires an Intelligence + Lore roll needing successes equal to the artifact's rating. At Essence 7+, the weaver may reconfigure multiple targets simultaneously for +5 motes per additional target (all within line of sight), though used this way it can only alter automata's programming/behavior rather than rebuild their forms, and no target may have permanent Essence greater than 3.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 6.
cost: 1 Willpower plus (rating affected x 10) motes; +5 motes per additional simultaneous target at Essence 7+.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 156 (PDF 157); visually cross-checked. Duration: Permanent; Target: one automaton.

name: Destiny-Optimizing Meditation
summary: A God-Machine Protocol in which the weaver communes with the Core of the Machine God to discern the optimal path toward her current goal, adding automatic successes to every roll for the protocol's duration.
mechanics: For the duration, the weaver adds (Essence rating) automatic successes to every roll she makes.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 6.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 156 (PDF 157); visually cross-checked. Duration: (Essence) turns; Target: Weaver.

name: Essence Matrix Inversion Procedure
summary: A God-Machine Protocol prepared up to a day in advance that makes the weaver's Essence flow matrix highly reflective, turning almost all incoming sorcery, necromancy, protocols, and Essence weapon attacks back on whoever launched them.
mechanics: While active, all incoming protocols, sorcery spells, and necromancy effects targeting the sorcerer (or any area of effect including her) - except Solar Circle Sorcery and Void Circle Necromancy - are instantly reflected back at their caster; Essence weapon effects (implosion bows, Essence cannons, etc.) are likewise reflected back at the attacking weapon. A Perception + Investigation roll (difficulty 4) can spot a faint mirage-like ripple around the weaver, and anyone who can see Essence flows notices foot-long quills of blue light radiating from her body.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0; must be prepared up to one day in advance.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 156 (PDF 157); visually cross-checked. Duration: One day; Target: Weaver.

name: Executive Filature Protocol
summary: A dark, powerful God-Machine Protocol that unweaves a target being's pattern Trait by Trait, ultimately erasing her from existence entirely and purging all memory of her incarnation; historically used, left deliberately unfinished, to reduce exiles to helpless wrecks before abandoning them in the Reaches.
mechanics: The weaver must stay within her Essence in feet of the target and can do nothing else while maintaining the effect; being interrupted terminates it (unwoven Traits are not restored, though the weaver can spend 5 motes per dot to reweave them within a day if the target hasn't faded entirely). The first turn inflicts wracking anxiety and panic on the target; afterward, the target loses one Attribute dot per turn, highest first. Once all Attributes reach 1, the target begins losing health levels, growing progressively transparent; when the final health level is removed, the target fades from the pattern entirely and her soulgem clatters to the ground, purged of all memory of that incarnation. In Creation, souls destroyed this way fall instantly into Lethe. Weavers typically must obtain this protocol from the Divine Ministers or the design weavers themselves.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 6.
cost: 1 Willpower plus 5 motes plus 1 mote per turn maintained.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, pp. 156-157 (PDF 157-158); visually cross-checked. Duration: Varies; Target: One individual.

name: Homuncular Drone Deployment
summary: A God-Machine Protocol that lets the weaver detach her own forearms and deploy them as flying attack drones, letting her strike targets out of reach at the cost of temporary health levels per drone committed.
mechanics: The weaver is down one health level per drone deployed until the limbs return and re-fuse with her body. Drones use the sorcerer's own Traits but gain her Essence rating in Brawl and retain the benefits of brawling aids; they hover at twice the weaver's movement rate, and she always knows their location. Each drone has 3 health levels; if one is destroyed, the character remains permanently down one health level until she returns to the Vats for a replacement limb or is healed of the aggravated damage by an appropriate Charm.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 2.
cost: 1 Willpower plus 5 motes and one committed health level per drone.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 157 (PDF 158); visually cross-checked. Duration: One scene; Target: Weaver.

name: Incarnation of Bestial Malice
summary: A God-Machine Protocol comparable to a Lunar war form: the weaver transforms into a terrifying chimeric or vegetative nightmare creature entirely unlike anything native to Autochthonia, gaining enormous natural weapons, hardness, soak, and boosted Strength/Stamina, temporarily losing her mechanical nature altogether.
mechanics: The character becomes an enormous (a ton or more), living monstrous form - a chimera of unfamiliar beasts (yeddim, tyrant lizard, stryx, or others), a vegetative form (bark, thorns, prehensile vines), or a mix, agreed with the Storyteller beforehand; the mechanical nature disappears though some bulky Charms may show as vestigial metallic studs. The form gains an effective hardness of 10 and 10 additional soak against both bashing and lethal; Strength and Stamina each increase by 2 (even past 5). Brawl/Martial Arts/Melee attacks with claws gain +3 speed, +1 accuracy, and deal Strength + 6 lethal damage (Strength + 8 lethal in a clinch), with reach extended to (Essence) yards. Natural weapons are treated as roughly Artifact •• Magical-Material weapons without the Material bonus. Armor and weapons are incompatible with the form (buried within the character's bulk for the duration). Normal movement rate is retained, and the character can grow gills to breathe underwater; for +5 motes, she also grows wings enabling flight at three times land speed.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 2; Maximum Clarity 7.
cost: 1 Willpower plus 30 or 35 motes (+5 more for flight).
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, pp. 157-158 (PDF 158-159); visually cross-checked. Duration: (Essence) hours; Target: Weaver. Notably the only protocol seen in this catalog with both a Minimum and a Maximum Clarity requirement.

name: Instantaneous Transfer Protocol
summary: A God-Machine Protocol identical to the Terrestrial spell Travel Without Distance, except the Alchemical sinks physically into the substance of the Great Maker in one location and emerges from the ground at her destination an instant later.
mechanics: Identical to Travel Without Distance (Exalted core, p. 221), except the means of travel is sinking into and re-emerging from the substance of Autochthon rather than however the sorcery version works.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
cost: 1 Willpower (cost/target/duration otherwise as Travel Without Distance, not independently restated here).
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 157 (PDF 158); visually cross-checked. Full mechanics defer to the Terrestrial spell Travel Without Distance, not inventoried in this family's scope; flagged rather than guessed at its exact cost/target/duration.

name: Machine-Soul Essence Baffle
summary: A God-Machine Protocol in which the weaver assumes a sacred asana at the center of an area to render it proof against sorcery and protocols, attuning the space to her own Essence flow and expanding her soul to fill it; the book states this is equivalent to the sorcery effect Mercury's Deliverance.
mechanics: The weaver assumes an asana sacred to the Divine Ministers at the exact center of the target area, chants to attune the area to her own Essence flow to the exclusion of all others, then expands her soul out of her soulgem to fill the spherical space. In all other respects this is equivalent to Mercury's Deliverance (Savant and Sorcerer, p. 131, an external supplement not inventoried here).
requirements: Minimum Clarity 2.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, pp. 157-158 (PDF 158-159); visually cross-checked. Duration: Five shifts; Target: Area of Effect.

name: The Maker's Advanced Defense Array
summary: The God-Machine-tier upgrade of The Maker's Basic Defense Array: the weaver is surrounded by a sphere of whirling adamant shuriken instead of metal spheres, offering much stronger armor and a chance to sever an attacker's limb.
mechanics: The array has an effective hardness of 10 and adds 20L/20B to the weaver's soak. Each time a weapon hits the array, the Storyteller rolls one die: weapons not made of the Magical Materials shatter on a result of 1-9, while weapons of the Magical Materials shatter only on a 1. Even undamaged, the attacker's player must succeed on a Dexterity + Melee roll (difficulty 3) to avoid having the weapon knocked from their grasp. Unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attackers suffer 10 dice of soakable lethal damage, and if an attacker takes more than two health levels of damage from this, the attacking limb is severed. In bright light, the weaver is surrounded by a vivid storm of rainbow-colored refracted light.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 158 (PDF 159); visually cross-checked. Duration: 12 hours; Target: Weaver.

name: Maser Palm Technique
summary: A God-Machine Protocol equivalent to the Creation sorcery spell Blood of Boiling Oil, except that the target's blood simply boils and denatures in her veins rather than becoming oil.
mechanics: Equivalent to the spell Blood of Boiling Oil (Exalted core, p. 220), except the target's blood boils and denatures directly rather than transforming into oil first.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
cost: 1 Willpower (cost/target/duration otherwise as Blood of Boiling Oil, not independently restated here).
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 158 (PDF 159); visually cross-checked. Full mechanics defer to Blood of Boiling Oil, not inventoried in this family's scope; flagged rather than guessed at its exact cost/target/duration.

name: Passenger Hosting Protocol
summary: A God-Machine Protocol that interweaves the weaver's pattern with willing companions, letting them occupy the same physical space and share a telepathic link, with only the weaver able to act while all passengers' Strength/Stamina/Soak/Resistance stack onto hers and damage is split evenly.
mechanics: Up to (half the weaver's permanent Essence, rounded up) willing individuals may step into and occupy the same space as the weaver. All parties are telepathically linked for the duration; passengers think independently but only the weaver can act. The passengers' Strength, Stamina, Soak, and Resistance stack on top of the weaver's, with no external way to tell the sorcerer is more than one individual. All damage taken is split evenly between the weaver and all passengers. A spirit passenger must first Materialize to participate. A sorcerer using this protocol cannot be possessed.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 3.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 158 (PDF 159); visually cross-checked. Duration: One day; Target: The weaver and passenger(s).

name: Pattern Suspension Protocol
summary: A God-Machine Protocol known to both Alchemical weavers and design weavers alike, described as the Alchemical version of Eternal Crystalline Encasement, wrapping a target object in a scintillating cocoon of spun diamond fiber that suspends its pattern until a matching pearl of gem-stuff touches the cocoon.
mechanics: Except for the crystalline-filament cocoon (sprayed from the weaver's fingertips) replacing whatever medium the sorcery version uses, this protocol is mechanically identical to Eternal Crystalline Encasement (Savant and Sorcerer, p. 127, an external supplement not inventoried here). The weaver spins a pearl of tightly woven gem-stuff strands that must touch the cocoon to end the protocol and resume the object's pattern function.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 0.
cost: 1 Willpower (cost/target/duration otherwise as Eternal Crystalline Encasement, not independently restated here).
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 158 (PDF 159); visually cross-checked. Full mechanics defer to Eternal Crystalline Encasement, not inventoried in this family's scope; flagged rather than guessed at its exact cost/target/duration.

name: Radiant Matrix Transmutation
summary: A powerful God-Machine Protocol that transmutes solids and liquids in a large radius into beautiful faceted elemental crystal, petrifying creatures caught within it and healing blight zones or reclaiming shadowlands within Autochthon's own substance.
mechanics: The weaver assumes a divinely authorized asana; a wave of order radiates outward at 10 feet per turn, transmuting solids/liquids (except things already made of crystal, such as Hearthstones or adamant items) into faceted elemental crystal. Artifacts resist crystallizing for (Artifact rating) turns, or 10 turns if rated N/A; artifacts forged by the Maker himself (such as the Eye of Autochthon) are wholly immune. Creatures in the radius are transmuted too, usually from the feet up, taking the weaver's Essence in aggravated damage per turn within the area; creatures reduced to Incapacitated by this become crystal statues of themselves (any crystal must be cut away before Medicine Charms can heal the damage, or crystal slivers remain in the regenerated flesh). This protocol empowers Autochthon wherever it is used, healing blight zones and reclaiming any sectors that have become shadowlands.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 6.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, pp. 158-159 (PDF 159-160); visually cross-checked. Duration: Permanent; Target: (Essence x 10)-foot radius.

name: Transcendent Consciousness Protocol
summary: A God-Machine Protocol that dramatically expands all five of the weaver's senses to fill a 60-yard sphere, letting her sense and instantly process everything happening within it (including through solid barriers), making her impossible to surprise.
mechanics: Within the 60-yard-diameter sphere, the weaver feels everything as if touching it, sees everything as if closely examining it, and hears everything as if it were the only sound - solid objects are no barrier, so she can sense activity 30 yards below her, on the far side of a wall, or flowing through the Maker's veins in the area. She instantly processes all sensory data received, aiding reconnaissance, eavesdropping, and perimeter monitoring, and cannot be surprised (an invisible intruder can still be sensed by weight on the floor, air displacement, heartbeat, or scent). The player gains the Exalt's Essence rating as automatic successes on all Perception rolls within the 30-yard radius (i.e. within the sphere).
requirements: Minimum Clarity 4.
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm.
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 159 (PDF 160); visually cross-checked. Duration: One scene; Target: Weaver.

name: Transcendent Pattern-Weaving Protocol
summary: The single Alchemical protocol that works only in the Wyld (and nowhere else): an extraordinarily rare, extremely high-Clarity God-Machine Protocol that lets a truly powerful Alchemical spin order directly out of the Wyld's chaos, permanently reclaiming territory from it, at the cost of enraging every nearby Fair Folk and holding a rare potential to transform a raksha noble into one of the Mountain Folk.
mechanics: The weaver steps into the swirling Wyld and executes a long prayer and complex mudra; each hour spent praying and weaving, she formats a 20-yard radius of reality around her, for as many hours as she has points of Stamina. Fair Folk caught in the area of effect take aggravated damage equal to the weaver's permanent Essence. The protocol causes an unpleasant strangling sensation in every Fair Folk within a radius in miles equal to the weaver's Essence (doubled in the Deep Wyld), making completing a long weaving unlikely without provoking a hostile response. By weaving pattern directly from the substance of a targeted Fair Folk noble (rather than merely catching him in the effect area), the sorcerer can instead attempt to reformat him into one of the Mountain Folk: the raksha's player must win a contested Willpower + Essence roll against the weaver or be transformed into one of the Jadeborn, an inert, memoryless jade-egg soul awaiting a Mountain Folk Charm (Jade's Egg Hatched, Exalted: The Fair Folk p. 271) to quicken it.
requirements: Minimum Clarity 10 (perfect Clarity).
compatibility: God-Machine Protocol; usable via the God-Machine Weaving Engine Charm. Only Alchemical protocol confirmed to work exclusively within the Wyld (per the What Works Where sidebar).
notes: Chapter Four: God-Machine Protocols, p. 159 (PDF 160); visually cross-checked. Duration: Permanent; Target: Nearby Wyld areas. Requires Minimum Clarity 10, the highest Clarity requirement of any protocol in the catalog, matching Clarity's 0-10 scale already inventoried under clarity-effects-table. This is the last entry in the weaving-protocol catalog; the 'Autochthonian Thaumaturges' section begins immediately after it on the same page, moving into non-protocol content.

name: Sweet Sleep Surrogate Syrup
summary: An Autochthonian alchemical formula unique to this book: a cloyingly sweet syrup distilled from molds and fungi that lets a 30-second nap grant all the benefits of a full night's sleep, widely stockpiled by cities to squeeze extra shifts out of Populat laborers.
requirements: Alchemy ••; Intelligence + Occult roll (difficulty 3); Minimum Backing ••.
mechanics: A single dose grants all the benefits of a full night's rest - including feeling well-rested and a Conviction roll to regain Willpower - in a 30-second nap. It has no effect on Essence recovery, and a worker using it still needs one full night of true sleep every (Stamina x 2) nights or begins suffering sleep-deprivation penalties.
compatibility: Any character with the Alchemy formula and appropriate Backing; in practice used mainly on mortal Populat laborers.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Thaumaturges' -> 'Alchemy', p. 161 (PDF 162); visually cross-checked against the rendered page. One of only three alchemical formulae unique to Autochthonia listed in this section (the book notes several Creation formulae, e.g. ghost flower, are conversely unknown there).

name: Friction Banishing Preparation
summary: A mineral-oil-derived Autochthonian alchemical formula that perfectly eliminates friction between two surfaces, prized industrially for silencing grinding machinery but equally usable as an improvised hazard that turns a patch of floor into a nearly unwalkable slick.
requirements: Alchemy •••; Intelligence + Occult roll (difficulty 4); Minimum Backing •••.
mechanics: A single vial coats a 10-by-10-foot patch of floor. The treated patch requires a successful Perception + Alertness roll (difficulty 1) to spot. Standing still on it requires a difficulty 4 Dexterity + Athletics roll; walking across it, or moving or standing up without something to hold onto, is difficulty 6. It can be neutralized with a simple Alchemy •/Backing • counter-agent, or left to degrade in open air after about a week.
compatibility: Any character with the Alchemy formula and appropriate Backing; also used industrially to ease machinery.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Thaumaturges' -> 'Alchemy', p. 161 (PDF 162); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: The Maker's Inertial Bile
summary: The most tightly restricted Autochthonian alchemical formula in the book: an acrid pale-gray fluid harvested from wild machine spirits that instantly halts and exorcises any spirit or animating force from a machine, automaton, or gremlin on contact - a substance the Tripartite polices as a serious crime for ordinary citizens to possess.
requirements: Alchemy •••••; Intelligence + Occult roll (difficulty 8); Minimum Backing •••••.
mechanics: A single phial, shattered against any device, instantaneously stops a machine or automaton and exorcises any spirit or animating force from it - including gremlins, zombies, golems, corpses possessed by nemissaries, and automata summoned via protocols or spells (e.g. bone lions, bronze snakes). Important Tripartite officials keep a phial or two on hand for deactivating runaway factory machinery or exorcising marauding gremlins, but mere possession of the fluid by a member of the Populat is a crime worthy of severe downward mobility or, more probably, exile.
compatibility: Any character with the Alchemy formula and appropriate Backing; effectively restricted to senior Tripartite officials in practice.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Thaumaturges' -> 'Alchemy', p. 161 (PDF 162); visually cross-checked against the rendered page. The book's own example automata immune to this bile's animating spirit only in the sense that they'd be shut down by it (bone lions, bronze snakes) point back to this book's own Plague of Bronze Snakes weaving protocol and the Summon Autochthonian Elemental protocol as the kind of summoned automata this formula can stop.

name: Autochthonian Technology (chapter framing)
summary: A framing note introducing the Autochthonian Technology section: Autochthonia's overall tech level is comparable to the early Dragon-Blooded Shogunate, Essence replaces electricity as a power source, clockwork and steam-driven pistons are the norm, and Alchemical Charms themselves define the practical ceiling of the setting's science, so the artifacts in this section generally echo a single Charm's function at reduced efficiency.
mechanics: Artifacts in this section not stated as associated with a specific Magical Material may be attuned by any Essence user at standard cost, and many are explicitly intended for mortal use with no commitment requirement at all.
compatibility: All Alchemical castes; many items are mortal-usable.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' introduction, p. 180 (PDF 181); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Machines in the Machine God (Efficiency and Inspiration)
summary: A sidebar describing two passive effects of Autochthon's own psychic presence on technology throughout most of his body: devices last 10% longer between maintenance intervals (Efficiency), and rolls to invent new devices gain a bonus (Inspiration) - both suspended in blight zones.
mechanics: Efficiency: mechanical and magical devices last 10 percent longer before accruing wear penalties (e.g. a device normally needing service every 10 hours instead goes 11); this bonus is not already factored into any artifact statistics printed in this chapter, and does not apply in blight zones (where items function at normal or reduced efficiency at the Storyteller's discretion). Inspiration: rolls to create an all-new device gain one extra die (an automatic success instead, inside the sacred Core); this bonus does not apply when following a blueprint or copying an existing model, though it does apply to independently recreating a lost design or to two inventors who separately conceive the same device (only the project leader's player gains it on a team effort). No bonus applies in blight zones.
compatibility: Any Craft-based invention or artifact-maintenance roll made within Autochthonia (excluding blight zones); a stronger, doubled version of Efficiency applied only prior to the Primordial's exile Elsewhere and no longer applies except at the Core itself.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Machines in the Machine God' sidebar, p. 181 (PDF 182); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Artificial Textiles
summary: A survey of the alchemically produced fabrics Autochthonians use in place of organic materials: common synthetic 'leather' made from elemental oil, artificial silk favored for comfort and cut-resistance, and several rarer specialty textiles (a liquid-resistant stretch fabric, a heavy liquid-absorbing material, and a tightly woven fiber used for exceptional chain shirts and buff jackets).
mechanics: Resources rating scales from • for common synthetic leather or artificial silk goods up to ••••• for the rarest specialty weaves; no other independent game mechanics are given beyond what the specific armor/clothing items built from them (e.g. the exceptional chain shirts and buff jackets referenced elsewhere in this chapter) state.
cost: Resources • to ••••• depending on the specific textile.
compatibility: Any character; foundational material for Autochthonian clothing and light armor.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Artificial Textiles', p. 180 (PDF 181); visually cross-checked against the rendered page. Reference-only because it describes a category of raw material rather than a single purchasable item; the Fiber-Weave Bodysuit row is the concrete armor item built from the 'tightly woven fiber' variant.

name: Filter Mask
summary: A cup-shaped mask sealed over the mouth and nose that filters air through hundreds of layers of artificial cloth, blocking or muting toxic gasses and preventing all but the most virulent airborne diseases; mortal wearers are treated as Exalted for any poison or disease they do breathe.
mechanics: Grants three extra dice to resist breathed poisons and diseases, and lets mortal wearers treat themselves as Exalted for any such poison or disease they do breathe. Each mask is good for about a month of regular use before requiring disassembly and purification with industrial solvents; after that first month, its bonus decreases by one die per month of continued use until it becomes useless.
compatibility: Any character, including mortals; standard-issue for Autochthonian infantry.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Filter Mask', p. 180-182 (PDF 181-183); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Photo-Resonant Gel
summary: A simple, widely used alchemical compound that exists in two forms: one that fluoresces in the presence of concentrated Essence (used as warning badges, wall glyphs, and Essence-level gauges), and one that stores and slowly releases ordinary light like foxfire (used as backup illumination on worker uniforms).
mechanics: The Essence-sensitive form glows a chosen hue within a five-yard radius of concentrated Essence sources (spirits, power capacitors, Alchemical reservoir tanks, the Great Maker's own cables), bright enough to read by within a yard and noticeable almost as far as a torch; the Charms Essence Dormancy Mode and Essence Veil (and similar magic) can foil this detection. The light-storing form instead absorbs shined light and releases it in a dim, candle-level glow for three to five hours between recharges, needing only exposure to a strong light source to reset. Unauthorized possession is a (usually minor) crime, as the Glorious Luminors of the Brilliant Rapture jealously hoard the formulas.
compatibility: Any character; used as talismans/badges, painted warning glyphs, Essence-charge gauges on other artifacts, or illumination accents on clothing.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Photo-Resonant Gel', p. 182-183 (PDF 183-184); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Arc Protector
summary: Black-crystal goggles that let the wearer look directly at blinding light sources - open electrical arcs, plasma furnaces, and the like - without being permanently blinded, at the cost of hampering low-light vision.
mechanics: Wearers suffer no penalty or ill effect from staring at naked electrical arcs, open plasma furnaces, or similarly blinding sights (though the goggles offer no protection against magical effects with a visual component, such as Sidereal anima powers). In low-light conditions, they impose a one- to three-die penalty depending on how poor the light is. Issued to Autochthonians traveling to Creation as protection against the unfiltered sun; going to Creation unprotected imposes Awareness penalties for bright conditions (one die for indirect/weak sunlight up to three dice at cloudless noon) until the wearer completes a week-long gradual light-exposure weaning process.
compatibility: Any character, including mortals; standard issue for Autochthonians traveling to Creation.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Arc Protector', p. 182 (PDF 183); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Autolabe
summary: A gimbaled compass-like navigational artifact whose pointer always orients back toward a fixed beacon (usually the center of its owner's home city) rather than toward a cardinal direction, essential for finding one's way through Autochthonia's fully three-dimensional maze of passageways.
mechanics: The beacon can be reset by leaving the autolabe in physical contact with a new beacon for 25 hours; otherwise it always points back to whichever beacon it was attuned to at creation. Exploration models come as a matched set with a portable base-unit beacon; a rarer variant lets two autolabes interchange beacons to always point back to each other. A more sophisticated Artifact •• version has a secondary mode that memorizes an individual's exact path when a button is pressed, then guides the bearer back along the remembered path (returning her to the point she deviated from if she strays).
compatibility: Any character, including mortals; common among explorers of the Reaches and Far Reaches.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Autolabe', p. 182-183 (PDF 183-184); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Essence Capacitor
summary: Autochthonia's Hearthstone-equivalent: a nearly indestructible orichalcum-caged crystal that stores and emits a focused current of ambient motes to power large or advanced artifacts, distinguished from a true Hearthstone by running out of power after 25 hours unless recharged and by conveying no independent magical benefit of its own.
mechanics: Plugs into a socket exactly as a Hearthstone would; supplies constant power at twice its rating in motes per hour to mundane devices, but only its rating in motes per hour when committed (1 mote) to replenish an Alchemical or other Essence user directly. Functions for 25 hours before automatically shutting down for lack of motes, or may be switched off earlier and later reactivated; a deactivated capacitor recharges one hour of power per two hours spent respiring Essence in Autochthonia (it cannot recharge in blight zones, and must be specially calibrated at a half-hour technician's cost before it can recharge outside Autochthonia at all). If shattered (deliberately or by accident), it releases a pulse inflicting (rating x 10) lethal damage, minus 1L per full yard of distance; a deactivated capacitor only explodes on a botched attempt. The surrounding wire lattice has a separate soak of 10L/10B and 10 health levels, repairable with Resources equal to the artifact's rating (or half, rounded up, for partial lattice damage) by a technician with Occult and Lore •• and a pertinent Craft •••. A tri-socket adapter (Resources •••) houses three same-rated capacitors and automatically switches between them for uninterrupted power.
compatibility: Any character; the standard Autochthonian power source for artifacts, vehicles, and installations lacking a Manse or Demesne to draw on.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Essence Capacitor', p. 183 (PDF 184); visually cross-checked against the rendered page. Cross-referenced to manse-background-altered because the book explicitly frames capacitors as filling the technological niche Hearthstones/Manses serve in Creation, which Autochthonia otherwise entirely lacks.

name: Flaw Scanner
summary: A palm-mounted amethyst amulet that projects a violet light revealing cracks, flaws, and points of unintended stress in objects, mainly a narrative diagnostic tool but also a minor aid to repair work.
mechanics: Activated for a scene by spending 1 Willpower or 2 motes; scans up to a square yard per turn. Any Craft rolls made to repair a flaw the scanner revealed gain a one-die bonus, provided the technician studied the damage under the light for a full minute first.
compatibility: Any character, including mortals.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Flaw Scanner', p. 183 (PDF 184); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Light Amplification Visor
summary: Goggles (or, for mortals only, surgically implanted lens replacements) that duplicate the light-intensification filters submodule of the Alchemical Optical Enhancement Charm; a superior Artifact •• version adds a powered thermal-vision mode as well.
mechanics: Worn or implanted continuously, the base version grants the benefits and drawbacks of the light-intensification filters submodule of Optical Enhancement. The Artifact •• version additionally grants thermal vision (identical to that Charm's thermal-vision submodule) when powered - 1 Willpower point charges it for two hours, or 1 mote for one hour. Surgical implantation takes three hours and an Intelligence + Medicine roll (difficulty 5) by the surgeon; failure permanently blinds the patient. Implanted wearers gain no benefit from arc protectors worn at the same time (the two artifacts cancel out), and Alchemical Exalted specifically cannot have this artifact implanted (though they may wear it as goggles).
compatibility: Any character (implantation is mortal-only; Alchemicals may only wear the goggle form).
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Light Amplification Visor', p. 183-184 (PDF 184-185); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Light Sphere
summary: The standard portable light source of the sunless Realm of Brass and Shadow: a three-inch brass-and-glass globe that consumes a disc of low-quality jade fuel to produce a week (or longer, for higher-quality fuel) of harsh, cold torch-equivalent light without heat or smoke.
mechanics: Each standard jade fuel disc (Resources • in Autochthonia/Yu-Shan, •• elsewhere) burns for a full week; higher-quality discs last a month (Resources •• everywhere), and rare perfectly calibrated discs last a full year (Resources ••• everywhere, not mass-produced). A switch conserves fuel by breaking/restoring the jade-catalyst connection. A rarer shuttered model (also Artifact •) has a mirrored interior and an iris shutter that can slide colored glass filters across it, projecting light only in one direction but tripling illumination distance - used for signaling, including secret optical codes among dissidents.
compatibility: Any character, including mortals; Alchemicals themselves typically see by their own animas instead.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Light Sphere', p. 184 (PDF 185); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Omnimodal Wardrobe Unit
summary: A single garment-artifact that compresses an entire wardrobe into one item, woven through with moonsilver wires and swarming with microscopic spider automata that unravel and reweave its fabric into any previously seen or newly designed clothing shape on command.
mechanics: Once attuned (1 mote committed), the wearer may reflexively spend 1 mote to change the garment's form in a single turn; the process also cleans and repairs any damage to the suit as a side effect (or can be triggered for 1 mote purely to clean/repair without changing form). Recalling a previously assumed shape uses a Wits + Awareness roll (difficulty 2); designing an unfamiliar shape from scratch uses Wits + Craft (Textiles) (difficulty 2) as a simple (non-reflexive) action, with failure producing an imperfect result. Can become any clothing item or combination, in any coloration/texture/apparent material, and in all forms grants +1L soak (not armor, stacks with worn armor) - but it can never become actual armor.
compatibility: Essence 2-5 Alchemical Exalted primarily, though usable by other characters as clothing.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Omnimodal Wardrobe Unit', p. 184-185 (PDF 185-186); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Portable Nutriment Recycling Engine (Ponre)
summary: A person-sized, foldable field device (nicknamed a 'ponre') that grinds and sterilizes any organic matter fed into its intake chute into imperishable, chalky nutrient pellets equivalent to a full meal - a battlefield and exploration ration-maker.
mechanics: Collapses to a backpack-portable steel box (one minute to transform either way) despite weighing only about 30 pounds. In expanded mode, a hand-cranked spring mechanism (five minutes of winding = one hour of operation) powers grinding blades that process two pounds of organic material per minute into a single nourishing pellet; all toxins and diseases in the source material are removed. Ten pellets are a Resources •• item in Autochthonia (generally unobtainable elsewhere).
compatibility: Any character, including mortals; designed for battlefield or exploration use.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Portable Nutriment Recycling Engine', p. 185 (PDF 186); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Respirator Module
summary: An upgraded filter mask built around a blue jade nodule that can additionally seal completely and synthesize breathable air directly out of Essence, letting the wearer travel underwater or through vacuum without asphyxiating.
mechanics: Functions as a filter mask with no cleaning/upkeep requirement. Flipping a tongue-operated switch seals the module and begins synthesizing air, fully protecting the wearer from harmful airborne effects and permitting underwater or vacuum travel. Requires chips of crystallized thaumaturgical reagent to operate (Resources •• per batch of 10 in Autochthonia, ••• per batch elsewhere); each chip provides an hour of air, and the module vibrates when running low. Any Essence-channeling wearer may instead reflexively spend 1 mote to power the module for an hour.
compatibility: Any character, including mortals; issued to elite military units for toxic or airless missions.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Respirator Module', p. 185 (PDF 186); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Courier Drone
summary: A dragonfly-sized metallic automaton, the most common means of intercity messaging in Autochthonia, capable of carrying a quarter-pound of cargo (scroll tubes, memory crystals) at up to 300 miles per hour by homing in on Essence-broadcast city signals; a rarer exploration/military variant instead shuttles between two fixed beacons.
mechanics: Navigates by tracking metropoli Essence emissions across Autochthonia (leaving it blind and confused outside the Realm of Brass and Shadow) and follows an ancient Alchemical-broadcast neural signal to its drop site; the beacon-pair variant instead infallibly tracks two specific beacons on the same plane of reality, landing to wait if its destination beacon enters a scrying-warded area. Statistics: Intelligence 1, Perception 3, Wits 3, no Virtues (never fails Valor rolls, never succeeds at other Virtue checks); Strength 1/Dexterity 10/Stamina 1, Willpower 10, Health Levels -2/Squished, no attack, Dodge 15, Soak 1L/1B, Athletics 5, Awareness 5, Dodge 5, Stealth 5. Must respire living Essence through its wings; drops to 50 mph in a blight zone or shadowland by day, and after an hour in the Underworld goes erratic and lands until re-exposed to living Essence for an hour. Repair: an hour of work, Resources •• per health level, technician with Craft (Clockworks or similar) ••••.
compatibility: Any character; requisitionable as an artifact or as a Familiar Background purchase.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Courier Drone', p. 185-186 (PDF 186-187); visually cross-checked against the rendered page (stat block visually confirmed on p. 186/PDF 187).

name: Soulgem (mortal implant and Artifact rating)
summary: The mandatory forehead-implanted artifact every Autochthonian citizen receives within a week of birth: a Hearthstone-durable jewel (color and shape coded by social caste) that absorbs and stores its bearer's soul at death for eventual recycling into a new body, with Alchemical Exalted instead receiving a flawless diamond soulgem that never returns to Autochthon and is instead reinstalled in a new Alchemical.
mechanics: On the bearer's death, the jewel absorbs her fused higher and lower soul and stores it until it can be recycled (a Celestial Exalt's Essence cannot be captured this way). Soulgems share a Hearthstone's durability, so even severe industrial accidents cannot crack them; deliberately breaking one is a capital crime throughout Autochthonia. Soulgem color/shape denotes social caste: round polished onyx for the Populat, rectangular orange topaz for the Olgotary, square sapphire for Theomachrats, and diamond-shaped amethyst for Sodalts; outcasts' gems bear concentric tattooed rings recording their crimes. Exiles have their gems forcibly removed (a scarring procedure that, per Luminor doctrine, dooms the soul to Oblivion, though Autochthon actually still recycles it under a falsified genealogy number, secretly watched for three lifetimes). Alchemical soulgems are always flawless many-faceted diamonds that are never fed back to Autochthon at death; in extremely rare cases the Luminors transfer a mortal hero's soul into a new Alchemical gem instead (a failure-prone process that confuses genealogy tags). Players spend no Background points for an Autochthonian character to have a soulgem - it is assumed automatically.
cost: Artifact •• (implanted at birth at no player cost; see notes).
compatibility: Every Autochthonian citizen, mortal and Alchemical alike.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Soulgem', p. 186-187 (PDF 187-188); visually cross-checked against the rendered page. Classified reference-only rather than selectable because the book explicitly states players spend no Background points for it and every citizen is assumed to already have one - it is not a purchasable choice, unlike the other Artifact-rated items in this section. Cross-referenced to the pre-existing alchemical-life-and-death row (Chapter Two), which covers the same diamond soulgem from the post-Incapacitated-dissolution angle; this row adds the mortal-soulgem lore, caste color-coding, and the artifact's own combat/durability statistics.

name: Industrial Exoskeleton
summary: A 12-foot humanoid powered-armor frame that a mortal or low-Essence Alchemical straps into (via a painful but non-damaging neural-jack process) to massively augment Strength and gain heavy protection, at the cost of speed and constant maintenance.
mechanics: Piloting requires five minutes to strap in and commit 8 motes (or 2 Willpower for non-Essence users) plus an installed two-dot Essence capacitor. Augmented Strength: adds 12 to the pilot's effective Strength for lifting/breaking/damage purposes; joints can lock to hold a lifted object indefinitely. Protection: armored models give soak 12L/12B (hardness 6L/6B), mobility penalty -8, fatigue value 2; unarmored low-hazard models give soak 6L/6B (no hardness), mobility penalty -3, fatigue value 1. Slow: armored models halve ground speed and cannot jump or climb; lighter models reduce ground/climbing speed to 3/4 normal and halve jump distance; neither model can swim (both sink). Upkeep: needs recalibration by a technician (Lore, Occult, and a pertinent Craft at •••) every 25 hours of use, losing 1 point of its Strength bonus per 5 hours overdue (paralyzed once the bonus hits 0); routine maintenance is an hour of work plus Resources ••• in tools, with every fifth maintenance also requiring Resources ••• (•••• outside a large Creation city) in replacement parts.
cost: Artifact •••; requires an installed two-dot Essence capacitor.
compatibility: Mortals or Essence 2-3 Alchemical Exalted.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Autochthonian Technology' -> 'Industrial Exoskeleton', p. 187 (PDF 188); visually cross-checked against the rendered page. Its stat-table entries (Armored Industrial Exoskeleton and Industrial Exoskeleton) appear in the Autochthonian Weapons and Armor table, p. 192/PDF 193, folded into this row's mechanics rather than duplicated as a separate row.

name: Warfare (Autochthonian military technology overview)
summary: A framing overview of Autochthonian military technology and doctrine: roughly comparable to the early Dragon-Blooded Shogunate or Second Age Jadeborn, emphasizing tunnel/bottleneck warfare over open-field battles, with standard infantry issue of a reinforced buff jacket, rubbery bodysuit, filter mask or respirator module, opaque goggles or arc protectors/light-amplification visors, shields, and crossbows.
mechanics: Alchemical Exalted invariably field artifact weapons and gear early on, gradually internalizing a preferred arsenal as implanted Charms as they age; Essence 6-7 Alchemicals generally need warstrider-scaled weapons (though they can still wield smaller items via tentacle appendages). Their favored armor is an artifact buff jacket or reinforced buff jacket worn over implanted Charm-armor; those on covert missions favor fiber-weave shirts or their own Charms instead of visible artifact gear.
compatibility: Any character; sets the baseline equipment loadout referenced by the more specific weapon/armor rows that follow.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Warfare' section introduction, p. 187-188 (PDF 188-189); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Crossbows (Autochthonian varieties)
summary: Autochthonia's dominant ranged weapon family (conventional bows are nearly unknown there): personal crossbows, wrist-mounted assassin's models, emplacement-only siege crossbows, and the artifact-grade assault crossbow favored by Alchemicals, firing mostly armor-piercing 'target' bolts (effective against metal-skinned gremlins) alongside rarer broadhead and spring-tipped 'razor' bolts.
mechanics: Crossbow damage does not depend on the user's Strength, letting even weak or untrained users hit as hard as a trained archer. All crossbows are slow to reload (rate 1, or 1/10 for the emplacement-only siege model) and have relatively poor range; neither Exceptional-quality crafting nor Archery Charms can improve their rate unless a Charm is specifically built for that purpose. Razor bolts (spring-loaded tips that open into a three-bladed claw in flight) use the same rules as frog-crotch arrows against flesh but are useless against hard targets. Assault Crossbow: Accuracy +3, Damage 8L, Rate 1, Range 250, Str 1 minimum, Artifact ••, 5-mote attunement, generally shares powerbow-style Magical Material bonuses (jade models add +2 speed and 30 yards range instead of a rate bonus). Base statistics from the Autochthonian Weapons and Armor table: Crossbow (Acc +0, Dmg 5L, Rate 1, Range 125, Str 1, Resources ••), Hand Crossbow (Acc +0, Dmg 3L, Rate 2, Range 75, Resources •••), Siege Crossbow (Acc +0, Dmg 8L, Rate 1/10, Range 250, emplacement only, Resources •••), Warstrider Crossbow (Acc +0**, Dmg 8L, Rate 1, Range 250, Str 12, Resources ••••), Warstrider Onslaught Crossbow (Acc +2**, Dmg 16L, Rate 1, Range 450, Str 12, Artifact •••).
cost: Resources •• or ••• for mundane models, or Artifact •• for the assault crossbow.
compatibility: Any character; the assault crossbow is specifically an Alchemical weapon of choice, though Alchemicals more often favor their own Charm-based ranged weapons (Essence cannons, pneumatic bows) instead.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Warfare' -> 'Crossbows', p. 188-189 (PDF 189-190), with statistics from the 'Autochthonian Weapons and Armor' table, p. 192 (PDF 193); visually cross-checked against both rendered pages.

name: Fiber-Weave Bodysuit
summary: A supple, chain-shirt-equivalent light armor woven from high-quality fiber-weave textile threaded with Magical Material nodes, thin enough to wear discreetly under ordinary clothing; an upgraded Artifact •• version additionally functions as an Omnimodal Wardrobe Unit.
mechanics: Requires a 3-mote commitment. Grants an additional special property beyond its base soak: lethal piercing attacks based on kinetic penetration do not halve the armor's soak unless their raw damage is at least twice the armor's base lethal soak (before Magical Material bonuses). Benefits normally from its Magical Material (tempered Autochthonian adamant grants +3L soak and a -1 mobility-penalty reduction). The Artifact •• version adds every Omnimodal Wardrobe Unit property except that artifact's own soak bonus, for the same 3-mote commitment, letting an Alchemical always be armored regardless of the clothing shape currently worn - but it cannot be worn under other armor. Base statistics: soak 5L/3B, no hardness, -0 mobility penalty, 0 fatigue value.
compatibility: Any character; favored by Alchemicals on covert missions instead of visible artifact armor.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Warfare' -> 'Fiber-Weave Bodysuit', p. 189-190 (PDF 190-191), with base statistics from the 'Autochthonian Weapons and Armor' table, p. 192 (PDF 193); visually cross-checked against both rendered pages.

name: Gyroscopic Chakram
summary: The most widely used and feared thrown weapon of the Alchemical Exalted: a six-holed metal throwing disk that deploys spinning blades and homing clockwork in flight, banking to relentlessly pursue its target and returning to its owner's hand after each attempt, with a distinct bonus power for each of the six Magical Materials.
mechanics: Attuned for 5 motes. Acts at initiative 20 with a 10-dice pool (accuracy included) every turn it hunts a missed target, continuing until it hits or botches (striking an unintended target and lodging on a botch, requiring manual retrieval); its owner may abort the attack as a reflexive action to recall it early. Maximum range from the owner is 90 yards; it returns instantly on a hit or on any non-dodge/non-parry miss, or at the end of the turn otherwise. Magical Material powers: Orichalcum adds 1 to the difficulty of dodges/parries against it and returns instantly rather than at turn's end; Moonsilver can fold to coin-size for concealment and its blades extend up to a foot for +1 damage; Jade adds 2 damage against inanimate objects and repeatedly strikes such targets (even after hitting) until fully destroyed or recalled; Starmetal treats botches as simple failures, adds 1 accuracy, and never strikes an unintended target even when redirected by hostile magic; Soulsteel hunts and repeatedly attacks living/animate Essence-bearing prey until recalled, botched, or its quarry dies; Adamant inflicts piercing damage but is rarely used due to its high attunement cost. May also be wielded in close combat as a saw with normal Magical Material melee bonuses (adamant inflicts piercing damage there too). A warstrider-scaled version (yard diameter, 8-mote commitment) also exists. Statistics: as a thrown weapon, Speed +1, Accuracy +1, Damage +4L, Defense +2, minimum Str 1/Dex 3, Artifact ••• (Exalted Power Combat: Rate 6).
compatibility: Any Alchemical caste; Alchemicals of the 'wrong' caste for a given Magical Material double the attunement cost as normal.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Warfare' -> 'Gyroscopic Chakram', p. 189-190 (PDF 190-191), with statistics from the 'Autochthonian Weapons and Armor' table, p. 192 (PDF 193); visually cross-checked against all three rendered pages.

name: Thousand Wounds Gear Style
summary: A Celestial-level martial art unique to the Alchemical Exalted, built entirely around paired gyroscopic chakram use; practitioners are noted for calculated efficiency at killing or maiming with the disks and for interposing them defensively as improvised shields.
compatibility: Alchemical Exalted with Perfected Lotus Matrix installed and gyroscopic chakrams available.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Warfare' -> 'Gyroscopic Chakram', p. 190 (PDF 191); visually cross-checked against the rendered page. Classified reference-only, matching the existing alchemical-martial-artists row's precedent: the book names this style and its narrative flavor but gives none of its actual Charms, so there is nothing here to mark selectable beyond noting the style's existence.

name: Beam Klave
summary: The signature melee weapon of the Alchemical Exalted: an unassuming crystal-tipped cylinder that extends a glowing three-foot Essence blade on command, functioning as a daiklave with the destructive bonus power of burning through whatever it strikes or parries - available as an equivalent conversion of every basic Magical Material melee weapon type.
mechanics: Attuned for 3 motes; activating the blade for a scene costs an additional 5 motes. Blade color follows its Magical Material (orichalcum gold-white, moonsilver pale silver-blue, jade the shade of its jade type, starmetal shifting crimson-to-violet, soulsteel dried-blood red-black with a shadow contrail, adamant nearly invisible pale-blue prisms). Shares daiklave statistics and Magical Material bonuses (adamant inflicts piercing damage). Special powers: if it parries a non-magical weapon and scores any success, the parried weapon is destroyed (natural weapons like claws/fists may be severed from extras, though more significant characters instead take two soakable lethal levels); if a non-magical weapon parries it and scores a success, that weapon is likewise destroyed and all its parry successes are halved thereafter; on a successful hit against non-magical armor, the raw damage permanently reduces the armor's soak (both bashing and lethal) to a minimum of zero, destroying the armor entirely if both reach zero; against inanimate targets it works the same way (charring/gashing without full destruction until health levels are exhausted), reducing soak only in the struck area for larger structures. Magical weapons take no damage from contact with a beam klave. Other daiklave-family weapons have beam equivalents at the same rules (grimcleaver -> beam axe; dire lance -> beam lance, treated as an unpowered javelin when off; razor claws -> paired beam talons), all at Artifact rating two dots higher than their mundane equivalent with the same 3-mote attunement/5-mote activation. A warstrider-scaled beam klave also exists (Artifact •••••, 4-mote attunement plus normal warstrider-weapon commitment). Statistics: Speed +3, Accuracy +2, Damage +5L, Defense +2, minimum Str 2, Artifact •••• (Exalted Power Combat: Rate 5).
cost: Artifact •••• (or higher for warstrider scale/other weapon-type conversions); 3-mote attunement plus 5 motes per scene to activate.
compatibility: Any Alchemical caste.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Warfare' -> 'Beam Klave', p. 190-192 (PDF 191-193), with statistics from the 'Autochthonian Weapons and Armor' table, p. 192 (PDF 193); visually cross-checked against all three rendered pages. 'The Secret of Soulsteel' sidebar sharing this page (explaining how soulsteel exists in Autochthonia without a Labyrinth) was reviewed and intentionally excluded as pure narrative/lore with no independent game mechanics.

name: Transportation (Autochthonian mass and personal transit overview)
summary: A framing note on Autochthonian transit: most travel within cities is on foot, since Autochthonia's only steeds are automatons or lesser machine gods (usually requisitioned as Alchemical familiars), so the Machine God's society instead developed the exotic clockwork/Essence-driven conveyances detailed in this section.
compatibility: Any character.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Transportation' section introduction, p. 192 (PDF 193); visually cross-checked against the rendered page.

name: Pneumatic Trams
summary: Tube-shaped subway trains that provide Autochthonia's primary mass transit: vertical arrangements serve as elevators linking a city's tiers, lateral trams move passengers within a tier, and much larger cargo trams connect entire cities and nations along paramagnetic-accelerated arterial highways.
mechanics: Intracity trams top out around 50 miles per hour; cargo trams can reach 200 miles per hour once inside airtight highway tubes. Trains lack life support (excluding unbreathing Alchemicals as passengers, as a precaution against dissident stowaways). Fixed-path trams need no skill or rolls to operate, though anyone unable to read Autochthonic pictogram instructions needs an Intelligence + Lore roll (difficulty 2) to figure out the controls. Arterial highways have many branching paths and require actual piloting (handled with the Sail Ability) to avoid disastrous crashes.
compatibility: Any character; the standard means of intercity and intracity travel.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Transportation' -> 'Pneumatic Trams', p. 192-193 (PDF 193-194); visually cross-checked against both rendered pages.

name: Mechanical Rickshaw
summary: A two-passenger, Essence-driven wheeled vehicle used by Autochthonia's high-status or infirm citizens for personal transit, powered by rear-mounted Essence-gathering sails and a two-dot Essence capacitor; a rarer insectile variant trades wheels for skittering legs to cross rough terrain and shallow liquid.
mechanics: Driven with side-mounted control levers; anyone with dots in Ride is assumed to know the controls, otherwise an Intelligence + Lore roll (difficulty 3) is needed to figure them out. A single successful Wits + Ride roll (difficulty 1) at the start of a smooth, obstacle-free journey suffices; maneuvers or combat-turn driving need new rolls each turn (Storyteller-assigned difficulty 1-5). Maximum speed 30 mph (42 yards/turn), requiring generally level ground. Statistics: 10 health levels, hardened soak 6L/10B (of which 1L/3B counts as armor), ignoring attacks whose raw damage is below its soak; treats aggravated damage as lethal; not an inanimate object for Charm purposes, so damage must be rolled rather than auto-applied. Gives 25% cover from the front, 50% from other directions. Accrues one unsoakable bashing-damage level per 10 hours of operation (8 hours for the insectile variant); at 1/3, 1/2, and 3/4 health lost it suffers cumulative speed and handling penalties, and losing its last level from bashing damage causes it to lose power and stop, while losing its last level to lethal damage causes a crash or explosive motor failure (minimum 10L to occupants). Repair: lethal damage needs Resources •• and three hours from a technician with Lore ••, Occult ••, and Craft (Clockwork or similar) ••• (less-qualified technicians may attempt it via Intelligence + Craft at a scaled difficulty penalty, risking further unsoakable damage on failure, lethal on a botch); bashing damage needs only Resources • and an hour.
cost: Artifact ••; requires an installed two-dot Essence capacitor.
compatibility: Any character; typically used by high-status or infirm Autochthonian citizens.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Transportation' -> 'Mechanical Rickshaws, Skimmercraft and Aerial Skiffs', p. 193-194 (PDF 194-195); visually cross-checked against both rendered pages.

name: Skimmercraft
summary: A rarer and more valuable ovoid hovering vehicle resembling a metal beetle's carapace, seating up to three human-sized passengers (or two Essence 4-5 Alchemicals/heavily armored mortals) and hovering up to two yards above any horizontal surface.
mechanics: Travels up to 60 mph (84 yards/turn) using paramagnetic drives, hovering at a maximum altitude of two yards; if placed higher (e.g. driving off a cliff), it descends gently at one yard per turn until it reaches that height. Grants one extra die to all handling rolls for its inertia-defying maneuverability. Gives total cover from directly below, 25% from above, 50% from all sides; passengers at maximum altitude count as being in a howdah for attack purposes. Statistics: soak 6L/12B (1L/5B counts as armor), 12 health levels; accrues wear damage only after 50 hours since last maintenance, then one bashing level plus one more per five subsequent hours. Requires a three-dot Essence capacitor. Otherwise follows the same rules as a mechanical rickshaw.
cost: Artifact •••; requires an installed three-dot Essence capacitor.
compatibility: Any character; carries up to two Essence 4-5 Alchemicals or heavily armored mortals, or three ordinary human-sized passengers.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Transportation' -> 'Mechanical Rickshaws, Skimmercraft and Aerial Skiffs', p. 193-194 (PDF 194-195); visually cross-checked against both rendered pages.

name: Aerial Skiff
summary: The most powerful clockwork vehicle in Autochthonia: an elongated skimmercraft-derived flying craft with four dragonfly-like paramagnetic 'wings,' able to hover or fly without altitude restriction and carry several Alchemicals or many mortal passengers; variants include the deep-sea oil diver submersible and combat-oriented reconnaissance/transport models.
mechanics: Can hover or fly up to 80 mph (112 yards/turn) with no altitude restriction, carrying up to five Essence 4-5 Alchemicals/heavily armored mortals, eight mortals comfortably, or up to 12 mortals if cramped. Statistics: soak 10L/15B (3L/5B counts as armor), 15 health levels; a 30-hour maintenance-free grace period, then one damage level per five hours of flight; requires a four-dot Essence capacitor; repair needs Lore •••, Occult •••, and a Craft at •••••. The oil diver variant (Artifact ••••) is a fully sealed, deep-sea-pressure-rated submersible holding an hour of air per mortal passenger (irrelevant to Alchemicals); it is neutrally buoyant with adjustable buoyancy, uses twin Essence-driven impeller jets to travel up to 40 mph (56 yards/turn) through liquid, and navigates via echolocation-generated light-projected maps (half a mile ahead/quarter mile all directions normally, dropping to 50 yards running silent); otherwise it duplicates aerial skiff rules. Combat-oriented recon and transport variants of both skimmercraft and aerial skiff exist at one Artifact rating and Essence-capacitor tier higher, adding +2L/+2B armored soak plus one further feature: reconnaissance models add a cloaking device duplicating the Dynamic Cloaking Module Charm while active (each hour cloaked counts double against maintenance intervals); transport models grow to nine-yard trilobite-like hulls with an extra +2L/+2B natural soak, five more health levels, full cover for all occupants, half speed, a one-die handling penalty (using Sail instead of Ride), and a rear cargo bay holding 15 Essence 4-5 Alchemicals or heavily armored mortals (two warstriders or Essence 6-7 Alchemicals curled up), 20 mortals comfortably, or 30 cramped, opening via petaling doors or a single ramp.
cost: Artifact •••• (••••• for the oil diver or for combat-oriented variants); requires an installed four-dot (or higher, for combat variants) Essence capacitor.
compatibility: Any character; the largest personal/small-group Autochthonian clockwork vehicle short of a warstrider.
notes: Chapter Four: Miracles of the Machine God, 'Transportation' -> 'Mechanical Rickshaws, Skimmercraft and Aerial Skiffs', p. 194-195 (PDF 195-196); visually cross-checked against both rendered pages. The Exalted Power Combat Statistics table sharing p. 195/PDF 196 (Alpha Custodian, Arc Tender, Cogwheel Dragon, Design Weaver, Destroyer, Fix Beetle, Gezlak, Gremlin, Lapidary, Slacstag) was reviewed and intentionally excluded as pure Storyteller-side creature/NPC combat statistics with no character-creation relevance.

name: Steamcar, Refurbished
summary: A large, eight-legged, multi-terrain steel cargo/troop transport with red jade and orichalcum 'circuitry,' originally built to haul heavy replacement parts across Autochthonia's conduits; the Five Sodalities refurbish one to carry the Chapter Six expedition (and up to 20 passengers) into Creation in search of the Eye of Autochthon.
mechanics: Suspended on eight short multi-segmented legs that turn and rotate independently to handle both Autochthonian conduits and Creation's uneven terrain; burns any combustible fuel in a rear-mounted Essence-powered furnace, transmitting power to the legs through jade/orichalcum circuitry. A driver steers with two control levers using Dexterity + Ride; understanding the exotic controls requires Craft (First Age Weapons) •• and Lore •, and non-Autochthonians suffer a two-die penalty. Equipped with ports for Alchemicals to use the Electroneural Control Spurs and Universal Pilot Key Charms, plus a built-in Portable Nutriment Recycling Engine to feed passengers. Very noisy (audible from about a mile away). Travels 80 mph in clear terrain, 60 mph in difficult terrain, 30 mph in mountainous terrain. Statistics: soak 8L/15B, 8 health levels to damage and 30 to destroy. Needs at least an hour's maintenance every 500 miles traveled (minimum Craft (Large Mechanism Repair) ••• and Lore •• for Autochthonians, or Craft (First Age Weapons) ••••• and Lore •••• for Creation dwellers); missing maintenance reduces speed by 10 mph, and once speed drops to 30 mph the Storyteller rolls a die every hour, with a result of 6 or higher causing a breakdown (repaired with Intelligence + Craft (Large Mechanism Repair or First Age Weapons) at difficulty 3, taking half a day and permanently reducing top speed by 10 mph). A full day of maintenance restores the steamcar to full speed, minus any permanent reduction from prior breakdowns. Carries up to 20 passengers with no cargo.
cost: Artifact N/A (a shared expedition/cargo vehicle rather than a personally rated Artifact; comes with Electroneural Control Spurs/Universal Pilot Key Charm ports and a built-in Portable Nutriment Recycling Engine).
compatibility: Any character; built for Autochthonian expedition/cargo use, with Charm ports specifically for installed Alchemicals.
notes: Chapter Six: The Quest for the Great Source, in the sidebar introducing the Sodalities' refurbished steamcar used to carry the Chapter Six expedition into Creation, printed p. 238 (PDF 239); visually cross-checked against the rendered page. Unlike Chapter Four's Autochthonian Technology/Transportation section (mechanical rickshaw, skimmercraft, aerial skiff), this vehicle appears within the adventure text itself rather than the equipment chapter, but gives the same kind of concrete, player-usable vehicle stat block (soak, health levels, speed, maintenance/repair rules), so it is inventoried here alongside them.
