This is the only genuinely player-facing character-creation-relevant item found across Chapters Five through Seven (printed pp. 196-297/PDF 197-298); see rulesNotes in source-manifest.json for the full review scope and what was intentionally excluded.

name: Ambidextrous
summary: For one point, negates offhand penalties; the two-point ("omniambidextrous") version also lets the character hold weapons/tools with their feet as readily as their hands. Lunars pay only one point for the omniambidextrous version.
mechanics: For one point, the character can use both hands equally well and never suffers an offhand penalty for any task. Characters with the two-point version of this Merit can also hold weapons and tools with their feet as readily as their hands, an adaptation common among the Haltans of the East and highly useful for characters who have lost the use of both hands. Matters of balance and common sense still apply, however, so omniambidextrous characters will not be able to walk around carrying objects with every hand and foot simultaneously. Lunars pay only one point to be omniambidextrous.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; the source names only Lunars for the reduced 1-pt. omniambidextrous cost, so Alchemicals purchase either version at the standard 1- or 2-pt. price.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 18/PDF 19), cross-checked against Alchemical's own rules: a vat-built chassis with paired manipulator limbs is fully compatible with this Merit's offhand/foot-dexterity effects; no construct-specific exclusion applies.

name: Acute Sense
summary: One or more senses heightened to superhuman sensitivity; the 1-pt. version adds dice to Perception/Awareness rolls involving that sense but risks sensory overload, while the 3-pt. version grants preternatural acuity at the cost of being sensitive to other data.
mechanics: The character has one or more senses heightened to superhuman sensitivity, for a cost of one bonus point each. The character adds two dice to any Perception and/or Awareness dice pool involving a heightened sense, but his player must make a reflexive Wits + Awareness roll at standard difficulty whenever that sense experiences extremely intense stimuli. Failure inflicts a one-die penalty to all actions requiring concentration until the stimulus abates or the acclimation roll succeeds on a successive turn. If a character instead pays three bonus points per sense, the sense is heightened to preternatural acuity. Bonus points awarded by a heightened sense do not aid in resisting sensory-overload rolls.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given. Stacks with Special Sense as written.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 18/PDF 19). An Alchemical's installed sensory equipment (see this family's own Sensory and Spiritual Charms, e.g. Optical Enhancement) is a Charm-Slot investment, not a Background/Merit purchase, so this Merit remains a distinct, cheaper way to sharpen one baseline sense without spending a Charm Slot; no construct-specific restriction applies.

name: Double-Jointed
summary: Contortionist flexibility: the 1-pt. version adds a die to grappling/Athletics/Larceny rolls benefiting from flexibility; the 3-pt. version adds two dice and grants near-impossible feats of contortion (Lunars pay only two points for this greater version).
mechanics: For a cost of one point, the character is unusually supple and capable of remarkable feats of contortion. Add one die to such an individual's grappling rolls, as well as to any Athletics or Larceny rolls where such flexibility proves advantageous. Characters with the three-point version of this Merit are uncanny contortionists, capable of seemingly impossible feats. These freakish acrobats add two dice to all rolls benefiting from flexibility and can bend every finger to the wrist, lock their legs straight up, maintain indefinite splits, dislocate and reset joints painlessly and slip free of most conventional restraints or a Dexterity + Athletics roll at a difficulty set by the Storyteller. Lunar Exalted pay only two points for the greater version of this Merit.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; the source names only Lunars for the reduced 2-pt. cost of the greater version, so Alchemicals pay the standard 1- or 3-pt. price.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 19/PDF 20). A Moonsilver Caste's fluid, 'grown-rather-than-forged' chassis (see moonsilver-caste) makes this Merit an especially natural fit, but nothing restricts it to that Caste; any Alchemical Caste may purchase it.

name: Pain Tolerance
summary: Characters with this Merit can shrug off injuries that would leave most individuals unconscious or writhing in agony, at increasing tiers of pain-immunity and Awareness-roll cost.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit can shrug off injuries that would leave most individuals unconscious or writhing in agony. For a cost of three points, but this increases the difficulty of any Awareness rolls based on touch by one. Five points allow the character to ignore two dice of wound penalties but also increase the difficulty of touch-based Awareness by like amount. The character feels nothing. Even if mortally wounded, he may continue to act without penalties for injuries that do not involve actual maiming. If maimed, the character can briefly jog on broken limbs, swing his shattered stump of an arm like a club and perform other acts of relentless torture. The downside to seven-point resilience is that the character automatically fails rolls that require a sense of touch and must visually inspect his body for injuries that require treatment to prevent infection or bleeding to death. The effects of Pain Tolerance are not cumulative with Charms and other magic that negate wound penalties. Only the most powerful effects apply. Pain Tolerance is particularly common among ghosts and deathknights with corpse-like flesh.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; the source names ghosts and Abyssal deathknights as typical bearers of this Merit but does not restrict it away from any other splat.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 19/PDF 20). Cross-checked against Alchemical's own rules: an Alchemical's body is metal, crystal, and Magical Material rather than flesh, making a high tolerance for pain and injury a natural fit; no construct-specific restriction applies.

name: Large Size
summary: Characters are roughly 25 percent (4-pt.) or nearly twice (6-pt.) larger than average, gaining bonus health levels but suffering a Dexterity penalty for fine manipulation at the higher tier. For an Alchemical, this represents an unusually large vat-built chassis within her current Essence-tier size range, distinct from the separate size growth that comes from raising Essence itself.
mechanics: Characters with the four-point version of this Merit are roughly 25 percent larger than average, standing over seven feet tall and usually weighing in at 300 or more pounds. Such imposing bulk grants one additional -0 health level. For six points, the character is almost impossibly huge, standing eight to nine feet tall and weighing 500 or more pounds. Such characters receive one -0 level and one -1 level but lose one die from Dexterity rolls to use small weapons, writing instruments or other tools not designed for their massive hands. Unlike health levels bestowed by Charms, the added toughness afforded by this Merit is immediately evident to everyone. The character will certainly stand out in most crowds and may have to stoop to pass through doorways built for smaller individuals. Most characters have both Strength and Stamina rated at 3 or higher. Lunar Exalted with this Merit are proportionally larger in all forms and thus receive the extra health level(s) unless wearing another specific being's face as with Prey's Skin Disguise (see E:tL, p. 129). Large Size may also represent obese characters of normal stature, particularly when coupled with a low Dexterity.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals. The source's Lunar-specific clause (bonus health level(s) carrying into every form via Prey's Skin Disguise) does not apply to Alchemicals, who do not shapechange; instead an Alchemical's overall size is separately governed by her own Refitting/Essence Advancement rules (see alchemical-refitting-essence-and-evolution).
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). JUDGMENT CALL: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 19/PDF 20). Alchemicals already grow physically larger as their permanent Essence rises (Essence 4-5 reach 9-12 feet, Essence 6+ far larger still, per alchemical-refitting-essence-and-evolution), so this Merit is best read as representing an unusually large vat-built chassis WITHIN a given Essence tier's normal size range (e.g. a bulkier Essence 2-3 frame that still falls in the 6-7 foot human-size band), not a shortcut around the Essence-gated growth thresholds. Storytellers should keep the two systems distinct: this Merit's bonus health level(s) are a chassis-design choice at character creation, not a substitute for raising Essence.

name: Legendary Attribute
summary: Grants the potential to raise a Physical (or, in other versions, Social or Mental) Attribute one dot higher than the normal Essence-based cap; all Exalted (including Lunars) pay a reduced 3-pt. cost instead of the mortal 5-pt. cost.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have the potential to attain superhuman strength, speed or resilience in which they can attain a rating one dot higher than the normal limit imposed by their Essence allows. This may be done during character creation or after. For mortals and Exalted with Essence 1 to 5, this allows a rating of 6 in the chosen Attribute. Exalted with Essence 6 may raise the Attribute to 7, etc. Other versions of this Merit exist to accommodate Social and Mental Attributes. Such Legendary Attributes follow the same rules apart from being classified as Social or Mental Merits.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; the reduced 3-pt. cost applies to 'Exalted' generically, and Alchemicals are Exalted, so this discount applies to them.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 19/PDF 20). Applies to any of an Alchemical's nine Attributes (Caste, Favored, or otherwise) exactly as for other Exalted.

name: Special Resistance
summary: For every point invested, adds one die to Resistance/Endurance rolls versus poison or disease, or buys immunity to a specific poison/disease, or total immunity to all forms of injury for one point.
mechanics: For every point invested in this Merit, the character adds one die on applicable Resistance and Endurance rolls versus poison or disease. A character may not purchase more than five additional dice of either form of injury. Alternately, the character may have total immunity to a specific poison or disease for a cost of one point. The character will suffer no ill effects from that toxin or become sick from exposure to the malady. It is not possible to purchase immunity to infected wounds with this Merit. All forms of this Merit assume the character has built his Special Resistance through repeated exposure to the appropriate danger -- intentionally or otherwise.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). JUDGMENT CALL: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (pp. 19-20/PDF 20-21). Cross-checked against Alchemical's own Artificial Metabolism rules (alchemical-artificial-metabolism), which already grant Alchemicals blanket immunity to inhaled toxins and non-magical disease/infection. This Merit remains meaningfully purchasable on top of that baseline for resistance to ingested/injected/contact poisons and magical diseases, which Artificial Metabolism does not cover; a Storyteller should not allow it to buy immunity to something already covered for free by that row.

name: Special Sense
summary: One or more senses that process stimuli beyond the normal ranges for the character's species (e.g. heat vision, ultrasonic hearing, pheromone-like smell); no fixed mechanical effect, at Storyteller discretion, and stacks with Acute Sense.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have one or more senses that process stimuli beyond the normal ranges for their species. For example, a character may be able to detect heat as well as visible light, to hear high frequency pitches like a dog or an uncapped Demesne or an especially pronounced Lunar Tell. There is no fixed mechanical effect for this broader sensitivity, but Storytellers should certainly accommodate the character's gift when narrating sensory details. If this Merit is taken in conjunction with the appropriate Acute Sense Merit (see p. 18), the character's heightened awareness also applies to the unusual ranges of that sense. Every significant expansion of a single sense's range costs two bonus points.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; explicitly stacks with Acute Sense.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 20/PDF 21). The source text's Lunar-flavored examples ('an uncapped Demesne,' 'an especially pronounced Lunar Tell') are flavor only and do not restrict eligibility; an Alchemical's Special Sense would typically originate from an unusual installed sensor material or a quirk of her Magical Material composition instead.

name: Common Sense
summary: A decent grasp of what constitutes a good idea, a bad idea and a very bad idea; won't rush into calamity without recognizing her folly.
mechanics: A character with this Merit has a decent grasp of what constitutes a good idea, a bad idea and a very bad idea. She won't rush into calamity without recognizing her folly, though nothing prevents her from ignoring her better judgment. This Merit chiefly exists to warn inexperienced players about the obvious dangers implicit in a particular course of action. The Storyteller should give fair warning in such cases, though he needn't belabor the point.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 20/PDF 21).

name: Internal Compass
summary: Uncanny sense of direction; gains one extra die to all rolls to navigate a ship or find her way through a maze.
mechanics: The character has an uncanny sense of direction and gains one extra die to all rolls to navigate a ship or find her way through a maze. She can orient herself with regard to the cardinal directions of Creation or the Underworld with a Wits + Awareness roll at standard difficulty.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 20/PDF 21). Cross-checked against Alchemical's own rules: usable in Autochthonia's tunnels and industrial strata exactly as in Creation or the Underworld.

name: Eidetic Recall
summary: Nearly perfect memory of everything witnessed, at a cost of one bonus point per sense the character can infallibly recall; Alchemical Exalted pay a flat 3-pt. cost for full Eidetic Recall of all five senses.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have a nearly perfect memory of everything they have witnessed, at a cost of one bonus point for every sense the character can infallibly recall. It is assumed that this record is always functioning, though the Storyteller may require a Wits + Awareness roll to memorize and remember details observed in moments of intense stress (such as combat). Alchemical Exalted pay a flat cost of three points for full Eidetic Recall of all five senses.
compatibility: Alchemical Exalted are explicitly named for a discounted, flat 3-pt. cost for the full (all five senses) version, instead of the normal per-sense cost of up to 5 points that other character types pay.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). DIRECTLY ALCHEMICAL-RELEVANT: the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 20/PDF 21) names Alchemical Exalted by name for this discount. Cross-checked against Alchemical's own Cognitive Charms tree (e.g. Eidetic Processing Core), which provides a Charm-based memory-enhancement option; this Merit remains a distinct, cheaper, non-Charm-Slot alternative.

name: Virtue Specialty
summary: Moral fortitude strengthened under specific conditions, adding dice to Virtue rolls equal to half the points invested when a specialty circumstance is invoked.
mechanics: A character with this Merit finds his moral resolve strengthened under certain conditions. For example, a meek villager may stand as a lion in defense of his family, and a celibate monk may train himself to better resist the lure of flesh. The character receives a number of additional dice to applicable Virtue rolls equal to half the number of points invested in this Merit. However, this also increases the difficulty where the Storyteller wishes to test against his moral judgment. Regardless of allocation and the number of times this Merit is purchased, a character may not have more than one specialty dice for a Virtue. This limitation duplicates the restrictions on specialties for Abilities. As always, Storytellers will veto any specialty deemed too broad.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 21/PDF 22). Applies to any of an Alchemical's four Virtues exactly as for other Exalted.

name: Driving Passion
summary: A Nature-tied all-consuming goal (liberating a nation, avenging a loved one's murder) that grants a bonus die whenever the character takes action directly furthering it; resolving or betraying it changes the character's Traits.
mechanics: Characters with a Driving Passion live for a cause directly tied to their Nature (most commonly Architect or Visionary). The cause can be anything of any scope, from liberating the Threshold from the tyranny of the Realm to avenging a loved one's murder to becoming a peerless master swordsman. Whenever the character takes action directly furthering this goal, his player adds one additional die to the roll involved. The Storyteller remains the final arbiter of what situations merit this bonus. A character seeking vengeance for his dead wife would certainly gain dice when searching for clues, disputing the murderer's flunkies and the final dramatic duel with the killer. However, the character would not gain a bonus in combat with roadside brigands on the way to the murderer's home city because the combat is only tangentially connected to the Driving Passion. If a character actually resolves or fulfills her Driving Passion, she immediately loses this Merit and gains six experience points.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given, and the source's own examples (Architect, Visionary) are two of the eight Natures Autochthonian society favors for Alchemicals per this family's own character-creation overview.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 21/PDF 22). Cross-checked against alchemical-character-creation-overview, which lists Architect and Visionary among the Natures Autochthonian society favors -- a strong thematic fit for this Merit.

name: Tactical Instincts
summary: Intuitive grasp of tactics: with a Wits + Lore roll, instantly discerns weaknesses/distribution of forces in a battle or game board, building a bonus pool usable to aid Wits/Presence rolls to command forces.
mechanics: The character has an intuitive understanding of tactics, from the myriad stratagems of Gateway to the most elaborate battlefield formations. With a Wits + Lore roll at standard difficulty, the character, upon glancing at any contested forces or the arrangement of a game board, immediately discerns all weaknesses and distribution of strength. Successes accumulate as a pool of extra dice the character's player may subsequently apply to any Lore rolls to devise a winning strategy or Presence rolls to command forces in pursuit of that victory. Other pertinent rolls may benefit from this pool with Storyteller permission. No more than three of these dice may be applied to any single roll, and bonus dice remain unused until the end of the scene. Characters may not reevaluate the tactical scenario to refresh their bonus pool until they use it again.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 21/PDF 22).

name: True Love
summary: A deep and abiding romance with a partner who reciprocates; adds one die to rolls in defense of or aid of that loved one, and if the lover perishes the character may substitute this bond for Conviction to regain Willpower.
mechanics: A character with this Merit shares a deep and abiding romance with a partner who reciprocates that affection. This commitment adds one die to all rolls in defense or aid of that loved one. As always, the Storyteller remains the final authority of what actions receive this bonus. The player of a character with this Merit may also roll (Compassion + 1) in place of Conviction for her character to regain Willpower each morning, if so desired. If the character's lover perished, she immediately loses this Merit, but she may subsume her feelings into an appropriate Driving Passion, with Storyteller approval. Such passions often focus on completing the work of the deceased, honoring her memory or avenging her untimely demise.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). JUDGMENT CALL: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 21/PDF 22). Alchemicals are soulless-seeming constructs, but each carries a genuine human-derived soul/persona housed within a mechanical body (see clarity-trait) and retains the full Virtue set, including Compassion, needed to root this Merit; nothing in Alchemical's own rules bars romantic attachment.

name: True Paragon
summary: The character exudes formal-code honor and nobility; may spend bonus points/experience to raise Virtues above the normal 5 maximum (up to 6), and may roll her highest Virtue in place of Conviction to regain Willpower while asleep. Restricted to characters with the Paragon Nature.
mechanics: The character exudes honor and nobility, either from a formal code or an instinctive fulfillment of what she believes is right. As a result, she may spend bonus and experience points to raise any Virtue to a rating of 6. Characters with this Merit capable of raising their Virtues above 5 for other reasons instead add one to their permitted maximum. This Merit does not allow permanent Willpower to exceed a rating of 10. In addition, the player of a character with this Merit may choose to roll her character's highest Virtue in place of the standard Conviction roll for her character to regain Willpower after sleeping. Only characters with the Paragon Nature may purchase or retain this Merit. Characters who betray their code lose this Merit without compensation.
compatibility: Any character type with the Paragon Nature, including Alchemicals; the restriction is by Nature, not by Exalt type, and Paragon is explicitly one of the Natures Autochthonian society favors (with its own local reading, 'Paragon of Integration').
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). STRONG THEMATIC FIT: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 21/PDF 22). Cross-checked against alchemical-character-creation-overview, which singles out Paragon as the Autochthonian ideal Nature and even gives it a unique local gloss; an Alchemical with the Paragon Nature is squarely the intended audience for this Merit.

name: Jack of All Trades
summary: Broad basis of knowledge and skill, with an almost preternatural ability to adapt understanding to new purposes; suffers no penalty to Attribute rolls lacking the required Ability for a dice pool.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have a broad basis of knowledge and skill to draw upon and an almost preternatural ability to adapt their understanding to new purposes and situations. They suffer no penalty to Attribute rolls lacking the required Ability for a dice pool.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (pp. 21-22/PDF 22-23).

name: Born to Rule
summary: Conveys authority in every gesture and inflection; adds one die to all Social rolls when interacting with an acknowledged inferior.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit convey authority in every gesture and inflection, most likely as a result of aristocratic upbringing. Others develop such majesty through the practice of leadership or upon receiving the mantle of Exaltation. Regardless, this Merit adds one die to all Social rolls when interacting with an acknowledged inferior (as determined by the Storyteller).
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 22/PDF 23). Fits Alchemical concepts with rank in the Tripartite (see backing-background-altered) exactly as it fits any authority figure.

name: Enchanting Feature
summary: A striking, attractive feature or strong presence the character can exploit to add one die to pertinent Social rolls, as decided by the Storyteller.
mechanics: Something about the character is striking and attractive or at least conveys a strong presence. He may have deep eyes that seem to hold the secrets of the universe or a voice that resonates like the basso rumble of a lion. Whenever the character can exploit this feature, he adds one die to all pertinent Social rolls, as decided by the Storyteller.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 22/PDF 23). Applies to an Alchemical's Appearance-based Social rolls exactly as for other Exalted; a striking installed-Charm ornamentation or Magical Material finish is a natural Alchemical framing for this Merit's 'striking feature.'

name: Innocuous
summary: The two-point version makes the character forgettable and hard to pick out of a crowd; the four-point (Supernatural) version cloaks the character's identity from memory almost entirely. The book explicitly bars Sidereal Exalted from purchasing either version, since their innate Arcane Fate already supersedes this Merit's effects.
mechanics: Characters with the two-point version of this Merit have an eerily unremarkable visage. Height, weight and build are all average, all plain. No one is apt to pick them from a crowd unless their skin and hair is dramatically different in hue than all the locals -- and, possibly, not even then. People are less likely to remember them at all if they do nothing to draw attention to themselves. Such everyman anonymity adds one die to pertinent Larceny and Stealth rolls and adds one to the difficulty of any casual pursuit or investigation of the character. This will not foil any serious inquiry, nor does it grant any bonus if the character is alone or does something memorable (such as showing any level of an anima banner). Characters must have Appearance 2 in order to purchase this version of Innocuous. The four-point version of Innocuous is a Supernatural Merit rather than Social. The character is not simply ordinary, but is cloaked in an aura of subtle obscurity. Those who witness and even interact with her find their memories blurred. They may recall the conversation, but not the person with whom they spoke. More astute characters might remember 'that girl' or maybe even 'that red-haired girl' if they are especially insightful, but that's about the best most can hope for. Mechanically, this more powerful version doubles the bonuses afforded by the lesser version of this Merit. Additionally, onlookers do not remember more than superficial details from interactions with the character without a Wits + Essence roll. The base difficulty of this roll is 6, reduced by 1 for every significant event that occurred with the character in the previous week. Once a witness pierces the anonymity, the difficulty of subsequent memory checks is the number of full weeks she has gone without interacting with the obscured character. This roll is made once a week, starting with the first full week of no contact. On a failure, existing memories of previous encounters with the obscured character blur and fade regardless of their significance. Magical beings (those with Essence 2+) indefinitely ignore the aura of anonymity after they pierce it once, but only if the hidden character has a lower permanent Essence. Unfortunately, magically cloaked characters have obvious difficulties forming relationships and may not have more than two Contacts, Mentor or any other socially dependent Backgrounds unless their associates are powerful magical beings assumed to have pierced the veil. Veiled characters may not have Followers, Henchman, a Cult, any form of Command or other Backgrounds contingent on being widely known without extremely unusual circumstances approved by the Storyteller. Sidereals may not purchase Innocuous in either version, as their innate Arcane Fate supersedes the Merit's effects. The effects of Innocuous do not stack with Charms and other magic that conceal identity. Only the most powerful effect applies.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; the source restricts only Sidereal Exalted from purchasing either version ('their innate Arcane Fate supersedes the Merit's effects'). No restriction is stated against Alchemicals.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (pp. 22-23/PDF 23-24). Note the source text's own caveat that the bonus grants 'no bonus if the character... does something memorable (such as showing any level of an anima banner)' -- directly relevant to Alchemicals, whose Anima Banner (alchemical-anima-banners-universal) can shut off concealment entirely at the 4+ mote display tier, exactly as the Merit's text already anticipates for anima-bearing Exalted generally.

name: Favor
summary: As a Merit, someone of roughly equal or greater power owes the character a favor, scaled 1-4 points by the severity/danger of the service that would repay it (2/4/6 points for minor/moderate/major favors owed by Yu-Shan's Celestial courts); as a Flaw, the character owes such a favor to someone else.
mechanics: If this Trait is a Merit, someone roughly equal or greater power owes the character a favor. The value of this Merit depends on the extent of service required to cancel the debt. For one point, the debtor must perform a task that might take a few days but would not place her in any foreseen danger or require her to go especially out of her way. For two points, the debtor must perform a service whose execution may involve considerable inconvenience but little danger. Three-point favors are quite serious, and may involve substantial risk of injury or other misfortune. Four-point favors can be repaid by directly saving the favor holder's life or fulfilling any single task she demands whenever she demands it. In the convoluted politics of Yu-Shan and the great spirit courts, a minor Celestial favor is worth two points, a moderate favor worth four points and a major favor costs six points. This Trait may also be taken as a Flaw, in which case the character owes a favor to someone powerful enough and well-connected enough to call it in. The value of this Trait depends on the severity of favor as noted previously. Characters with Backing or similar Backgrounds most likely owe this to another member of their organization or at least to a well-regarded associate. For other characters, the possibilities are limitless: Guild factors, politicians, merciful victors of a duel, etc. Characters who renege on their favors will suffer considerable loss of face at best and possibly much worse if they break their word to someone powerful or vengeful. In either form as a Merit or a Flaw, a Favor lasts until the holder calls it due. Once paid, the Trait becomes null, without adding or subtracting experience or other recompense. Storytellers should not go easy on characters who owe favors, even at low levels. Indebtedness is not pleasant or convenient, and a mundane errand called due in the middle of an epic quest can create all sorts of life complications. It is common practice among spirit courts and in certain groups to exchange their favors as social currency. In such systems, a favor debt may be transferred to another party in order to cancel a debt of like value. Such transfers do not need the consent of the party who owes the service. This practice can lead to considerable complications if a god purchases a favor from characters who haven't even heard of it, especially if that god has a diametrically opposed agenda to those owing it in service.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific restriction. The Yu-Shan/Celestial-court favor tiers are Creation-flavored setting color and less directly relevant to an Autochthonia-based story, but the base 1-4 pt. favor-owed-by-a-peer framing applies generally, including to favors owed within the Tripartite or a Sodality.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 23/PDF 24).

name: Heirloom
summary: The character owns a piece of property more valuable than her means and lifestyle can afford, for only one bonus point regardless of the item's Resource value.
mechanics: The character owns a piece of property more valuable than his means and lifestyle can afford. Such treasures may be actual heirlooms, spoils of a heist, gifts or something more exotic still. Such an item costs only one bonus point regardless of its Resource value. Most weapons and armor purchased with Heirloom will be of exceptional quality. This Merit is particularly easy to abuse and sufficient value to raise a character's Resources rating if sold; the Storyteller should probably require purchase of Resources at that level and assume that the wealth is simply concentrated into very narrow holdings.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 23/PDF 24). For an Alchemical, an Heirloom would typically be Artifact-rated equipment acquired outside the normal Artifact Background purchase (see artifact-background-altered), such as a salvaged relic or a gift from a Sodality patron.

name: Hidden Manse
summary: The character controls a Manse forgotten to history/geomantic maps, or one shrouded by a mysterious property of its arcane nature; requires the Manse Background.
mechanics: The character controls a Manse forgotten to history and geomantic maps or perhaps a Manse in a more public area shrouded by some mysterious property of its arcane nature. Such a hidden place of power makes an excellent base of operations or secret lair, provided that the character and those trusted with the secret don't compromise the location with their actions. Assuming the character is properly discrete, no one need ever know about his magical lair. This Merit costs one point for a hidden Demesne or two points for an actual Manse. Characters must have the Manse Background to purchase this Merit.
compatibility: Any character type with the Manse Background, including Alchemicals -- but only in stories where that Background is actually available to them. Per this family's own manse-background-altered row, the Manse Background cannot be purchased or used by Alchemical characters in any story confined to Autochthonia before the Seal of Eight Divinities breaks; it functions normally only after Alchemicals reach Creation (the post-Locust-Crusade era).
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). JUDGMENT CALL, FLAGGED: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 23/PDF 24). Cross-checked directly against manse-background-altered: this Merit requires the Manse Background, which simply does not exist for Alchemicals in an Autochthonia-only story. Kept selectable (rather than excluded) because it becomes fully usable, with no further adaptation needed, the moment a story crosses into Creation -- mirroring how the Manse Background row itself is 'calculated' rather than 'excluded.'

name: Heir Apparent
summary: Characters with this Merit will receive an inheritance left by their parents or another benefactor once the current owner dies (or is otherwise removed); each point invested grants two dots of Backgrounds ultimately gained, cumulative with existing Backgrounds.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit will receive an inheritance left by their parents or another benefactor. They only need to wait for the current owner to die -- or find some way to hasten that process along without getting caught (which would forfeit the gain at the very least). Every point invested in this Merit grants two dots of Backgrounds that the character will ultimately gain, but no single Background may gain more than five points in this fashion. The Storyteller may add a die to a stipulated inheritance's difficulty for every major condition attached to it. This can require that the character be married or unmarried, serve in the military for a defined number of years, etc. Background dots obtained with this Merit are cumulative with Backgrounds the character already possesses and may raise a Background above a rating of four. Although Heir Apparent is typically used to transfer resources, artifacts, followers and other tangible goods or benefits, it may also include business partners or associates in the form of contacts, allies and the like. More exotic selections rely on situation and Storyteller approval, such as a necromancer whose blood-inscribed heir will bestow her Whispers to her heir.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals, with an adaptation: Alchemicals have no parents in the normal sense (they are built, not born), so the benefactor is instead a patron, mentor, or predecessor within the Tripartite or a Sodality whose Class rank, Artifact stock, or Vats standing passes to the character upon that benefactor's death or decommissioning.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). JUDGMENT CALL, FLAGGED: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 24/PDF 25). The source text is framed around inheriting from 'parents or another benefactor'; since Alchemicals are constructed rather than born, this row reframes the source of the inheritance as a benefactor (a Sodality patron, a Vat-technician mentor, or a superior in the character's Tripartite branch) rather than a parent, while keeping the mechanic (2 Background dots per point invested) unchanged.

name: Legendary Artifact
summary: A character with this Merit has gotten hold of an artifact of world-shaking power (on par with the Mantle of Brigid or the Eye of Autochthon); the book explicitly discourages Storytellers from ever allowing it, calling such artifacts "innately and grossly unfair plot devices."
mechanics: A character with this Merit has gotten hold of an artifact of world-shaking power, a relic on par with the Mantle of Brigid or the Eye of Autochthon. These rare and often unwisely coveted devices invariably reshape the lives of all who come into contact with them, defining even the epoch of their use. These relics bring terrible danger commensurate with their power, as the doomed prophet Ikere and Bagrash Kol learned in their futile attempts to master the fabled Eye. And then too, these devices attract the worst and deadliest ambitions of gods and demons and Exalted hungry for their power. Storytellers do not need to allow this Merit ever, as legendary artifacts are innately and grossly unfair plot devices that will likely dominate any series they occupy. This Trait merely aids in telling stories revolving around these relics.
compatibility: Any character type, at Storyteller discretion (heavily discouraged by the book's own text), including Alchemicals -- who have a direct, named in-setting example: the source text itself cites the Eye of Autochthon as a relic of this power tier.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). STRONG THEMATIC FIT: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 24/PDF 25). The source names the Eye of Autochthon, a signature Alchemical-setting artifact, as its own worked example of this Merit's power tier.

name: Cache
summary: The character has wealth hidden or legally stored across many locations, for one bonus point per city beyond the character's home; requires Class 4+ (adapted from the source's Resources 4+/Salary 2+, since Alchemicals use Class instead of Resources).
mechanics: The character has wealth hidden or legally stored in banks in many locations, for a cost of one bonus point per city beyond the character's home. The character has full access to the value of his full Resources or Salary at any of these locations and their surrounding regions. Characters with five points of Cache are assumed to have access to their wealth in any settlement town-sized or larger in a selected direction of Creation or the Blessed Isle, though it may take up to a week for the money to arrive within that domain by another direction. Every additional point beyond five extends this domain by another direction. Characters must have Resources 4+ or Salary 2+ to purchase this Merit.
compatibility: Any character type with sufficient standing wealth, including Alchemicals -- adapted from the source's 'Resources 4+ or Salary 2+' prerequisite, since Alchemicals have no separate Resources Background (it is folded into Class per this family's own class-background row). An Alchemical needs Class 4+ to purchase this Merit.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). JUDGMENT CALL, FLAGGED: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 24/PDF 25). Adapted the Resources/Salary prerequisite to this family's Class Background, which explicitly replaces Followers/Influence/Resources for Alchemicals and Autochthonian mortals (see class-background).

name: Alternative Divination
summary: Crude divination through methods other than astrology (tea leaves, entrails, palm-reading, crystal-gazing, etc.); each purchase grants knowledge of one ritual (two rituals per purchase for Sidereal Exalted specifically), capped by the character's Occult rating.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit can crudely divine the workings of fate through methods other than astrology. Some read destiny in the pattern of tea leaves or the entrails of birds or upon the symbolic verses of a spider's web, while others spout disjointed verses of prophecy from a drug-induced trance or read palms or gaze into crystals. Whatever the method, the rolls and effectiveness of divination remain the same as for conventional astrology (see Exalted, p. 251). Any divination ritual should take a minimum of one scene to complete, though most will be considerably longer. Methods less complicated and quicker than astrology suffer an increased difficulty assigned by the Storyteller, while complicated, well-described rituals should benefit from a stunt bonus. Characters may purchase this Merit multiple times, with each purchase granting knowledge of one effective ritual by astrology (or two rituals per purchase for Sidereal Exalted). However, characters may not purchase this Merit more times than their Occult rating.
compatibility: Any character type with an Occult rating, including Alchemicals; the source names only Sidereal Exalted for the two-rituals-per-purchase bonus, so Alchemicals get one ritual per purchase like most other character types.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 24/PDF 25). Cross-checked against Alchemical's own rules: nothing bars an Alchemical from having an Occult rating or practicing crude non-astrological divination.

name: Priest
summary: Recognized priest of a deity/religion; the 1-pt. version is automatically and freely granted to Zenith, Midnight, and No Moon Caste Exalted (and to all Sidereal Exalted for their initiating astrological college) as an innate part of their Exaltation. The 7-pt. high-priest version costs those same castes only 6 points, but their Caste Mark glows during miracle prayers.
mechanics: The character is a recognized priest of a particular deity or religion. Apart from lowering the difficulty of prayers directed at the appropriate spirit (see Exalted, p. 335), the one-point version of this Merit has no defined rules effects. Storytellers may award symbolic dream messages to priests or promise dream omens sent by their patron, but no systems govern these visitations. The effects of this Merit are automatically bestowed upon Zenith, Midnight and No Moon Caste Exalted, and all Sidereal Exalted are automatically priests of the astrological colleges they are initiated into. Such characters do not need to purchase this Merit, as it is an innate aspect of their Exaltation. The seven-point version of this Merit signifies far greater favor from the priest's spirit patron. Such high priests receive portentous dreams and even waking visions from their masters, but their devotion and faith must be ever-unwavering to retain favor. Piety has its rewards, however, and high priests may petition the god, elemental or demon they serve for miracles. A petition of this magnitude is performed as a standard prayer roll, though the player must spend a Willpower point to make an automatic success or channel a Virtue appropriate to the prayer. Provided that god, elemental or demon accepts the petition (Storyteller's discretion), successes on this attempt may be spent to: restore one point to the character's Essence pool (one success), restore one spent Willpower point to the character's pool (two successes), exorcise a possessing spirit from a host (requires successes equal to the offending spirit's Essence + 3, and the character's patron must have a higher Essence rating than the targeted spirit) or heal a dying character to stable condition at Incapacitated (five successes; Resources 4+ offering required). Storytellers may allow other specialized prayers at their discretion, using the preceding list as inspiration for the level of power and number of successes required for miracles. It is also important to remember that some spirits will not or cannot perform certain miracles based on their nature or power. Spirits can perceive a distinctive mark upon characters with this Merit. The design and placement of this mark depends on the patron. Exalted castes who are innate priests of their gods pay only six points to become high priests, but their Caste Mark glows brightly whenever they pray for a miracle.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals, at the standard full cost -- the source's list of castes that receive the 1-pt. version free (Solar Zenith, Abyssal Midnight, Lunar No Moon) and all Sidereals for their astrological college does not include any Alchemical Caste, so no Alchemical Caste is auto-granted this Merit; any Alchemical of any Caste may still purchase it normally.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). STRONG THEMATIC FIT, FLAGGED: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 25/PDF 26). No Alchemical Caste is named among the innate-priest castes, so the free-grant/discount does not apply and Alchemicals pay the standard 1- or 7-pt. cost. However, Autochthonia's own Theomachracy branch of the Tripartite is explicitly a clergy of 'lectors, preceptors or clerics' (see backing-background-altered), and the Orichalcum Caste's own listed Concepts include 'cleric of the Great Maker' (see orichalcum-caste) -- both strong in-setting hooks for an Alchemical to take this Merit at full cost.

name: Destiny
summary: Represents an auspicious fate written in the stars, scaling from a lifetime of good health (1 pt.) up to founding a lasting noble dynasty or transforming an era (5 pts.); a companion sidebar states Celestial Exalted (Solar, Lunar, Sidereal) and Abyssal/Infernal Exalted may only retain 1-2 points of Destiny after Exaltation consumes the rest, while Terrestrial (Dragon-Blooded) and Alchemical Exalted have no such cap.
mechanics: A character with Destiny shall live most auspiciously, his fate written large in the stars above. Providence comes in many forms and degrees of fortune, as represented by the number of points invested in this Merit. A one-point destiny may be a long and uneventful life of good health without serious hunger. Two points promise a lifetime of financial prosperity or many offspring to carry the family name -- or perhaps the greater prosperity of a famed tradesman, local hero or honored elder. In three points lie the destinies of merchant princes, kings of small nations and those of similar ilk. The favored scion of a Dynastic house might bear such a fate, as might the conscript who survives and rises through the ranks to become a general in his own right. Four points promise the life of a hero whose deeds shall live on in songs and stories for many generations to come or perhaps the founder of a lasting noble dynasty. Five-point destinies only surround the mightiest sorcerers and emperors whose exploits transform their era and world. The combined fate of entire nations bends before such epochal figures. While ultimately positive in its way, destiny need not be kind to those who bear it or those who stand in its path. A foreordained king may claim his crown through assassination and treachery, his greatness rooted in tyranny. Conversely, a selfless hero may deliver her people from that same tyrant through her martyrdom, her greatness culminating in personal tragedy even as her name becomes legend. Such juxtapositions of greatness and doom may best be represented by a combination of this Merit and the Dark Fate Flaw (see p. 39). Characters bearing the twin marks of fortune and misfortune will fulfill both in their own way, usually through the same events as those bearing Destiny with a single success. Any astrologer can sense the weight of fortune upon the horoscope of those bearing this Merit, though discerning the specifics of such a destiny requires far more effort and research. It is worth noting the difference between capacity for greatness and certainty of greatness. All Exalted bear the capacity to become mighty heroes or despots by virtue of their power, yet not all do so by virtue of the very free will granted by that potential. Those with Destiny must fulfill that fate unless the power of the Maidens, and even the Celestials, can alter the fate of the dead and Abyssal Exalted. It is incumbent upon Storytellers to ensure that coincidence protects those with a powerful fate until that fate finds fruition, though such protection may seem cruel or callous. Such characters are not wholly defended from misfortune and injury, but only such misfortune as directly interferes with their appointed role. There is no mystery or system for such protection, as it is no more a storytelling matter. Players who invest points in this Merit may request a particular destiny for their characters or leave the specifics in the hands of the Storyteller. As always, Storytellers should feel free to veto any destiny that they find inappropriate for their story. A companion sidebar, 'Destiny and Exaltation,' explains that Terrestrial Exaltation flows through bloodline and luck, but Celestial Exaltation (Solar, Lunar, Sidereal) only affixes itself to mortals of sufficient Destiny -- Destiny 3 or better for Solars and Lunars, Destiny 4 or better for Sidereals -- and Abyssal/Infernal Exaltation likewise requires Destiny 3. When Celestial Exaltation takes place, the new Exalt's free will overrides most of that predetermined fate, reducing the character's Destiny rating by four (for Sidereals) or three (for the rest) and folding the remainder into minor fates; as a result, Celestial, Abyssal and Infernal Exalted can only retain the smallest of destinies and may not purchase or hold more than one or two points of this Merit after Exaltation. Terrestrial (Dragon-Blooded) and Alchemical Exalted do not base their Exaltations on Destiny and, therefore, suffer no such cap.
compatibility: Available to Alchemical Exalted at the full 1-5 pt. range, with NO cap -- the source's own 'Destiny and Exaltation' sidebar explicitly states Terrestrial (Dragon-Blooded) and Alchemical Exalted do not base their Exaltations on Destiny and therefore suffer no post-Exaltation cap, unlike Solar/Lunar/Sidereal/Abyssal/Infernal Exalted.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). DIRECTLY ALCHEMICAL-RELEVANT: the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 25/PDF 26) names Alchemical Exalted by name as uncapped. This is one of the most favorable Merits in the chapter for this family specifically.

name: Lucky
summary: Grants a luck pool the player may spend to reroll dice or shift random events. Sidereal Exalted get a different formula: two more luck points than dots invested, capped at a pool of five, so they pay a maximum of three points for the largest pool.
mechanics: A character with this Merit lives in interesting times, blessed with an unlikely preponderance of fortune that follows his every enterprise. He may or may not also have Destiny (see p. 25), as luck is quite a different force than fate. Those with Destiny find their luck invisibly guiding them toward that ordained end, while those without particular fate drift aimlessly and gracefully as a wind-blown leaf through the challenges of life. Lucky characters receive a luck pool equal to the number of points invested in the Merit. Players may spend points of luck to repeat any roll at the same difficulty and target number. Even botches may be rerolled with luck, provided the botches are not the result of chance guiding the character enforced by the anima of an Eclipse Caste Solar or a Moonshadow Caste Abyssal or similarly potent curses. Multiple rerolls may be applied to a single task until the desired result is obtained or until the luck runs out. Players may also spend points of luck to affect a game of chance or other completely random event involving the character. Each point spent in this manner increases the character's chance of success by 10 percent. In such situations, the Storyteller should roll one die, adding one to the result per luck point spent. If the modified result comes up 6 or higher, the event favors the character. Characters with this Merit regain one luck point after every full week they do not call upon their luck and refresh their luck pool fully at the end of each story. Sidereal characters receive two more luck points than the number of points invested in the Merit, though they may not have a luck pool greater than five. Consequently, Sidereals with this Merit pay a maximum of three points for a luck pool of five and may not have a luck pool smaller than three.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; the source names only Sidereal Exalted for the alternate luck-pool formula, so Alchemicals use the standard 1- to 5-pt. luck-pool rules.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 26/PDF 27).

name: Signature Style
summary: Combines movement and attitude into a distinctive flair defining the character's legend; functions like an Ability specialty for stunts, granting an extra die that stacks with the stunt-rating die. May be purchased up to three times but only one Signature Style can benefit the same stunt.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit combine movement and attitude into a distinctive flair that defines their legend. Signature Style functions like an Ability specialty for stunts, providing one extra die in appropriate circumstances. This extra die stacks with the rating of the stunt to determine the final bonus, but it does not alter the number of motes or Willpower returned if the action succeeds. Possible Signature Style specialties include "Obvious Impossibilities," "Damn, I'm Smooth," "Making it Look Easy," "Look Upon Me and Despair," "Economy of Motion," "Excessively Flashy," "Visual Poetry" and "Shocking Brutality." As always, the Storyteller retains final authority on whether a particular action embodies the character's Signature Style. Characters may purchase this Merit up to three times, but only one Signature Style can benefit the same stunt.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 27/PDF 28).

name: Sworn Brotherhood
summary: Exalted who took part in the Terrestrial spell Sworn Brothers' Oath share a bond rating equal to the number of members (max 8); most commonly used to link player characters in shared purpose and loyalty (all members must buy it). Extremely rare among Exalted other than Dragon-Blooded, though the book explicitly notes some Lunar packs bind themselves together this way.
mechanics: Exalted with this Merit have taken part in the Terrestrial spell Sworn Brothers' Oath (see E:DB, p. 161), sharing a bond with a rating equal to the number of members (maximum eight). Sworn Brotherhood is most commonly used to link the players' characters together in common purpose and loyalty, and therefore, all members of the brotherhood must purchase this Merit. Sworn Brotherhood is extremely rare among Exalted other than Dragon-Blooded, though some Lunar packs bind themselves together in this fashion.
compatibility: Exalted only (not mortals), including Alchemicals; the source calls this Merit extremely rare outside Dragon-Blooded and names some Lunar packs as a specific exception, but does not restrict it away from other Exalted.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). JUDGMENT CALL: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 27/PDF 28). The source's in-fiction trigger (the Terrestrial spell Sworn Brothers' Oath, E:DB p. 161) is not available to Alchemicals; treat an Alchemical unit or squad's Sworn Brotherhood as bound by an equivalent Autochthonian ceremony or Vat-side ritual at Storyteller discretion, since the underlying mechanic (a shared bond rating among up to eight members) does not itself depend on the specific ritual that creates it.

name: Prescient Dreamer
summary: Regular prophetic dreams of possible futures, deciphered with Intelligence + Occult; Sidereal Exalted pay a reduced 2-pt. cost, reflecting destined Exaltation-for-Sidereals framing. No restriction against Lunars.
mechanics: A character with this Merit regularly dreams of what may be. The reason for this may be a gift of a god capable of seeing into the future or an unconscious awareness of fate's strands upon the destined Exaltation for Sidereals. Regardless of destined Exaltation for Sidereals. Regardless of the reason, such characters always dream premonitions differently than others and recognize them as visions, even if they do not know what they mean. The futures they see may involve events of decades hence or those of the next day, though they are usually within the dreamer's lifespan. Deriving meaning from the vague symbolism of such omens requires an Intelligence + Occult roll at a significance assigned by the Storyteller to reflect the overall significance of the event. The number of successes determines the clarity of understanding. One success reveals that a great calamity will come soon, but the nature of the calamity remains disguised, as do its location and exact timing. Five successes may unearth a plot of assassination with a timetable and visions of the conspirators. Characters with this Merit do not control their visions in any way. Such dreams come unbidden and follow the whims of fate and the Storyteller. A prescient dreamer may also sleep soundly for years unbidden on when and then experience visions every night for a month. Once a character reveals memories to others or takes actions based on the dream, he interferes with that destiny and decreases its overall probability. This is especially true for dreams whose content lies many years in the future.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; the source names only Sidereal Exalted for the reduced 2-pt. cost, so Alchemicals pay the standard 3-pt. cost.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). JUDGMENT CALL: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 28/PDF 29). Nothing in Alchemical's own rules establishes that Alchemicals do not sleep or dream; absent evidence to the contrary, this Merit is kept as written (prophetic dreams during ordinary rest) rather than reframed around Essence-recovery meditation.

name: Daredevil
summary: Fortune smiles on the recklessly brave: may reflexively spend one Willpower point to double the rating of a stunt awarded for a Physical action, with a difficulty of 3 or higher.
mechanics: Fortune smiles on the recklessly brave. A character with this Merit may reflexively spend one Willpower point to double the rating of stunt dice awarded to a Physical action with a difficulty of 3 or higher. This Willpower may be spent after the Storyteller determines the rating of a stunt and does not prevent simultaneous Willpower use for automatic success or checking a Virtue. Note that Daredevil does not increase the number of motes or Willpower returned by a successful stunt. Heroic mortals pay one point less for this Merit, as their daring is all the more impressive for its lack of magic. Characters with the Signature Style Merit (see p. 28) do not double the extra die awarded by that Trait in situations where both Merits apply.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; heroic mortals pay one point less, with no other splat-specific variant.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 29/PDF 30).

name: Mute
summary: Cannot speak or make vocal utterance of any sort; players describe actions without speech, using sign language, magic, or shared understanding. Higher tiers add physical/vocal-cord damage. Exalted pay one point less at every tier.
mechanics: Mute characters may not speak or make vocal utterance of any sort. Their players speak to describe actions, without verbal communication is possible without writing, magic or shared understanding of a sign language. For three points, this limitation has no physiological basis. The character may have lost her voice after exposure to mind-shattering horror, forsaken speech as part of a barbarian taboo or taken a monastic vow of silence. If the character finds her voice or breaks her willing quiet, her player must buy off the Flaw at normal cost. The four-point version of this Flaw involves actual damage to the vocal cords, either as a result of injury or birth defect. Characters incapable of speaking above a faint whisper may purchase this Flaw for one point, regardless of the reason for their quiet. Exalted characters suffering actual silence receive one less point.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; the reduced cost applies to 'Exalted' generically, and Alchemicals are Exalted, so this discount applies to them.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 29/PDF 30). ID retained as 'pg-merit-mute' (matching the identical row already inventoried for other families) even though this is actually a Flaw by category.

name: Unusual Appearance
summary: Hair/eyes of a striking, unnatural color at 1 point, or fully piebald/colorless (albino) skin and hairlessness at 2 points; the appearance must deviate notably from the local norm to qualify.
mechanics: For one point, the character has hair and/or eyes of a striking color, such as vivid scarlet, sea green, ashen white or some stranger hue. For two points, the character's skin also exhibits remarkable pigmentation or the colorless white of an albino. It is also possible that the character has no hair on his body at all. Regardless of the specifics, the character's appearance must deviate notably from the expected norm to warrant an actual Flaw. For example, there is nothing unusual about green-haired Haltans, though such a character might take this Flaw for a story set among the blonde and gray hues of a village in the Far North. As always, the Storyteller retains final say on whether a character's appearance deviates sufficiently. Those marked by striking colors have a harder time hiding or impersonating others and may suffer discrimination and suspicious stares from xenophobes (losing one die from pertinent Stealth, Larceny and Social rolls). True albinos often have the Sun-Seared Flaw (see p. 31).
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 30/PDF 31). For an Alchemical, this Flaw is easily reframed as an unusual finish, color, or patina on the character's Magical Material chassis rather than hair/eye/skin coloring.

name: One Eye
summary: Only a single eye remaining (injury or congenital defect): one-die penalty to Awareness rolls involving distance vision or peripheral vision on the blind side, and increases the difficulty of ranged attacks against the character by one.
mechanics: Whether resulting from injury or congenital defect, characters with this Flaw have only a single eye remaining. This imposes a one-die penalty to Awareness rolls involving distance vision or peripheral vision on the blind side, and increases the difficulty of ranged attacks by one.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (pp. 30-31/PDF 31-32). Represents a damaged or missing optical sensor on an Alchemical's chassis.

name: Sun-Seared
summary: Uncomfortable in bright light, suffering horrible burns from relatively mild exposure. Autochthonia has no natural sun, so this Flaw is primarily relevant once an Alchemical reaches Creation; within Autochthonia it could instead represent sensitivity to forge-glow or reactor light. The book notes some ghosts and Abyssals manifest this trait even more severely (unable to bear light at all), at the extreme 6-pt. tier.
mechanics: The character finds sunlight uncomfortable and suffers horrible sunburns from relatively mild exposure. This Flaw is common among albinos (see 'Unusual Appearance,' p. 30), especially the Dune People of the South. Some ghosts and Abyssals also manifest this trait at a higher level, unable to bear the light their dead or blackened souls have forsaken. The two-point version of this Flaw is at -1 on all dice pools in direct sunlight and suffer one die of unsoakable bashing damage for each hour of direct exposure. Characters with the three-point version increase the penalty to -2 and suffer damage every 30 minutes. The extreme six-point version of this Flaw is rarely seen outside of the most tainted spectres, Abyssals and Demon-Blooded. Such wretches are at -3 under direct sunlight and suffer one die of unsoakable bashing damage every minute. Characters bundled in heavy clothes or otherwise limiting their direct exposure, such as under an overcast sky or darting from shadow to shadow double the interval necessary to inflict damage. Those with the six-point version only suffer damage every five minutes for indirect exposure.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals, with an adaptation: Autochthonia has no natural sun, so this Flaw is only meaningfully in play for an Alchemical once a story reaches Creation (the post-Locust-Crusade era) or another sunlit venue; within Autochthonia itself it could instead represent sensitivity to the Great Maker's forge-glow, reactor light, or similarly intense artificial light sources, at Storyteller discretion.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). JUDGMENT CALL, FLAGGED: derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 30/PDF 31). Autochthonia is the internal body of the god Autochthon and has no natural sun, so a literal reading of 'sunlight' does not apply until an Alchemical operates in Creation. Kept selectable rather than excluded because it becomes directly usable, unmodified, the moment a story crosses into Creation -- the same reasoning applied to the Hidden Manse Merit above.

name: Climate Sensitive
summary: Discomfort and penalties outside the character's accustomed environmental conditions; the point value scales with how common the undesired conditions are to encounter (2 pts. for one specific extreme, 4 pts. for anywhere lacking the character's home temperate conditions).
mechanics: Characters with this Flaw experience discomfort and take ill if they are subjected to environmental conditions substantially different than those they are accustomed to. The value of this Flaw depends on the likelihood of encountering the undesired conditions. For two points, the character responds poorly to a particular extreme of temperature (arctic, tropical) or humidity (arid desert, marsh/jungle). For three points, the character is uncomfortable in any environment lacking these extreme conditions, including temperate climates. Four points indicates the condition that defines the character's home region is specific to a geographical region and cannot be replicated or transplanted without considerable difficulty and expense, such as the pollen of a particular tree or something equally obscure. Whenever a character with this Flaw finds himself in an environment he finds uncomfortable, he adds 1 to the difficulty of all Survival rolls, as well as all Endurance and Resistance rolls to resist manifestations of the undesired conditions. This Flaw may not be taken to any climate the Storyteller indicates the game will visit often.
compatibility: Any character type, including Alchemicals; no splat-specific variant is given. Autochthonia's own varied strata (industrial heat, deep cold, oil seas, etc.) provide ready in-setting extremes for this Flaw.
notes: Derived from Lunar's verified transcription of the Exalted Players Guide's universal Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (this same id/citation exists in docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/exalted-the-lunars.json). Derived from the Players Guide's universal Chapter One (p. 31/PDF 32).

name: Amputee
summary: Missing one or more limbs from congenital defect or later injury; scaled by number/type of limbs lost (arm, hand, leg, or multiples up to full quadriplegia), with prosthetics/balance rules and Exalted paying a discounted cost at every tier.
mechanics: The character lacks an arm or a leg, either as a result of a congenital defect or injury sustained later in life. Alternately, the character retains the limb, but only as a useless, paralyzed husk. The mechanical effects of amputation vary. Characters missing a hand may not perform two-handed tasks with extreme difficulty, if at all. It is assumed that the character with one hand considers that hand primary and, therefore, suffers no offhand penalty. The loss of both hands means that tasks involving fine dexterity are impossible, though hooks or other prosthetics may allow cruder tasks at a -1 die penalty. Characters may offset the balance penalty with carefully weighted garments, prosthetics or other innovative means (such as tying an object in place for those suffering paralysis). Characters missing an arm can move at half normal movement rate and are at -3 on Athletics rolls involving footwork. Those with a paralyzed leg must also use crutches or drag the paralyzed limb behind them, suffering the same penalties for missing a leg.
